book.title: Rig Veda
book.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary
book.license: Public domain translation (Griffith, 1896); transcription from Wikisource. Griffith’s commentary and notes are not included.
book.notes: Complete translation in Griffith’s arrangement: ten Maṇḍalas, one chapter per hymn, one verse per stanza. The Sanskrit text and Griffith’s commentary are not included. Hymn 1.179, which the 1896 edition prints only as an appendix note, is absent.

verses.translation: AGNI, subdue opposing bands, and drive our enemies away. Invincible, slay godless foes: give splendour to the worshipper.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Lit with libation, Agni, thou, deathless, who callest Gods to feast, Accept our sacrifice with joy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With splendour, Agni, Son of Strength, thou who art worshipped, wakeful One. Seat thee on this my sacred grass.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With all thy fires, with all the Gods, Agni, exalt the songs we sing. And living men in holy rites.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Grant, Agni, to the worshipper wealth rich in heroes, plenteous store, Make thou us rich with many sons.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THOU art the sapient Son of Dyaus, O Agni, yes and the Child of Earth, who knowest all things. Bring the Gods specially, thou Sage, for worship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni the wise bestows the might of heroes grants strengthening food, preparing it for nectar. Thou who art rich in food bring the Gods hither.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, infallible, lights Earth and Heaven, immortal Goddesses gracious to all men,- Lord through his strength, splendid through adorations.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come to the sacrifice, Agni and Indra come to the offerer's house who hath the Soma. Come, friendly-minded, Gods, to drink the Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In the floods' home art thou enkindled, Agni, O Jatavedas, Son of Strength, eternal, Exalting with thine help the gathering places.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: REVERING in our heart Agni Vaisvanara, the finder of the light, whose promises are true, The liberal, gladsome, car-borne God we Kusikas invoke him with oblation, seeking wealth with songs.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: That Agni, bright, Vaisvanara, we invoke for help, and Matarisvan worthy of the song of praise; Brhaspati for man's observance of the Gods, the Singer prompt to hear, the swiftly-moving guest.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Age after age Vaisvanara, neighing like a horse, is kindled with the women by the Kusikas. May Agni, he who wakes among Immortal Gods, grant us heroic strength and wealth in noble steeds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let them go forth, the strong, as flames of fire with might. Gathered for victory they have yoked their spotted deer. Pourers of floods, the Maruts, Masters of all wealth, they who can ne'er be conquered, make the mountains shake.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Maruts, Friends of men, are glorious as the fire: their mighty and resplendent succour we implore. Those storming Sons of Rudra clothed in robes of rain, boon-givers of good gifts, roar as the lions roar.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We, band on band and troop following troop, entreat with fair lauds Agni's splendour and the Maruts' might, With spotted deer for steeds, with wealth that never fails, they, wise Ones, come to sacrifice at our gatherings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni am I who know, by birth, all creatures. Mine eye is butter, in my mouth is nectar. I am light threefold, measurer of the region exhaustless heat am I, named burnt-oblation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bearing in mind a thought with light accordant, he purified the Sun with three refinings; By his own nature gained the highest treasure, and looked abroad over the earth and heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Spring that fails not with a hundred streamlets, Father inspired of' prayers that men should utter, The Sparkler, joyous in his Parents' bosom, -him, the Truth-speaker, sate ye, Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: IN ladle dropping oil your food goes in oblation up to heaven, Goes to the Gods in search of bliss.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni I laud, the Sage inspired, crowner of sacrifice through song, Who listens and gives bounteous gifts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Agni, if we might obtain control of thee the potent God, Then should we overcome our foes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Kindled at sacrifices he is Agni, hallower, meet for praise, With flame for hair: to him we seek.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Immortal Agni, shining far, enrobed with oil, well worshipped, bears The gifts of sacrifice away.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The priests with ladles lifted up, worshipping here with holy thought, Have brought this Agni for our aid.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Immortal, Sacrificer, God, with wondrous power he leads the way, Urging the great assembly on.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Strong, he is set on deeds of strength. In sacrifices led in front, As Singer he completes the rite.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Excellent, he was made by thought. The Germ of beings have I gained, Yea, and die Sire of active strength.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thee have I stablished, Excellent, O strengthened by the sage's prayer, Thee, Agni, longing, nobly bright.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, the swift and active One, singers, at time of sacrifice, Eagerly kindle with their food.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni the Son of Strength who shines up to the heaven in solemn rites, The wise of heart, I glorify.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Meet to be lauded and adored, showing in beauty through the dark, Agni, the Strong, is kindled well.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni is kindled as a bull, like a horse bearer of the Gods: Men with oblations worship him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thee will we kindle as a bull, we who are Bulls ourselves, O Bull. Thee, Agni, shining mightily.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: AGNI who knowest all, accept our offering and the cake of meal, At dawn's libation, rich in prayer!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, the sacrificial cake hath been prepared and dressed for thee: Accept it, O Most Youthful God.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, enjoy the cake of meal and our oblation three days old: Thou, Son of Strength, art stablished at our sacrifice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Here at the midday sacrifice enjoy thou the sacrificial cake, wise, Jatavedas! Agni, the sages in assemblies never diminish the portion due to thee the Mighty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Agni, at the third libation take with joy the offered cake of sacrifice, thou, Son of Strength. Through skill in song bear to the Gods our sacrifice, watchful and fraught with riches, to Immortal God.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O waxing Agni, knower, thou, of all, accept our gifts, the cake, And that prepared ere yesterday.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: HERE is the gear for friction, here tinder made ready for the spark. Bring thou the Matron: we will rub Agni in ancient fashion forth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: 1n the two fire-sticks Jatavedas lieth, even as the well-set germ in pregnant women, Agni who day by day must be exalted by men who watch and worship with oblations.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Lay this with care on that which lies extended: straight hath she borne the Steerwhen made prolific. With his red pillar-radiant is his splendour -in our skilled task is born the Son of Ila.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In Ila's place we set thee down, upon the central point of earth, That, Agni Jatavedas, thou mayst bear our offerings to the Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Rub into life, ye men, the Sage, the guileless, Immortal, very wise and fair to look on. O men, bring forth the most propitious Agni, first ensign of the sacrifice to eastward.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When with their arms they rub him straight he shineth forth like a strong courser, red in colour, in the wood. Bright, checkless, as it were upon the Atvins' path, lie passeth by the stones and burneth up the grass.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni shines forth when born, observant, mighty, the bountiful, the Singar praised by sages; Whom, as adorable and knowing all things, Gods set at solemn rites as offering bearer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Set thee, O Priest, in, thine own place, observant: lay down the sacrifice in the home of worship. Thou, dear to Gods, shalt serve them with oblation: Agni, give long life to the sacrificer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Raise ye a mighty smoke, my fellow-workers! Ye shall attain to wealth without obstruction. This Agni is the battle-winning Hero by whom the Gods have overcome the Dasyus.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This is thine ordered place of birth whence sprung to life thou shonest forth. Knowing this, Agni, sit thee down, and prosper thou the songs we sing.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As Germ Celestial he is called Tanunapat, and Narasamsa born diffused in varied shape. Formed in his Mother he is Matarisvan; he hath, in his course, become the rapid flight of wind.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With strong attrition rubbed to life, laid down with careful hand, a Sage, Agni, make sacrifices good, and for the pious bring the Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Mortals have brought to life the God Immortal, the Conqueror with mighty jaws, unfailing. The sisters ten, unwedded and united, together grasp the Babe, the new-born Infant.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Served by the seven priests, he shone forth from ancient time, when in his Mother's bosom, in her lap, he glowed. Giving delight each day he closeth not his eye, since from the Asura's body hewas brought to life.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Even as the Maruts, onslaughts who attack the foe, those born the first of all knew the full power of prayer. The Kusikas have made the glorious hymn ascend, and, each one singly in his home, have kindled fire.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As we, O Priest observant, have elected thee this day, what time the solemn sacrifice began, So surely hast thou worshipped, surely hast thou toiled: come thou unto the Soma, wise and knowing all.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THE friends who offer Soma long to find thee: they pour forth Soma and present their viands. They bear unmoved the cursing of the people, for all our wisdom comes from thee, O Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Not far for thee are mid-air's loftiest regions: start hither, Lord of Bays, with thy Bay Horses. Made for the Firm and Strong are these libations. The pressing-stones are set and fire is kindled.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Fair cheeks hath Indra, Maghavan, the Victor, Lord of a great host, Stormer, strong in action. What once thou didst in might when mortals vexed thee,-where now, O Bull, are those thy hero exploits?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For, overthrowing what hath ne'er been shaken, thou goest forth alone destroying Vrtras. For him who followeth thy Law the mountains and heaven and earth stand as if firmly stablished.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yea, Much-invoked! in safety through thy glories alone thou speakest truth as Vrtra's slayer. E'en these two boundless worlds to thee, O Indra, what time thou graspest them, are but a handful.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Forthwith thy Bay steeds down the steep, O Indra, forth, crushing foemen, go thy bolt of thunder! Slay those who meet thee, those who flee, who follow: make all thy promise true; be all completed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The man to whom thou givest as Provider enjoys domestic plenty undivided. Blest, Indra, is thy favour dropping fatness: thy worship, Much-invoked! brings gifts in thousands.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, Indra, Much-invoked! didst crush to pieces Kunaru handless fiend who dwelt with Danu. Thou with might, Indra, smotest dead the scorner, the footless Vrtra as he waxed in vigour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou hast established in her seat, O Indra, the level earth, vast, vigorous, unbounded. The Bull hath propped the heaven and air's mid-region. By thee sent onward let the floods flow hither.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who withheld the kine, in silence I yielded in fear before thy blow, O Indra. He made paths easy to drive forth the cattle. Loud-breathing praises helped the Much-invoked One.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra alone filled full the earth and heaven, the Pair who meet together, rich in treasures. Yea, bring thou near us from the air's mid-region strength, on thy car, and wholesome food, O Hero.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Surya transgresses not the ordered limits set daily by the Lord of Tawny Coursers. When to the goal he comes, his journey ended, his Steeds he looses: this is Indra's doing.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Men gladly in the course of night would look on the broad bright front of the refulgent Morning; And all acknowledge, when she comes in glory, the manifold and goodly works of Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: A mighty splendour rests upon her bosom: bearing ripe milk the Cow, unripe, advances. All sweetness is collected in the Heifer, sweetness which Indra made for our enjoyment.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Barring the way they come. Be firm, O Indra; aid friends to sacrifice and him who singeth. These must be slain by thee, malignant mortals, armed with ill arts, our quiver bearing foemen.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: A cry is beard from enemies most near us: against them send thy fiercest-flaming weapon. Rend them from under, crush them and subdue them. Slay, Maghavan, and make the fiends our booty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Root up the race of Raksasas, O Indra rend it in front and crush it in the middle. How long hast thou bebaved as one who wavers? Cast thy hot dart at him who hates devotion:
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When borne by strong Steeds for our weal, O Leader, thou seatest thee at many noble viands. May we be winners of abundant riches. May Indra be our wealth with store of children.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bestow on us resplendent wealth. O Indra let us enjoy thine overflow of bounty. Wide as a sea our longing hath expanded, fulfil it, O thou Treasure-Lord of treasures.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With kine and horses satisfy this longing with very splendid bounty skill extend it. Seeking the light, with hymns to thee, O Indra, Kusikas have brought their gift, the singers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Lord of the kine, burst the kine's stable open: cows shall be ours, and strength that wins the booty. Hero, whose might is true, thy home is heaven: to us, O Maghavan, grant gifts of cattle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Call we on Maghavan, auspicious Indra, best Hero in this fight where spoil is gathered, The Strong who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vrtras, wins and gathers riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WISE, teaching, following the thought of Order, the sonless gained a grandson from his daughter. Fain, as a sire, to see his child prolific, he sped to meet her with an eager spirit.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Son left not his portion to the brother, he made a home to hold him who should gain, it. What time his Parents gave the Priest his being, of the good pair one acted, one promoted.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni was born trembling with tongue that flickered, so that the Red's great children should be honoured. Great is their germ, that born of them is mighty, great the Bays' Lord's approach through sacrifices.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Conquering bands upon the Warrior waited: they recognized great light from out the darkness. The conscious Dawns went forth to meet his coming, and the sole Master of the kine was Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The sages freed them from their firm built prison: the seven priests drove them forward with their spirit. All holy Order's pathway they discovered he, full of knowledge, shared these deeds through worship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When Sarama had found the mountain's fissure, that vast and ancient place she plundered thoroughly. In the floods' van she led them forth, light-footed: she who well knew came first unto their lowing.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Longing for friendship came the noblest singer: the hill poured forth its treasure for the pious. The Hero with young followers fought and conquered, and straightway Angiras was singing praises,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Peer of each noble thing, yea, all excelling, all creatures doth he know, he slayeth Susna. Our leader, fain for war, singing from heaven, as Friend he saved his lovers from dishonour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They sate them down with spirit fain for booty, making with hymns a way to life eternal. And this is still their place of frequent session, whereby they sought to gain the months through Order.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Drawing the milk of ancient seed prolific, they joyed as they beheld their own possession. Their shout of triumph heated earth and heaven. When the kine showed, they bade the heroes rouse them.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra drove forth the kine, that Vrtra-slayer, while hymns of praise rose up and gifts were offered. For him the Cow, noble and far-extending, poured pleasant juices, bringing oil and sweetness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They made a mansion for their Father, deftly provided him a great and glorious dwelling; With firm support parted and stayed the Parents, and, sitting, fixed him there erected, mighty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What time the ample chalice had impelled him, swift waxing, vast, to pierce the earth and heaven,- Him in whom blameless songs are all united: all powers invincible belong to Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I crave thy powers, I crave thy mighty friendship: full many a team goes to the Vrtra-slayer. Great is the laud, we seek the Princes' favour. Be thou, O Maghavan, our guard and keeper.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He, having found great, splendid, rich dominion, sent life and motion to his friends and lovers. Indra who shone together with the Heroes begot the song, the fire, and Sun and Morning.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Vast, the House-Friend, he set the waters flowing, all-lucid, widely spread, that move together. By the wise cleansings of the meath made holy, through days, and nights they speed the swift streams onward.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To thee proceed the dark, the treasure-holders, both of them sanctified by Surya's bounty. The while thy overly storming Friends, O Indra, fail to attain the measure of thy greatness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Be Lord of joyous songs, O Vrtra-slayer, Bull dear to all, who gives the power of living. Come unto us with thine auspicious friendship, hastening, Mighty One, with mighty succours.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like Angiras I honour him with worship, and renovate old song for him the Ancient. Chase thou the many godless evil creatures, and give us, Maghavan, heaven's light to help m.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Far forth are spread the purifying waters convey thou us across them unto safety. Save us, our Charioteer, from harm, O Indra, soon, very soon, make us win spoil of cattle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: His kine their Lord hath shown, e'en Vrtra's slayer, through the black hosts he passed with red attendants. Teaching us pleasant things by holy Order, to, us hath he thrown open all his portals.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Call we on Maghavan, auspicious Indra, best Hero in this fight where spoil is gathered. The Strong who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vrtras, wins and gathers riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: DRINK thou this Soma, Indra, Lord of Soma; drink thou the draught of noonday which thou Iovest. Puffing thy cheeks, impetuous, liberal Giver, here loose thy two Bay Horses and rejoice thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Quaff it pure, meal-blent, mixt with milk, O Indra; we have poured forth the Soma for thy rapture. Knit with the prayer-fulfilling band of Maruts, yea, with the Rudras, drink till thou art sated;
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Those who gave increase to thy strength and vigour; the Maruts singing forth thy might, O Indra. Drink thou, O fair of cheek, whose hand wields thunder, with Rudras banded, at our noon libation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They, even the Maruts who were there, excited with song the meath-created strength of Indra. By them impelled to act he reached the vitals Of Vrtra, though he deemed that none might wound him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Pleased, like a man, with our libation, Indra, drink, for enduring hero might, the Soma. Lord of Bays, moved by sacrifice come hither: thou with the Swift Ones stirrest floods and waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When thou didst loose the streams to run like racers in the swift contest, having smitten Vrtra With flying weapon where he lay, O Indra, and, godless, kept the Goddesses encompassed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With reverence let us worship mighty Indra, great and sublime, eternal, ever youthful, Whose greatness the dear world-halves have not measured, no, nor conceived the might of him the Holy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Many are Indra's nobly wrought achievements, and none of all the Gods transgress his statutes. He beareth up this earth and heaven, and, doer of marvels, he begot the Sun and Morning.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Herein, O Guileless One, is thy true greatness, that soon as born thou drankest up the Soma. Days may not check the power of thee the Mighty, nor the nights, Indra, nor the months, nor autumns.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As soon as thou wast born in highest heaven thou drankest Soma to delight thee, Indra; And when thou hadst pervaded earth and heaven thou wast the first supporter of the singer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, puissant God, more mighty, slewest. Ahi showing his strength when couched around the waters. The heaven itself attained not to thy greatness when with one hip of thine the earth was shadowed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sacrifice, Indra, made thee wax so mighty, the dear oblation with the flowing Soma. O Worshipful, with worship help our worship, for worship helped thy bolt when slaying Ahi.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With sacrifice and wish have I brought Indra; still for new blessings may I turn him hither, Him magnified by ancient songs and praises, by lauds of later time and days yet recent.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I have brought forth a song when longing seized me: ere the decisive day will I laud Indra; Then may lie safely bear us over trouble, as in a ship, when both sides invocate him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Full is his chalice: Glory! Like a pourer I have filled up the vessel for his drinking. Presented on the right, dear Soma juices have brought us Indra, to rejoice him, hither.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Not the deep-flowing flood, O Much-invoked One! not hills that compass thee about restrain thee, Since here incited, for thy friends, O Indra, thou breakest e'en the firm built stall of cattle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Call we on Maghavan, auspicious Indra, best Hero in this fight where spoil is gathered, The Strong who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vrtras, wins and gathers riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: FORTH from the bosom of the mountains, eager as two swift mares with loosened rein contending, Like two bright mother cows who lick their youngling, Vipas and Sutudri speed down their waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Impelled by Indra whom ye pray to urge you, ye move as 'twere on chariots to the ocean. Flowing together, swelling with your billows, O lucid Streams, each of you seeks the other.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I have attained the most maternal River, we have approached Vipas, the broad, the blessed. Licking as 'twere their calf the pair of Mothers flow onward to their common home together.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We two who rise and swell with billowy waters move forward to the home which Gods have made us. Our flood may not be stayed when urged to motion. What would the singer, calling to the Rivers?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Linger a little at my friendly bidding rest, Holy Ones, a moment in your journey. With hymn sublime soliciting your favour Kusika's son hath called unto the River.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra who wields the thunder dug our channels: he smote down Vrtra, him who stayed our currents. Savitar, God, the lovely-handed, led us, and at his sending forth we flow expanded.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: That hero deed of Indra must be lauded for ever that he rent Ahi in pieces. He smote away the obstructers with his thunder, and eager for their course forth flowed the waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Never forget this word of thine, O singer, which future generations shall reecho. In hymns, O bard, show us thy loving kindness. Humble us not mid men. To thee be honour!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: List quickly, Sisters, to the bard who cometh to you from far away with car and wagon. Bow lowly down; be easy to be traversed stay, Rivers, with your floods below our axles.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yea, we will listen to thy words, O singer. With wain and car from far away thou comest. Low, like a nursing mother, will I bend me, and yield me as a maiden to her lover.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Soon as the Bharatas have fared across thee, the warrior band, urged on and sped by Indra, Then let your streams flow on in rapid motion. I crave your favour who deserve our worship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The warrior host, the Bharatas, fared over the singer won the favour of the Rivers. Swell with your billows, hasting, pouring riches. Fill full your channels, and roll swiftly onward.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So let your wave bear up the pins, and ye, O Waters, spare the thongs; And never may the pair of Bulls, harmless and sinless, waste away.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: FORT-RENDER, Lord of Wealth, dispelling foemen, Indra with lightnings hath o'ercome the Dasa. Impelled by prayer and waxen great in body, he hath filled earth and heaven, the Bounteous Giver.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I stimulate thy zeal, the Strong, the Hero decking my song of praise forth; Immortal. O Indra, thou art equally the Leader of heavenly hosts and human generations.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Leading, his band Indra encompassed Vrtra; weak grew the wily leader of enchanters. He who burns fierce in forests slaughtered Vyamsa, and made the Milch-kine of the nights apparent.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, light-winner, days' Creator, conquered, victorious, hostile bands with those who loved him. For man the days' bright ensign he illumined, and found the light for his joy and gladness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Forward to fiercely falling blows pressed Indra, hero like doing many hero exploits. These holy songs he taught the bard who praised him, and widely spread these Dawns' resplendent colour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They laud the mighty acts of him the Mighty, the many glorious deeds performed by Indra. He in his strength, with all-surpassing prowess, through wondrous arts crushed the malignant Dasyus.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Lord of the brave, Indra who rules the people gave freedom to the Gods by might and battle. Wise singers glorify with chanted praises these his achievements in Vivasvan's dwelling.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Excellent, Conqueror, the victory-giver, the winner of the light and Godlike Waters, He who hath won this broad earth and this heaven, -in Indra they rejoice who love devotions.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He gained possession of the Sun and Horses, Indra obtained the Cow who feedeth many. Treasure of gold he won; he smote the Dasyus, and gave protection to the Aryan colour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He took the plants and days for his possession; he gained the forest trees and air's mid-region. Vala he cleft, and chased away opponents: thus was he tamer of the overweening.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Call we on Maghavan, auspicious Indra, best Hero in the fight where spoil is gathered, The Strong, who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vrtras, wins and gathers treasures.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: MOUNT the Bay Horses to thy chariot harnessed, and come to us like Vayu with his coursers. Thou, hastening to us, shalt drink the Soma. Hail, Indra. We have poured it for thy rapture.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For him, the God who is invoked by many, the two swift Bay Steeds to the pole I harness, That they in fleet course may bring Indra hither, e'en to this sacrifice arranged completely.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bring the strong Steeds who drink the warm libation, and, Bull of Godlike nature, be thou gracious. Let thy Steeds eat; set free thy Tawny Horses, and roasted grain like this consume thou daily.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Those who are yoked by prayer I harness, fleet friendly Bays who take their joy together. Mounting thy firm and easy car, O Indra, wise and all-knowing come thou to the Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: No other worshippers must stay beside them thy Bays, thy vigorous and smooth-backed Coursers. Pass by them all and hasten onward hither: with Soma pressed we will prepare to feast thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thine is this Sorna: hasten to approach it. Drink thou thereof, benevolent, and cease not. Sit on the sacred grass at this our worship, and take these drops into thy belly, Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The grass is strewn for thee, pressed is the Soma; the grain is ready for thy Bays to feed on. To thee who lovest them, the very mighty, strong, girt by Maruts, are these gifts presented.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This the sweet draught, with cows, the men, the mountains, the waters, Indra, have for thee made ready. Come, drink thereof, Sublime One, friendly-minded, foreseeing, knowing well the ways thou goest.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Maruts, they with whom thou sharedst Soma, Indra, who made thee strong and were thine army,- With these accordant, eagerly desirous drink thou this Soma with the tongue of Agni.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Drink, Indra, of the juice by thine own nature, or by the tongue of Agni, O thou Holy. Accept the sacrificial gift, O Sakra, from the Adhvaryu's hand or from the Hotar's.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Call we on Maghavan, auspicious Indra, best Hero in the fight where spoil is gathered, The Strong, who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vrtras, wins and gathers riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WITH constant succours, fain thyself to share it, make this oblation which we bring effective. Grown great through strengthening gifts at each libation, he hath become renowned by mighty exploits.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For Indra were the Somas erst- discovered, whereby he grew strong-jointed, vast, and skilful. Indra , take quickly these presented juices: drink of the strong, that which the strong have shaken.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Drink and wax great. Thine are the juices, Indra, both Somas of old time and these we bring thee. Even as thou drankest, Indra, earlier Somas, so drink to-day, a new guest, meet for praises.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Great and impetuous, mighty-voiced in battle, surpassing power is his, and strength resistless. Him the broad earth hath never comprehended when Somas cheered the Lord of Tawny Coursers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Mighty and strong he waxed for hero exploit: the Bull was furnished a Sage's wisdom. Indra is our kind Lord; his steers have vigour; his cows are many with abundant offspring.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As floods according to their stream flow onward, so to the sea, as borne on cars, the waters. Vaster is Indra even than his dwelling, what time the stalk milked out, the Soma, fills him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Eager to mingle with the sea, the rivers carry the well-pressed Soma juice to Indra. They drain the stalk out with their arms, quick-banded, and cleanse it with a stream of mead and filters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like lakes appear his flanks filled full with Soma: yea, he contains libations in abundance. When Indra had consumed the first sweet viands, he, after slaying Vrtra, claimed the Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Then bring thou hither, and let none prevent it: we know thee well, the Lord of wealth and treasure. That splendid gift which is thine own, O Indra, vouchsafe to us, Lord of the Tawny Coursers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Indra, Maghavan, impetuous mover, grant us abundant wealth that brings all blessings. Give us a hundred autumns for our lifetime: give us, O fair-checked Indra, store of heroes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Call we on Indra, Maghavan, auspicious, best Hero in the fight where spoil is gathered, The Strong, who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vrtras, wins and gathers riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O INDRA, for the strength that slays Vrtra and conquers in the fight, We turn thee hitherward to us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Indra, Lord of Hundred Powers, may those who praise thee hitherward. Direct thy spirit and thine eye.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Indra, Lord of Hundred Powers, with all our songs we invocate Thy names for triumph over foes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We strive for glory through the powers immense of him whom many praise, Of Indra who supports mankind.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For Vrtra's slaughter I address Indra whom many invocate, To win us booty in the wars.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In battles be victorious. We seek thee, Lord of Hundred Powers, Indra, that Vrtra may be slain.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In splendid combats of the hosts, in glories where the fight is won. Indra, be victor over foes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Drink thou the Soma for our help, bright, vigilant, exceeding strong, O Indra, Lord of Hundred Powers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Satakratu, powers which thou mid the Five Races hast displayed- These, Indra, do I claim of thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, great glory hast thou gained. Win splendid fame which none may mar We make thy might perpetual.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come to us either from anear, Or, Sakra, come from far away. Indra, wherever be thy home, come to us thence, O Thunder-armed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: HASTING like some strong courser good at drawing, a thought have I imagined like a workman. Pondering what is dearest and most noble, I long to see the sages full of wisdom.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ask of the sages' mighty generations firm-minded and devout they framed the heaven. These are thy heart-sought strengthening directions, and they have come to be sky's upholders.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Assuming in this world mysterious natures, they decked the heaven and earth for high dominion, Measured with measures, fixed their broad expanses, set the great worlds apart held firm for safety.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Even as he mounted up they all adorned him: self-luminous he travels clothed in splendour. That is the Bull's, the Asura's mighty figure: he, omniform, hath reached the eternal waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: First the more ancient Bull engendered offspring; these are his many draughts that lent him vigour. From days of old ye Kings, two Sons of Heaven, by hymns of sacrifice have won dominion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Three seats ye Sovrans, in the Holy synod, many, yea, all, ye honour with your presence. There saw I, going thither in the spirit, Gandharvas in their course with wind-blown tresses.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: That same companionship of her, the Milch-cow, here with the strong Bull's divers forms they stablished. Enduing still some new celestial figure, the skillful workers shaped a form around him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let no one here debar me from enjoying the golden light which Savitar diffuses. He covers both all-fostering worlds with praises even as a woman cherishes her children.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Fulfil, ye twain, his work, the Great, the Ancient: as heavenly blessing keep your guard around us. All the wise Gods behold his varied actions who stands erect, whose voice is like a herdsman's.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Call we on Indra, Maghavan, auspicious, best Hero in the fight where spoil is gathered, The Strong, who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vrtras, wins and gathers riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To Indra from the heart the hymn proceedeth, to him the Lord, recited, built with praises; The wakening song sung forth in holy synod: that which is born for thee, O Indra, notice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Born from the heaven e'en in the days aforetime, wakening, sting aloud in holy synod, Auspicious, clad in white and shining raiment, this is the ancient hymn of our forefathers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Mother of the Twins hath borne Twin Children: my tongue's tip raised itself and rested silent. Killing the darkness at the light's foundation, the Couple newly born attain their beauty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Not one is found among them, none of mortals, to blame our sires who fought to win the cattle. Their strengthener was Indra the Majestic he spread their stalls of kine the Wonder-Worker.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Where as a Friend with friendly men, Navagvas, with heroes, on his knees he sought the cattle. There, verily with ten Dasagvas Indra found the Sun lying hidden in the darkness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra found meath collected in the milch-cow, by foot and hoof, in the cow's place of pasture. That which lay secret, hidden in the waters, he held in his right hand, the rich rewarder.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He took the light, discerning it from darkness: may we be far removed from all misfortune. These songs, O Soma-drinker, cheered by Soma, Indra, accept from thy most zealous poet.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let there be light through both the worlds for worship: may we be far from most overwhelming evil. Great woe comes even from the hostile mortal, piled up; but good at rescue are the Vasus.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Call we on Maghavan, auspicious Indra, best Hero in the fight where spoil is gathered, The Strong, who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vrtras, wins and gathers riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THEE, Indra, we invoke, the Bull, what time the Soma is expressed. So drink thou of the savoury juice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, whom many laud, accept the strength-conferring Soma juice: Quaff, pour down drink that satisfies.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, with all the Gods promote our wealth-bestowing sacrifice, Thou highly-lauded Lord of men.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Lord of the brave, to thee proceed these drops of Soma juice expressed, The bright drops to thy dwelling-place.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Within thy belly, Indra, take juice, Soma the most excellent: Thine are the drops celestial.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Drink our libation, Lord of hymns: with streams of meath thou art bedewed Our glory, Indra, is thy gift.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To Indra go the treasures of the worshipper, which never fail: He drinks the Soma and is strong
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: From far away, from near at hand, O Vrtra-slayer, come to us: Accept the songs we sing to thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When from the space between the near and far thou art invoked by us, Thence, Indra. come thou hitherward.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: INVOKED to drink the Soma juice, come with thy Bay Steeds, Thunder-armed Come, Indra, hitherward to me.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Our priest is seated, true to time; the grass is regularly strewn; The pressing-stones were set at morn.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These prayers, O thou who hearest prayer are offered: seat thee on the grass. Hero, enjoy the offered cake.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Vrtra-slayer, be thou pleased with these libations, with these hymns, Song-loving Indra, with our lauds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Our hymns caress the Lord of Strength, vast, drinker of the Soma's juice, Indra, as mother-cows their calf.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Delight thee with the juice we pour for thine own great munificence: Yield not thy singer to reproach.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We, Indra, dearly loving thee, bearing oblation, sing thee hymns Thou, Vasu, dearly lovest us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O thou to whom thy Bays are dear, loose not thy Horses far from us: Here glad thee, Indra, Lord divine.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May long-maned Coursers, dropping oil, bring thee on swift car hitherward, Indra, to seat thee on the grass.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: COME to the juice that we have pressed, to Sorna, Indra, bleat with milk: Come, favouring us, thy Bay-drawn car!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come, Indra, to this gladdening drink, placed on the grass, pressed out with stones: Wilt thou not drink thy fill thereof?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To Indra have my songs of praise gone forth, thus rapidly sent hence, To turn him to the Soma-draught.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hither with songs of praise we call Indra to drink the Soma juice: Will he not come to us by lauds?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, these Somas are expressed. Take them within thy belly, Lord Of Hundred Powers, thou Prince of Wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We know thee winner of the spoil, and resolute in battles, Sage! Therefore thy blessing we implore.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Borne hither by thy Stallions, drink, Indra, this juice which we have pressed, Mingled with barley and with milk.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, for thee, in thine own place, I urge the Soma for thy draught: Deep in thy heart let it remain,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We call on thee, the Ancient One, Indra, to drink the Soma juice, We Kusikas who seek thine aid.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: MOUNTED upon thy chariot-seat approach us: thine is the Soma-draught from days aforetime. Loose for the sacred grass thy dear companions. These men who bring oblation call thee hither.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come our true Friend, passing by many people; come with thy two Bay Steeds to our devotions; For these our hymns are calling thee, O Indra, hymns formed for praise, soliciting thy friendship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Pleased, with thy Bay Steeds, Indra, God, come quickly to this our sacrifice that heightens worship; For with my thoughts, presenting oil to feed thee, I call thee to the feast of sweet libations.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yea, let thy two Bay Stallions bear thee hither, well limbed and good to draw, thy dear companions. Pleased with the corn-blent offering which we bring thee, may Indra, Friend, hear his friend's adoration.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wilt thou not make me guardian of the people, make me, impetuous Maghavan, their ruler? Make me a Rsi having drunk of Soma? Wilt thou not give me wealth that lasts for ever?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yoked to thy chariot, led thy tall Bays, Indra, companions of thy banquet, bear thee hither, Who from of old press to heaven's farthest limits, the Bull's impetuous and well-groomed Horses.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Drink of the strong pressed out by strong ones, Indra, that which the Falcon brought thee when thou longedst; In whose wild joy thou stirrest up the people, in whose wild joy thou didst unbar the cow-stalls.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Call we on Indra, Makhavan, auspicious, best Hero in the fight where spoil is gathered; The Strong, who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vrtras, wins and gathers riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May this delightsome Soma be expressed for thee by tawny stones. Joying thereat, O Indra, with thy Bay Steeds come: ascend thy golden-coloured car.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In love thou madest Usas glow, in love thou madest Surya shine. Thou, Indra, knowing, thinking, Lord of Tawny Steeds, above all glories waxest great.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The heaven with streams of golden hue, earth with her tints of green and gold- The golden Pair yield Indra plenteous nourishment: between them moves the golden One.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When born to life the golden Bull illumines all the realm of light. He takes his golden weapon, Lord of Tawny Steeds, the golden thunder in his arms.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The bright, the well-loved thunderbolt, girt with the bright, Indra disclosed, Disclosed the Soma juice pressed out by tawny stones, with tawny steeds drave forth the kine.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: COME hither, Indra, with Bay Steeds, joyous, with tails like peacocks' plumes. Let no men cheek thy course as fowlers stay the bird: pass o'er them as o'er desert lands.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who slew Vrtra, burst the cloud, brake the strongholds and drave the floods, Indra who mounts his chariot at his Bay Steeds' cry, shatters e'en things that stand most firm.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like pools of water deep and full, like kine thou cherishest thy might; Like the milch-cows that go well-guarded to the mead, like water-brooks that reach the lake.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bring thou us wealth with power to strike, our share, 'gainst him who calls it his. Shake, Indra, as with hooks, the tree for ripened fruit, for wealth to satisfy our wish.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, self-ruling Lord art thou, good Leader, of most glorious fame. So, waxen in thy strength, O thou whom many praise, be thou most swift to hear our call.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: OF thee, the Bull, the Warrior, Sovran Ruler, joyous and fierce, ancient and ever youthful, The undecaying One who wields the thunder, renowned and great, great are the exploits, Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Great art thou, Mighty Lord, through manly vigour, O fierce One, gathering spoil, subduing others, Thyself alone the universe's Sovran: so send forth men to combat and to rest them.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He hath surpassed all measure in his brightness, yea, and the Gods, for none may be his equal. Impetuous Indra in his might exceedeth wide vast mid-air and heaven and earth together.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To Indra, even as rivers to the ocean, flow forth from days of old the Soma juices; To him wide deep and mighty from his birth-time, the well of holy thoughts, all-comprehending.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Soma, Indra, which the earth and heaven bear for thee as a mother bears her infant, This they send forth to thee, this, vigorous Hero! Adhvaryus purify for thee to drink of.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: DRINK, Indra, Marut-girt, as Bull, the Soma, for joy, for rapture even as thou listest. Pour down the flood of meath within thy belly: thou from of old art King of Soma juices.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, accordant, with the banded Maruts, drink Soma, Hero, as wise Vrtra-slayer. Slay thou our foemen, drive away assailants and make us safe on every side from danger.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And, drinker at due seasons, drink in season, Indra, with friendly Gods, our pressed-out Soma. The Maruts following, whom thou madest sharers, gave thee the victory, and thou slewest Vrtra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Drink Soma, Indra, banded with the Maruts who, Maghavan, strengthened thee at Ahi's slaughter, 'Gainst Sambara, Lord of Bays! in winning cattle, and now rejoice in thee, the holy Singers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Bull whose strength hath waxed, whom Maruts follow, free-giving Indra, the celestial Ruler, Mighty, all-conquering, the victory-giver, him let us call to grant us new protection.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: SOON as the young Bull sprang into existence he longed to taste the pressed-out Soma's liquor. Drink thou thy fill, according to thy longing, first, of the goodly mixture blent with Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: That day when thou wast born thou, fain to taste it, drankest the plant's milk which the mountains nourish. That milk thy Mother first, the Dame who bare thee, poured for thee in thy mighty Father's dwelling.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Desiring food he came unto his Mother, and on her breast beheld the pungent Soma. Wise, he moved on, keeping aloof the others, and wrought great exploits in his varied aspects.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Fierce, quickly conquering, of surpassing vigour, he framed his body even as he listed. E'en from his birth-time Indra conquered Tvastar, bore off the Soma and in beakers drank it.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Call we on Maghavan, auspicious Indra, best Hero in the fight where spoil is gathered; The Strong, who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vrtras, wins and gathers riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: GREAT Indra will I laud, in whom all people who drink the Soma have attained their longing; Whom, passing wise, Gods, Heaven and Earth, engendered, formed by a Master's hand, to crush the Vrtras.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whom, most heroic, borne by Tawny Coursers, verily none subdueth in the battle; Who, reaching far, most vigorous, hath shortened the Dasyu's life with Warriors bold of spirit.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Victor in fight, swift mover like a warhorse, pervading both worlds, rainer down of blessings, To be invoked in war like Bhaga, Father, as 'twere, of hymns, fair, prompt to hear, strength-giver.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Supporting heaven, the high back of the region, his car is Vayu with his team of Vasus. Illumining the nights, the Sun's creator, like Dhisana he deals forth strength and riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Call we on Maghavan, auspicious Indra, best Hero in the fight where spoil is gathered; The Strong, who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vrtras, wins and gathers treasure.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: LET Indra drink, All-hail! for his is Soma,-the mighty Bull come, girt by Maruts, hither. Far-reaching, let him fill him with these viands, and let our offering sate his body's longing.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I yoke thy pair of trusty Steeds for swiftness, whose faithful service from of old thou lovest. Here, fair of cheek! let thy Bay Coursers place thee: drink of this lovely welleffused libation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With milk they made Indra their good Preserver, lauding for help and rule the bounteous rainer. Impetuous God, when thou hast drunk the Soma, enraptured send us cattle in abundance.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With kine and horses satisfy this longing with very splendid bounty still extend it. Seeking the light, with hymns to thee, O Indra, the Kusikas have brought their gift, the singers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Call we on Maghavan, auspicious Indra, best Hero in the fight where spoil is gathered; The Strong, who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vrtras, wins and gathers riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: HIGH hymns have sounded forth the praise of Maghavan, supporter of mankind, of Indra meet for lauds; Him who hath waxen great, invoked with beauteous songs, Immortal One, whose praise each day is sung aloud.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To Indra from all sides go forth my songs of praise, the Lord of Hundred Powers, strong, Hero, like the sea, Swift, winner of the booty, breaker-down of forts, faithful and ever-glorious, finder of the light.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Where battle's spoil is piled the singer winneth praise, for Indra taketh care of matchless worshippers. He in Vivasvan's dwelling findeth his delight: praise thou the ever-conquering slayer of the foe.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thee, valorous, most heroic of the heroes, shall the priests glorify with song and praises. Full of all wondrous power he goes to conquest: worship is his, sole Lord from days aforetime.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Abundant are the gifts he gives to mortals: for him the earth bears a rich store of treasures. The heavens, the growing plants, the living waters, the forest trees preserve their wealth for Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To thee, O Indra, Lord of Bays, for ever are offered prayers and songs: accept them gladly. As Kinsman think thou of some fresh assistance; good Friend, give strength and life to those who praise thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Here, Indra, drink thou Soma with the Maruts, as thou didst drink the juice beside Saryata. Under thy guidance, in thy keeping, Hero, the singers serve, skilled in fair sacrifices.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So eagerly desirous drink the Soma, our juice, O Indra, with thy friends the Maruts, Since at thy birth all Deities adorned thee for the great fight, O thou invoked of many.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He was your comrade in your zeal, O Maruts: they, rich in noble gifts, rejoiced in Indra. With them together let the Vrtra-slayer drink in his home the worshipper's libation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So, Lord of affluent gifts, this juice hath been pressed for thee with strength Drink of it, thou who lovest song.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Incline thy body to this juice which suits thy Godlike nature well: May it cheer thee who lovest it.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Brave Indra, let it work through both thy flanks, and through thy head by prayer, And through thine arms, to prosper us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: INDRA, accept at break of day our Soma mixt with roasted corn, With groats with cake, with eulogies.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Accept, O Indra, and enjoy the well-dressed sacrificial cake: Oblations are poured forth to thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Consume our sacrificial cake, accept the songs of praise we sing, As he who woes accepts his bride.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Famed from of old, accept the cake at our libation poured at dawn, For great, O Indra, is thy power.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let roasted corn of our midday libation, and sacrificial cake here please thee, Indra, What time the lauding singer, keen of purpose and eager as a bull, with hymns implores thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: At the third sacrifice, O thou whom many praise, give glory to the roasted corn and holy cake. With offered viands and with songs may we assist thee, Sage, whom Vaja and the Rbhus wait upon.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The groats have we prepared for thee with Pusan, corn for thee, Lord of Bay Steeds, with thy horses. Eat thou the meal-cake, banded with the Maruts, wise Hero, Vrtra-slayer, drink the Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bring forth the roasted corn to meet him quickly, cake for the bravest Hero mid the heroes. Indra, may hymns accordant with thee daily strengthen thee, Bold One, for the draught of Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: ON a high car, O Parvata and Indra, bring pleasant viands, with brave heroes, hither. Enjoy the gifts, Gods, at our sacrifices wax strong by hymns, rejoice in our oblation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Stay still, O Maghavan, advance no farther. a draught of well-pressed Soma will I give thee. With sweetest song I grasp, O Mighty Indra, thy garment's hem as a child grasps his father's.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Adhvaryu, sing we both; sing thou in answer: make we a laud acceptable to Indra. Upon this sacrificer's grass he seated: to Indra shall our eulogy be uttered.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: A wife, O Maghavan is home and dwelling: so let thy Bay Steeds yoked convey thee hither. Whenever we press out for thee the Soma, let Agni as our Herald speed to call thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Depart, O Maghavan; again come hither: both there and here thy goat is Indra, Brother, Where thy tall chariot hath a place to rest in, and where thou loosest thy loud-neighing Courser.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou hast drunk Soma, Indra, turn thee homeward; thy joy is in thy home, thy gracious Consort; Where thy tall chariot hath a place to rest in, and thy strong Courser is set free with guerdon.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bounteous are these, Angirases, Virupas: the Asura's Heroes and the Sons of Heaven. They, giving store of wealth to Visvamitra, prolong his life through countless Soma-pressings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Maghavan weareth every shape at pleasure, effecting magic changes in his body, Holy One, drinker out of season, coming thrice, in a moment, through fit prayers, from heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The mighty sage, God-born and God-incited, who looks on men, restrained the billowy river. When Visvamitra was Sudas's escort, then Indra through the Kusikas grew friendly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary
