verses.translation: Like swans, prepare a song of praise with pressing-stones, glad in your hymns with juice poured forth in sacrifice. Ye singers, with the Gods, sages who look on men, ye Kutikas drink up the Soma's savoury meath.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come forward, Kusikas, and be attentive; let loose Sudas's horse to win him riches. East, west, and north, let the King slay the foeman, then at earth's choicest place perform his worship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Praises to Indra have I sung, sustainer of this earth and heaven. This prayer of Visvamitra keeps secure the race of Bharatas.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Visvamitras have sung forth this prayer to Indra Thunder-aimed: So let him make us prosperous.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Among the Kikatas what do thy cattle? They pour no milky draught, they heat no caldron. Bring thou to us the wealth of Pramaganda; give up to us, O Maghavan, the low-born.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sasarpari, the gift of Jamadagnis, hath lowed with mighty voice dispelling famine. The Daughter of the Sun hath spread our glory among the Gods, imperishable, deathless.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sasarpari brought glory speedily to these, over the generations of the Fivefold Race; Daughter of Paksa, she bestows new vital power, she whom the ancient Jamadagnis gave to me.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Strong be the pair of oxen, firm the axles, let not the pole slip nor the yoke be broken. May Indra, keep the yoke-pins from decaying: attend us, thou whose fellies are uninjured.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Indra, give our bodies strength, strength to the bulls who draw the wains, Strength to our seed and progeny that they may live, for thou art he who giveth strength.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Enclose thee in the heart of Khayar timber, in the car wrought of Sinsapa put firmness. Show thyself strong, O Axle, fixed and strengthened: throw us not from the car whereon we travel.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let not this sovran of the wood leave us forlorn or injure us. Safe may we be until we reach our homes and rest us and unyoke.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With various aids this day come to us, Indra, with best aids speed us, Maghavan, thou Hero. Let him who hateth us fall headlong downward: him whom we hate let vital breath abandon.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He heats his very axe, and then cuts a mere Semal blossom off. O Indra, like a caldron cracked and seething, so he pours out foam.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Men notice not the arrow, O ye people; they bring the red beast deeming it a bullock. A sluggish steed men run not with the courser, nor ever lead an ass before a charger.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These men, the sons of Bharata, O Indra, regard not severance or close connexion. They urge their own steed as it were another's, and take him, swift as the bow's string, to battle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To him adorable, mighty, meet for synods, this strengthening hymn, unceasing, have they offered. May Agni hear us with his homely splendours, hear us, Eternal One, with heavenly lustre.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To mighty Heaven and Earth I sing forth loudly: my wish goes out desirous and well knowing Both, at whose laud in synods, showing favour, the Gods rejoice them with the living mortal.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Heaven and Earth, may your great law he faithful: he ye our leaders for our high advantage. To Heaven and Earth I offer this my homage, with food, O Agni, as I pray for riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yea, holy Heaven and Earth, the ancient sages whose word was ever true had power to find you; And brave men in the fight where heroes conquer, O Earth, have known you well and paid you honour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What pathway leadeth to the Gods? Who knoweth this of a truth, and who will now declare it? Seen are their lowest dwelling-places only, but they are in remote and secret regions.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Sage who looketh on mankind hath viewed them bedewed, rejoicing in the seat of Order. They make a home as for a bird, though parted, with one same will finding themselves together.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Partners though parted, with far-distant limits, on one firm place both stand for ever watchful, And, being young for evermore, as sisters, speak to each other names that are united.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: All living things they part and keep asunder; though bearing up the mighty Gods they reel not. One All is Lord of what is fixed and moving, that walks, that flies, this multiform creation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Afar the Ancient from of old I ponder, our kinship with our mighty Sire and Father,- Singing the praise whereof the Gods by custom stand on the spacious far-extended pathway.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This laud, O Heaven and Earth, to you I utter: let the kind-hearted hear, whose tongue is Agni, Young, Sovran Rulers, Varuna and Mitra, the wise and very glorious Adityas.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The fair-tongued Savitar, the golden-handed, comes thrice from heaven as Lord in our assembly. Bear to the Gods this song of praise, and send us, then, Savitar, complete and perfect safety.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Deft worker, skiful-handed, helpful, holy, may Tvastar, God, give us these things to aid us, Take your delight, Ye Rbhus joined with Pusan: ye have prepared the rite with stones adjusted.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Borne on their flashing car, the spear-armed Maruts, the nimble Youths of Heaven, the Sons of Order, The Holy, and Sarasvati, shall hear us: ye Mighty, give us wealth with noble offspring.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To Visnu rich in marvels, songs And praises shall go as singers on the road of Bhaga,- The Chieftain of the Mighty Stride, whose Mothers, the many young Dames, never disregard him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, who rules through all his powers heroic, hath with his majesty filled earth and heaven. Lord of brave hosts, Fort-crusher, Vrtra-slayer, gather thou up and bring us store of cattle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: My Sires are the Nasatyas, kind tokensmen: the Asvins' kinship is a glorious title. For ye are they who give us store of riches: ye guard your gift uncheated by the bounteous.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This is, ye Wise, your great and glorious title, that all ye Deities abide in Indra. Friend, Much-invoked! art thou with thy dear Rbhus: fashion ye this our hymn for our advantage.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Aryaman, Aditi deserve our worship: the laws of Varuna remain unbroken. The lot of childlessness remove ye from us, and let our course be rich in kine and offspring.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May the Gods' envoy, sent to many a quarter, proclaim us sinless for our perfect safety. May Earth and Heaven, the Sun, the waters, hear us, and the wide firmament and constellations.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hear us the mountains which distil the rain-drops, and, resting firm, rejoice in freshening moisture. May Aditi with the Adityas hear us, and Maruts grant us their auspicious shelter.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Soft be our path for ever, well-provisioned: with pleasant meath, O Gods, the herbs besprinkle. Safe be my bliss, O Agni, in thy friendship: may I attain the seat of foodful riches,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Enjoy the offering: beam thou strength upon us; combine thou for our good all kinds of glory. Conquer in battle, Agni, all those foemen, and light us every day with loving kindness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: AT the first shining of the earliest Mornings, in the Cow's home was born the Great Eternal. Now shall the statutes of the Gods be valid. Great is the Gods' supreme and sole dominion -
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let not the Gods here injure us, O Agni, nor Fathers of old time who know the region, Nor the sign set between two ancient dwellings. Great is the Gods' supreme and sole dominion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: My wishes fly abroad to many places: I glance back to the ancient sacrifices. Let us declare the truth when fire is kindled. Great is the Gods' supreme and sole dominion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: King Universal, born to sundry quarters, extended through the wood be lies on couches. One Mother rests: another feeds the Infant. Great is the Gods' supreme and sole dominion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Lodged in old plants, he grows again in younger, swiftly within the newly-born and tender. Though they are unimpregned, he makes them fruitful. Great is the Gods' supreme and sole dominion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now lying far away, Child of two Mothers, he wanders unrestrained, the single youngling. These are the laws of Varuna and Mitra. Great is the Gods' supreme and sole dominion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Child of two Mothers, Priest, sole Lord in synods, he still precedes while resting as foundation. They who speak sweetly bring him sweet addresses. Great is the Gods' supreme and sole dominion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As to a friendly warrior when he battles, each thing that comes anear is seen to meet him. The hymn commingles with the cow's oblation. Great is the Gods' supreme and sole dominion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Deep within these the hoary envoy pierceth; mighty, he goeth to the realm of splendour, And looketh on us, clad in wondrous beauty. Great is the Gods' supreme and sole dominion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Visnu, the guardian, keeps the loftiest station, upholding dear, immortal dwelling-places. Agni knows well all these created beings. Great is the Gods' supreme and sole dominion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye, variant Pair, have made yourselves twin beauties: one of the Twain is dark, bright shines the other; And yet these two, the dark, the red, are Sisters. Great is the Gods' supreme and sole dominion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Where the two Cows, the Mother and the Daughter, meet and give suck yielding their lordly nectar, I praise them at the seat of law eternal. Great is the Gods' supreme and sole dominion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Loud hath she lowed, licking the other's youngling. On what world hath the Milch-cow laid her udder? This Ila streameth with the milk of Order. Great is the Gods' supreme and sole dominion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Earth weareth beauties manifold: uplifted, licking her Calf of eighteen months, she standeth. Well-skilled I seek the seat of law eternal. Great is the Gods' supreme and sole dominion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Within a wondrous place the Twain are treasured: the one is manifest, the other hidden. One common pathway leads in two directions. Great is the Gods' supreme and sole dominion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let the milch-kine that have no calves storm downward, yielding rich nectar, streaming, unexhausted, These who are ever new and fresh and youthful. Great is the Gods' supreme and sole dominion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What time the Bull bellows in other regions, another herd receives the genial moisture; For he is Bhaga, King, the earth's Protector. Great is the Gods' supreme and sole dominion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let us declare the Hero's wealth in horses, O all ye folk: of this the Gods have knowledge. Sixfold they bear him, or by fives are harnessed. Great is the Gods' supreme and sole dominion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Tvastar the God, the omniform. Creator, begets and feeds mankind in various manner. His, verily, arc all these living creatures. Great is the Gods' supreme dominion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The two great meeting Bowls hath he united: each of the Pair is laden with his treasure. The Hero is renowned for gathering riches. Great is the Gods' supreme and sole dominion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yea, and on this our earth the All-Sustainer dwells like a King with noble friends about him. In his protection heroes rest in safety. Great is the Cods' supreme and sole dominion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Rich in their gifts for thee are herbs and waters, and earth brings all her wealth for thee, O Indra. May we as friends of thine share goodly treasures. Great is the Gods' supreme and sole dominion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: NOT men of magic skill, not men of wisdom impair the Gods' first steadfast ordinances. Ne'er may the earth and heaven which know not malice, nor the fixed hills, be bowed by sage devices.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: One, moving not away, supports six burthens: the Cows proceed to him the true, the Highest. Near stand three Mighty Ones who travel swiftly: two are concealed from sight, one is apparent.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Bull who wears all shapes, the triple-breasted, three-uddered, with a brood in many places, Ruleth majestic with his triple aspect, the Bull, the Everlasting Ones' impregner.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When nigh them, as their tracer he observed them: he called aloud the dear name of Adityas. The Goddesses, the Waters, stayed to meet him: they who were wandering separate enclosed him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Streams! the wise Gods have thrice three habitations. Child of three Mothers, he is Lord in synods. Three are the holy Ladies of the Waters, thrice here from heaven supreme in our assembly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Do thou, O Savitar, from heaven thrice hither, three times a day, send down thy blessings daily. Send us, O Bhaga, triple wealth and treasure; cause the two worlds to prosper us, Preserver!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Savitar thrice from heaven pours down abundance, and the fair-handed Kings Varuna, Mitra; And spacious Heaven and Earth, yea, and the Waters, solicit wealth that Savitar may send us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Three are the bright realms, best, beyond attainment, and three, the Asura's Heroes, rule as Sovrans, Holy and vigorous, never to be injured. Thrice may the Gods from heaven attend our synod.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: MY thought with fine discernment hath discovered the Cow who wanders free without a herdsman, Her who hath straightway poured me food in plenty: Indra and Agni therefore are her praisers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra and Pusan, deft of hand and mighty, well-pleased have drained the heaven's exhaustless udder. As in this praise the Gods have all delighted, may I win blessing here from you, O Vasus.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Fain to lend vigour to the Bull, the sister with reverence recognize the germ within him. The Cows come lowing hither to the Youngling, to him endued with great and wondrous beauties.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Fixing with thought, at sacrifice, the press-stones, I bid the well-formed Heaven and Earth come hither; For these thy flames, which give men boons in plenty, rise up on high, the beautiful, the holy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, thy meath-sweet tongue that tastes fair viands, which among Gods is called the far-extended,- Therewith make all the Holy Odes be seated here for our help, and feed them with sweet juices.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let thy stream give us drink, O God, O Agni, wonderful and exhaustless like the rain-clouds. Thus care for us, O Vasu Jatavedas, show us thy loving-kindness, reaching all men.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THE Ancient's Milch-cow yields the things we long for: the Son of Daksina travels between them. She with the splendid chariot brings refulgence. The praise of Usas hath awoke the Asvins.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They bear you hither by well-ordered statute: our sacred offerings rise as if to parents. Destroy in us the counsel of the niggard come hitherward, for we have shown you favour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With lightly-rolling car and well-yoked horses hear this, the press-stone's song, ye Wonder-Workers. Have not the sages of old time, ye Asvins, called you most prompt to come and stay misfortune?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Remember us, and come to us, for ever men, as their wont is, invocate the Asvins. Friends as it were have offered you these juices, sweet, blent with milk at the first break of morning.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Even through many regions, O ye Asvins high praise is yours among mankind, ye Mighty- Come, helpers, on the paths which Gods have travelled: here your libations of sweet meath are ready.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ancient your home, auspicious is your friendship: Heroes, your wealth is with the house of Jahnu. Forming again with you auspicious friendship, let us rejoice with draughts of meath together.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Asvins, Very Mighty ones, with Vayu and with his steeds, one-minded, ever-youthful, Nasatyas, joying in the third day's Soma, drink it, not hostile, Very Bounteous Givers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Asvins, to you are brought abundant viands in rivalry with sacred songs, unceasing. Sprung from high Law your car, urged on by press-stones, goes round the earth and heaven in one brief moment.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Asvins, your Soma sheds delicious sweetness: drink ye thereof and come unto our dwelling. Your car, assuming many a shape, most often goes to the Soma-presser's place of meeting.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: MITRA, when speaking, stirreth men to labour: Mitra sustaineth both the earth and heaven. Mitra beholdeth men with eyes that close not. To Mitra bring, with holy oil, oblation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Foremost be he who brings thee food, O Mitra, who strives to keep thy sacred Law, Aditya. He whom thou helpest ne'er is slain or conquered, on him, from near or far, falls no affliction.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: joying in sacred food and free from sickness, with knees bent lowly on the earth's broad surface, Following closely the Aditya's statute, may we remain in Mitra's gracious favour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Auspicious and adorable, this Mitra was born with fair dominion, King, Disposer. May we enjoy the grace of him the Holy, yea, rest in his propitious loving-kindness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The great Aditya, to be served with worship, who stirreth men, is gracious to the singer. To Mitra, him most highly to be lauded, offer in fire oblation that he loveth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The gainful grace of Mitra, God, supporter of the race of man, Gives splendour of most glorious fame.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Mitra whose glory spreads afar, he who in might surpasses heaven, Surpasses earth in his renown.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: All the Five Races have repaired to Mitra, ever strong to aid, For he sustaineth all the Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Mitra to Gods, to living men, to him who strews the holy grass, Gives food fulfilling sacred Law.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: HERE is your ghostly kinship, here, O Men: they came desirous to these holy rites with store of wealth, With wondrous arts, whereby, with schemes to meet each need, Ye gained, Sudhanvan's Sons! your share in sacrifice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The mighty powers wherewith. ye formed the chalices, the thought by which ye drew the cow from out the hide, The intellect wherewith ye wrought the two Bay Steeds,-through these, O Rbhus, ye attained divinity.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Friendship with Indra have the Rbhus, fully gained: grandsons of Manu, they skilfully urged the work. Sudhanvan's Children won them everlasting life, serving with holy rites, pious with noble acts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In company with Indra come ye to the juice, then gloriously shall your wishes be fulfilled. Not to be paragoned, ye Priests, are your good deeds, nor your heroic acts, Rbhus, Sudhanvan's Sons.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Indra, with the Rbhus, Mighty Ones, pour down the Soma juice effused, well-blent, from both thy hands. Maghavan, urged by song, in the drink-offerer's house rejoice thee with the Heroes, with Sudhanvan's Sons.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With Rbhu near, and Vaja, Indra, here exult, with Saci, praised of many, in the juice we pour. These homes wherein we dwell have turned themselves to thee, devotions to the Gods, as laws of men ordain.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come with the mighty Rbhus, Indra, come to us, strengthening with thy help the singer's holy praise; At hundred eager calls come to the living man, with thousand arts attend the act of sacrifice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Usas, strong with strength, endowed with knowledge, accept the singer's praise, O wealthy Lady. Thou, Goddess, ancient, young, and full of wisdom, movest, all-bounteous! as the Law ordaineth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Shine forth, O Morning, thou auspicious Goddess, on thy bright car awaking pleasant voices. Let docile horses of far-reaching splendour convey thee hitherward, the golden coloured.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, Morning, turning thee to every creature, standest on high as ensign of the Immortal, To one same goal ever and ever wending now, like a wheel, O newly-born, roll hither.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Letting her reins drop downward, Morning cometh, the wealthy Dame, the Lady of the dwelling; Bringing forth light, the Wonderful, the Blessed hath spread her from the bounds of earth and heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hither invoke the radiant Goddess Morning, and bring with reverence your hymn to praise her. She, dropping sweets, hath set in heaven her brightness, and, fair to look on, hath beamed forth her splendour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: From heaven, with hymns, the Holy One was wakened: brightly to both worlds came the wealthy Lady. To Morning, Agni, when she comes refulgent, thou goest forth soliciting fair riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: On Law's firm base the speeder of the Mornings, the Bull, hath entered mighty earth and heaven. Great is the power of Varuna and Mitra, which, bright, hath spread in every place its splendour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: YOUR well-known prompt activities aforetime needed no impulse from your faithful servant. Where, Indra-Varuna, is now that glory wherewith ye brought support to those who loved you?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This man, most diligent, seeking after riches, incessantly invokes you for your favour. Accordant, Indra-Varuna, with Maruts, with Heaven and Earth, hear ye mine invocation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Indra-Varuna, ours be this treasure ours be wealth, Maruts, with full store of heroes. .May the Varutris with their shelter aid us, and Bharati and Hotri with the Mornings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Be pleased! with our oblations, thou loved of all Gods, Brhaspati: Give wealth to him who brings thee gifts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: At sacrifices, with your hymns worship the pure Brhaspati- I pray for power which none may bend-
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Bull of men, whom none deceive, the wearer of each shape at will, Brhaspati Most Excellent.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Divine, resplendent Pusan, this our newest hymn of eulogy, By us is chanted forth to thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Accept with favour this my song, be gracious to the earnest thought, Even as a bridegroom to his bride.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May he who sees all living things, see, them together at a glancc,- May lie, may Pusan be our help.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May we attain that excellent glory of Savitar the God: So May he stimulate our prayers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With understanding, earnestly, of Savitar the God we crave Our portion of prosperity.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Men, singers worship Savitar the God with hymn and holy rites, Urged by the impulse of their thoughts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Soma who gives success goes forth, goes to the gathering place of Gods, To seat him at the seat of Law.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To us and to our cattle may Soma give salutary food, To biped and to quadruped.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Soma, strengthening our power of life, and conquering our foes, In our assembly take his seat.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Mitra-Varuna, sapient Pair, bedew our pasturage with oil, With meath the regions of the air.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Far-ruling, joyful when adored, ye reign through majesty of might, With pure laws everlastingly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Lauded by Jamadagni's song, sit in the place of holy Law: Drink Soma, ye who strengthen Law.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THEE Agni, have the Gods, ever of one accord, sent hither down, a God, appointed messenger, yea, with their wisdom sent thee down. The Immortal, O thou Holy One, mid mortal men, the God-devoted God, the wise, have they brought forth, brought forth the omnipresent God-devoted Sage.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As such, O Agni, bring with favour to the Gods thy Brother Varuna who loveth sacrifice, True to the Law, the Aditya who supporteth men, the King, supporter of mankind.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Do thou, O Friend, turn hither him who is our Friend, swift as a wheel, like two car-steeds in rapid course, Wondrous! to us in rapid course. O Agni, find thou grace for us with Varuna, with Maruts who illumine all. Bless us, thou Radiant One, for seed and progeny, yea, bless us, O thou Wondrous God.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Do thou who knowest Varuna, O Agni, put far away from us the God's displeasure. Best Sacrificer, brightest One, refulgent remove thou far from us all those who hate us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Be thou, O Agni, nearest us with succour, our closest Friend while now this Morn is breaking. Reconcile to us Varuna, be bounteous enjoy the gracious juice; be swift to hear us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Excellent is the glance, of brightest splendour, which the auspicious God bestows on mortals- The God's glance, longed-for even as the butter, pure, heated, of the cow, the milch-cow's bounty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Three are those births, the true, the most exalted, eagerly longed-for, of the God, of Agni. He came invested in the boundless region, pure, radiant, friendly, mightily resplendent.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This envoy joyeth in all seats of worship, borne on his golden car, sweet-tongued Invoker: Lovely to look on, with red steeds, effulgent, like a feast rich in food, joyous for ever.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Allied by worship, let him give man knowledge: by an extended cord they lead him onward. He stays, effectual in this mortal's dwelling, and the God wins a share in his possessions.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let Agni -for he knows the way- conduct us to all that he enjoys of God-sent riches, What all the Immortals have prepared with wisdom, Dyaus, Sire, Begetter, raining down true blessings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In houses first he sprang into existence, at great heaven's base, and in this region's bosom; Footless and headless, both his ends concealing, in his Bull's lair drawing himself together.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wondrously first he rose aloft, defiant, in the Bull's lair, the home of holy Order, Longed-for, young, beautiful, and far-resplendent: and seven dear friends sprang up unto the Mighty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Here did our human fathers take their places, fain to fulfil the sacred Law of worship. Forth drave they, with loud call, Dawn's teeming Milch-kine bid in the mountain stable, in the cavern.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Splendid were they when they had rent the mountain: others, around, shall tell forth this their exploit. They sang their song, prepared to free the cattle: they found the light; with holy hymns they worshipped.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Eager, with thought intent upon the booty, the men with their celestial speech threw open, The solid mountain firm, compact, enclosing, confining Cows, the stable full of cattle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Milch-cow's earliest name they comprehended: they found the Mother's thrice-seven noblest titles. This the bands knew, and sent forth acclamation: with the Bull's sheen the Red One was apparent.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The turbid darkness fled, the heaven was splendid! up rose the bright beam of celestial Morning. Surya ascended to the wide expanses, beholding deeds of men both good and evil.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Then, afterwards they looked around, awakened, when first they held that Heaven allotted treasure. Now all the Gods abide in all their dwellings. Varuna, Mitra, be the prayer effective.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I will call hither brightly-beaming Agni, the Herald, all-supporting, best at worship. He hath disclosed, like the milch cows' pure udder, the Sorria's juice when cleansed and poured from beakers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The freest God of all who should be worshipped, the guest who is received in all men's houses, Agni who hath secured the Gods' high favour,-may he be gracious, to us Jatavedas.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THE, Faithful One, Immortal among mortals, a God among the Gods, appointed envoy, Priest, best at worship, must shine forth in glory . Agni shall be raised high with man's oblations.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Born for us here this day, O Son of Vigour, between both races of born beings, Agni, Thou farest as an envoy, having harnessed, Sublime One! thy strong-muscled radiant stallions.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I laud the ruddy steeds who pour down blessing, dropping oil, fleetest through the thoualit of Order. Yoking red horses to and fro thou goest between you Deities and mortal races.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Aryaman, Mitra, Varuna, and Indra with Visnu, of the Gods, Maruts and Asvins- These, Agni, with good car and steeds, bring hither, most bountiful, to folk with fair oblations.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, be this our sacrifice eternal, with brave friends, rich in kine and sheep and horses, Rich, Asura! in sacred food and children, in full assembly, wealth broad-based and during.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The man who, sweating, brings for thee the fuel, and makes his head to ache, thy faithful servant,- Agni, to him be a self-strong Protector guard him from all who seek to do him mischief.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who brings thee food, though thou hast food in plenty, welcomes his cheerful guest and speeds him onward, Who kindles thee devoutly in his dwelling to him be wealth secure and freely giving.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whoso sings praise to thee at eve or morning, and, with oblation, doth the thing thou lovest,- In his own home, even as a gold-girt courser, rescue him from distress, the bounteous giver.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whoso brings gifts to thee Immortal, Agni, and doth thee service with uplifted ladle,- Let him not, sorely toiling, lose his riches; let not the sinner's wickedness enclose him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whose well-wrought worship thou acceptest, Agni, thou God a mortal's gift, thou liberal Giver,- Dear be his sacrifice to thee, Most Youthful! and may we strengthen him when he adores thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May he who knows distinguish sense and folly of men, like straight and crooked backs of horses. Lead us, O God, to wealth and noble offspring: keep penury afar and grant us plenty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This Sage the Sages, ne'er deceived, commanded, setting him down in dwellings of the living. Hence mayst thou, friendly God, with rapid footsteps behold the Gods, wonderful, fair to look on.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Good guidance hast thou for the priest, O Agni, who, Youngest God! with outpoured Soma serves thee. Ruler of men, thou joyous God, bring treasure splendid and plentiful to aid the toiler.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now all that we, thy faithful servants, Agni, have done with feet, with hands, and with our bodies, The wise, with toil, the holy rite have guided, as those who frame a car with manual cunning.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May we, seven sages first in rank, engender, from Dawn the Mother, men to be ordainers. May we, Angirases, be sons of Heaven, and, radiant, burst the wealth-containing mountain.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As in the days of old our ancient Fathers, speeding the work of holy worship, Agni, Sought pure light and devotion, singing praises; they cleft the ground and made red Dawns apparent.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Gods, doing holy acts, devout, resplendent, smelting like ore their human generations. Enkindling Agni and exalting Indra, they came encompassing the stall of cattle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Strong One! he marked them-and the Gods before them-like herds of cattle in a foodful pasture. There they moaned forth their strong desire for mortals, to aid the True, the nearest One, the Living.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We have worked for thee, we have laboured nobly-bright Dawns have shed their light upon our worship- Adding a beauty to the perfect Agni, and the God's beauteous eye that shines for ever.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, Disposer, we have sung these praises to thee the Wise: do thou accept them gladly. Blaze up on high and ever make us richer. Give us great wealth, O thou whose boons are many.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WIN, to assist you, Rudra, Lord of worship, Priest of both worlds, effectual Sacrificer, Agni, invested with his golden colours, before the thunder strike and lay you senseless.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This shrine have we made ready for thy coming, as the fond dame attires her for her husband. Performer of good work, sit down before us, invested while these flames incline to meet thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: A hymn, O Priest, to him who hears, the gentle, to him who looks on men, exceeding gracious, A song of praise sing to the God Immortal, whom the stone, presser of the sweet juice, worships.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Even as true knower of the Law, O Agni, to this our solemn rite he thou attentive. When shall thy songs of festival be sung thee? When is thy friendship shown within our dwelling?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Why this complaint to Varuna, O Agni? And why to Heaven? for what is our transgression? How wilt thou speak to Earth and bounteous Mitra? What wilt thou say to Aryaman and Bhaga?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What, when thou blazest on the lesser altars, what to the mighty Wind who comes to bless us, True, circumambient? what to Earth, O Agni, what wilt thou say to man-destroying Rudra?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: How to great Pusan who promotes our welfare,- to honoured Rudra what, who gives oblations? What sin of ours to the far-striding Visnu, what, Agni, wilt thou tell the Lofty Arrow.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What wilt thou tell the truthful band of Maruts, how answer the great Sun when thou art questioned? Before the Free, before the Swift, defend us: fulfil heaven's work, all-knowing Jatavedas.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I crave the cow's true gift arranged by Order: though raw, she hath the sweet ripe juice, O Agni. Though she is black of hue with milk she teemeth, nutritious, brightly shining, all-sustaining.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni the Bull, the manly, hath been sprinkled with oil upon his back, by Law eternal. He who gives vital power goes on unswerving. Prsni the Bull hath milked the pure white udder.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: By Law the Angirases cleft the rock asunder, and sang their hymns together with the cattle. Bringing great bliss the men encompassed Morning: light was apparent at the birth of Agni.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: By Law the Immortal Goddesses the Waters, with meath-rich waves, O Agni, and uninjured, Like a strong courser lauded in his running, sped to flow onward swiftly and for ever.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Go never to the feast of one who harms us, the treacherous neighbour or. unworthy kinsman. Punish us not for a false brother's trespass. Let us riot feel the might of friend or foeman.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Agni, keep us safe with thy protection, loving us, honoured God! and ever guarding. Beat thou away, destroy severe affliction slay e'en the demon when he waxes mighty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Through these our songs of praise be gracious, Agni; moved by ourprayers, O Hero, touch our viands. Accept, O Angiras, these our devotions, and let the praise which Gods desire address thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To thee who knowest, Agni, thou Disposer, all these wise secret speeches have I uttered, Sung to thee, Sage, the charming words of wisdom, to thee, O Singer, with. my thoughts and Praises.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: PUT forth like a wide-spreading net thy vigour; go like a mighty King with his attendants. Thou, following thy swift net, shootest arrows: transfix the fiends with darts that burn most fiercely.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Forth go in rapid flight thy whirling weapons: follow them closely, glowing in thy fury. Spread with thy tongue the winged flames, O Agni; unfettered, cast thy firebrands all around thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Send thy spies forward, fleetest in thy motion; be, ne'er deceived, the guardian of this people From him who, near or far, is bent on evil, and let no trouble sent from thee o'ercome us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Rise up, O Agni, spread thee out before us: burn down our foes, thou who hast sharpened arrows. Him, blazing Agni! who hath worked us mischief, consume thou utterly like dried-up stubble.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Rise, Agni, drive off those who fight against us: make manifest thine own celestial vigour. Slacken the strong bows of the demon driven: destroy our foemen whether kin or stranger.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Most Youthful God, he knoweth well thy favour who gave an impulse to this high devotion. All fair days and magnificence of riches hast thou beamed forth upon the good man's portals.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Blest, Agni, be the man, the liberal giver, who with his lauds and regular oblation Is fain to please thee for his life and dwelling. May all his days be bright: be this his longing.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I praise thy gracious favour: sing in answer. May this my song sing like a loved one with thee. Lords of good steeds and cars may we adorn thee, and day by day vouchsafe thou us dominion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Here of free choice let each one serve thee richly, resplendent day by day at eve and morning. So may we honour thee, content and joyous, passing beyond the glories of the people.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whoso with good steeds and fine gold, O Agni, comes nigh thee on a car laden with treasure, His Friend art thou, yea, thou art his Protector whose joy it is to entertain thee duly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Through words and kinship I destroy the mighty: this power I have from Gotama my father. Mark thou this speech of ours, O thou Most Youthful, Friend of the House, exceeding wise, Invoker.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Knowing no slumber, speedy and propitious, alert and ever friendly, most unwearied, May thy protecting powers, unerring Agni, taking their places here, combined, preserve us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thy guardian rays, O Agni, when they saw him, preserved blind Mamateya from affliction. Lord of all riches, he preserved the pious: the fees who fain would harm them did no mischief
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Aided by thee with thee may we be wealthy, may we gain strength with thee to guide us onward. Fulfil the words of both, O Ever Truthful: straightway do this, thou God whom power emboldens.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Agni, with this fuel will we serve thee; accept the laud we sing to thee with favour Destroy the cursing Raksasas: preserve us, O rich in friends, from guile and scorn and slander.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: How shall we give with one accord oblation to Agni, to Vaisvanara the Bounteous? Great light, with full high growth hath he uplifted, and, as a pillar bears the roof, sustains it.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Reproach not him who, God and self reliant, vouchsafed this bounty unto me a mortal,- Deathless, discerner, wise, to me the simple, Vaisvanara most manly, youthful Aini.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sharp-pointed, powerful, strong, of boundless vigour, Agni who knows the lofty hymn, kept secret As the lost milch-cow's track, the doubly Mighty,-he hath declared to me this hidden knowledge.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May he with sharpened teeth, the Bounteous Giver, Agni, consume with flame most fiercely glowing. Those who regard not Varuna's commandments and the dear steadfast laws of sapient Mitra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like youthful women without brothers, straying, like dames who hate their lords, of evil conduct, They who are full of sin, untrue, unfaithful, they have engendered this abysmal station.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To me, weak, innocent, thou, luminous Agni, bast boldly given as 'twere a heavy burthen, This Prstha hymn, profound and strong and mighty, of seven elements, and with offered dainties.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So may our song that purifies, through wisdom reach in a moment him the Universal, Established on the height, on earth's best .station, above the beauteous grassy skin of Prsni.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Of this my speech what shall I utter further? They indicate the milk stored up in secret When they have thrown as 'twere the cows' stalls open. The Bird protects earths' best and well-loved station.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This is the Great Ones' mighty apparition which from of old the radiant Cow hath followed. This, shining brightly in the place of Order, swift, hasting on in secret, she discovered.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He then who shone together with his Parents remembered Prsni's fair and secret treasure, Which, in the Mother Cow's most lofty station, the Bull's tongue, of the flame bent forward, tasted.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With reverence I declare the Law, O Agni; what is, comes by thine order, Jatavedas. Of this, whate'er it be, thou art the Sovran, yea, all the wealth that is in earth or heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What is our wealth therefrom, and what our treasure? Tell us O Jatavedas, for thou knowest, What is our best course in this secret passage: we, unreproached, have reached a t)lace far distant.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What is the limit, what the rules, the guerdon? Like fleet-foot coursers speed we to the contest. When will the Goddesses, the Immortal's Spouses, the Dawns, spread over us the Sun-God's splendour?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Unsatisfied, with speech devoid of vigour, scanty and frivolous and inconclusive, Wherefore do they address thee here, O Agni? Let these who have no weapons suffer sorrow.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The majesty of him the Good, the Mighty, aflame, hath shone for glory in the dwelling. He, clothed in light, hath shone most fair to look on, wealthy in boons, as a home shines with riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: PRIEST of our rite, stand up erect, O Agni, in the Gods' service best of sacrificers, For over every thought thou art the Ruler: thou furtherest e'en the wisdom of the pious.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He was set down mid men as Priest unerring, Agni, wise, welcome in our holy synods. Like Savitar he hath lifted up his splendour, and like a builder raised his smoke to heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The glowing ladle, filled with oil, is lifted; choosing Gods' service to the right he circles. Eager he rises like the new-wrought pillar which, firmly set and fixed, anoints the victims.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When sacred grass is strewn and Agni kindled, the Adhvaryu rises to, his task rejoicing. Agni the Priest, like one who tends the cattle, goes three times round, as from of old he wills it.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni himself, the Priest, with measured motion, goes round, with sweet speech, cheerful, true to Order. His fulgent flames run forth like vigorous horses; all creatures are affrighted when he blazes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Beautiful and auspicious is thine aspect, O lovely Agni, terrible when spreading. Thy splendours are not covered by the darkness: detraction leaves no stain upon thy body.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Naught hindered his production, Bounteous Giver: his Mother and his Sire were free to send him. Then as Friend benevolent, refulgent, Agni shone forth in human habitations.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He, Agni, whom the twice-five sisters, dwelling together, in the homes of men engendered, Bright like a spear's tooth, wakened in the morning, with powerful mouth and like an axe well-sharpened.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These thy Bay Coursers, Agni, dropping fatness, ruddy vigorous, speeding straightly forward, And red steeds, wonderful, of mighty muscle, are to this service of the Gods invited:
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These brightly-shining games of thine, O Agni, that move for ever restless, allsubduing, Like falcons hasting eagerly to the quarry, roar loudly like the army of the Maruts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To thee, O flaming God, hath prayer been offered. Let the priest laud thee: give to him who worships. Men have established Agni as Invoker, fain to adore the glory of the living.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: HERE by ordainers was this God appointed first Invoker, best at worship, to be praised at rites: Whom Apnavana, and the Bhrgus caused to shine bright-coloured in the wood, spreading from home to home.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When shall thy glory as a God, Agni, be suddenly shown forth. For mortal men have held thee fast, adorable in all their homes,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Seeing thee faithful to the Law, most sapient, like the starry heaven, Illumining with cheerful ray each solemn rite in every house.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Vivasvan's envoy living men have taken as their ensign, swift, The ruler over all mankind, moving like Bhrgu in each home.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him the intelligent have they placed duly as Invoking Priest, Welcome, with sanctifying flame, best worshipper, with sevenfold might;
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In his Eternal Mothers, in the wood, concealed and unapproached, Kept secret though his flames are bright seeking on all sides, quickly found.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: That as food spreads forth in this earthly udder, Gods may rejoice them in the home of Order, Great Agni, served with reverence and oblation, flies ever to the sacrifice, the Faithful.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bird of each rite, skilled in an envoy's duties, knowing both worlds and that which lies between them, Thou goest from of old a willing Herald, knowing full well heaven's innermost recesses.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bright God, thy path is black: light is before thee: thy moving splendour is the chief of wonders. When she, yet unimpregnate, hath conceived thee, even when newly born thou art an envoy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yet newly born, his vigour is apparent when the wind blows upon his fiery splendour, His sharpened tongue he layeth on the brushwood, and with his teeth e'en solid food consumeth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When he hath borne off food with swift flame swiftly, strong Agni makes himself a speedy envoy, Follows the rustling of the wind, consuming, and courser-like, speeds, drives the swift horse onward.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: YOUR envoy who possesses all, Immortal, bearer of your gifts, Best worshipper, I woo with song.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He, Mighty, knows the gift of wealth, he knows the deep recess of heaven: He shall bring hitherward the Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He knows, a God himself, to guide Gods to the righteous in his home: He gives e'en treasures that we love.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He is the Herald: well-informed, he doth his errand to and fro, Knowing the deep recess of heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May we be they who gratify Agni with sacrificial gifts, Who cherish and enkindle him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Illustrious for wealth are they, and hero deeds, victorious, Who have served Agni reverently.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So unto us, day after day, may riches craved by many come, And power and might spring up for us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: That holy Singer in his strength shoots forth his arrows swifter than The swift shafts of the tribes of men.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: AGNI, show favour: great art thou who to this pious man art come, To seat thee on the sacred grass.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May he the Immortal, Helper, bard to be deceived among mankind, Become the messenger of all.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Around the altar is he led, welcome Chief Priest at solemn rites, Or as the Potar sits him down.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni in fire at sacrifice, and in the house as Lord thereof, And as a Brahman takes his seat.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou comest as the guide of folk who celebrate a sacrifice, And to oblations brought by men.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou servest as his messenger whose sacrifice thou lovest well, To bear the mortal's gifts to heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Accept our solemn rite; be pleased, Angiras, with our sacrifice: Give ear and listen to our call.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May thine inviolable car, wherewith thou guardest those who give, Come near to us from every side.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This day with praises, Agni, we bring thee that which thou lovest. Right judgment, like a horse, with our devotions.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For thou hast ever been the Car-driver, Agni, of noble Strength, lofty sacrifice, and rightful judgment.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Through these our praises come thou to meet us, bright as the sunlight, O Agni, well disposed, with all thine aspects.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now may we serve thee singing these lauds this day to thee, Agni. Loud as the voice of Heaven thy blasts are roaring.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: just at this time of the day and the night thy look is the sweetest . It shineth near us even as gold for glory.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Spotless thy body, brilliant as gold, like clarified butter: This gleams like gold on thee, O Self. dependent.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: All hate and mischief, yea, if committed, Agni, thou turnest, Holy One, from the man who rightly worships.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, with you Gods, prosperous be our friendships and kinships. Be this our bond here by this place, thine altar.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THY blessed majesty, victorious Agni, shines brightly in the neighbourhood of Surya. Splendid to see, it shows even at nighttime, and food is fair to look on in thy beauty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, disclose his thought for him who singeth, the well, Strong God! while thou art praised with fervour. Vouchsafe to us that powerful hymn, O Mighty, which, Radiant One! with all the Gods thou lovest.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: From thee, O Agni, springs poetic wisdom, from thee come thoughts and hymns of praise that prosper; From thee flows wealth, with heroes to adorn it, to the true-hearted man who gives oblation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: From thee the hero springs who wins the booty, bringer of help, mighty, of real courage. From thee comes wealth, sent by the Gods, bliss-giving; Agni, from thee the fleet impetuous charger.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Immortal Agni, thee whose voice is pleasant, as first in rank, as God, religious mortals Invite with hymns; thee who removest hatred, Friend of the Home, the household's Lord, unerring.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Far from us thou removest want and sorrow, far from us all ill-will when thou protectest. Son of Strength, Agni, blest is he at evening, whom thou as God attendest for his welfare.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WHOSO enkindles thee, with lifted ladle, and thrice this day offiers thee food, O Agni, May he excel, triumphant through thy splendours, wise through thy mental power, O Jatavedas.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whoso with toil and trouble brings thee fuel, serving the majesty of mighty Agni, He, kindling thee at evening and at morning, prospers, and comes to wealth, and slays his foemen.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni is Master of sublime dominion, Agni is Lord of strength and lofty riches. Straightway the self-reliant God, Most Youthful, gives treasures to the mortal who adores him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Most Youthful God, whatever sin, through folly, we here, as human beings, have committed, In sight of Aditi make thou us sinless remit, entirely, Agni, our offences.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Even in the presence of great sin, O Agni, free us from prison of the Gods or mortals. Never may we who are thy friends be injured: grant health and strength unto our seed and offspring.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Even as ye here, Gods Excellent and Holy, have loosed the cow that by the foot was tethered, So also set us free from this affliction long let our life, O Agni, be extended.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: AGNI hath looked, benevolently-minded, on the wealth-giving spring of radiant Mornings. Come, Asvins, to the dwelling of the pious: Surya the God is rising with his splendour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Savitar, God, hath spread on high his lustre, waving his flag like a spoil-seeking hero. Their stablished way go Varuna and Mitra, what time they make the Sun ascend the heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him whom they made to drive away the darkness, Lords of sure mansions, constant to their object, Him who beholds the universe, the Sun-God, seven strong and youthful Coursers carry onward.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Spreading thy web with mightiest Steeds thou comest, rending apart, thou God, the black-hued mantle. The rays of Surya tremulously shining sink, like a hide, the darkness in the waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: How is it that, unbound and not supported, he falleth not although directed downward? By what self power moves he? Who hath seen it? He guards the vault of heaven, a close-set pillar.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THE God hath looked, even Agni Jatavedas, to meet the Dawns refulgent in their glories. Come on your chariot, ye who travel widely, come to this sacrifice of ours, Nasatyas.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Producing light for all the world of creatures, God Savitar hath raised aloft his banner. Making his presence known by sunbeams, Surya hath filled the firmament and earth and heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Red Dawn.is come, riding with brightness onward, distinguished by her beams, gay-hued and mighty. Dawn on her nobly-harnessed car, the Goddess, awaking men to happiness, approacheth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May those most powerful steeds and chariot bring you, O Asvins, hither at the break of morning. Here for your draught of meath are Soma juices: at this our sacrifice rejoice, ye Mighty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: How is it that, unbound and unsupported, he falleth not although directed downward? By what self-power moves he? Who hath seen it? He guards the vault of heaven, a close-set pillar?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: AGNI the Herald, like a horse, is led forth at our solemn rite, God among Gods adorable.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Three times unto our solemn rite comes Agni like a charioteer, Bearing the viands to the Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Round the oblations hath he paced, Agni the Wise, the Lord of Strength, Giving the offerer precious boons.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who is kindled eastward for Srnjaya, Devavata's son, Resplendent, tamer of the foe.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So mighty be the Agni whom the mortal hero shall command, With sharpened teeth and bountiful.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Day after day they dress him, as they clean a horse who wins the prize. Dress the red Scion of the Sky.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When Sahadeva's princely son with two bay horses thought of me, Summoned by him I drew not back.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And truly those two noble bays I straightway took when offered me, From Sahadeva's princely son.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Long, O ye Asvins, may he live, your care, ye Gods, the princely son. Of Sahadeva, Somaka.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Cause him the youthful prince, the son of Sahadeva, to enjoy Long life, O Asvins, O ye Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: IMPETUOUS, true, let Maghavan come hither, and let his Tawny Coursers speed to reach us. For him have we pressed juice exceeding potent: here, praised with song, let him effect his visit.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Unyoke, as at thy journey's end, O Hero, to gladden thee today at this libation. Like Usana, the priest a laud shall utter, a hymn to thee, the Lord Divine, who markest.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When the Bull, quaffing, praises our libation, as a sage paying holy rites in secret, Seven singers here from heaven hath he begotten, who e'en by day have wrought their works while singing.
