verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When heaven's fair light by hymns was made apparent (they made great splendour shine at break of morning), He with his succour, best of Heroes, scattered the blinding darkness so that men saw clearly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, Impetuous One, hath waxed immensely: he with his vastness hath filled earth and heaven. E'en beyond this his majesty extendeth who hath exceeded all the worlds in greatness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sakra who knoweth well all human actions hath with his eager Friends let loose the waters. They with their songs cleft e'en the mountain open and willingly disclosed the stall of cattle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He smote away the floods' obstructer, Vrtra; Earth, conscious, lent her aid to speed thy thunder. Thou sentest forth the waters of the ocean, as Lord through power and might, O daring Hero.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When, Much-invoked! the water's rock thou cleftest, Sarama showed herself and went before thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come, Maghavan, Friend of Man, to aid the singer imploring thee in battle for the sunlight. Speed him with help in his inspired invokings: down sink the sorcerer, the prayerless Dasyu.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come to our home resolved to slay the Dasyu: Kutsa longed eagerly to win thy friendship. Alike in form ye both sate in his dwelling the faithful Lady was in doubt between you.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou comest, fain to succour him, with Kutsa,-a goad that masters both the Wind-God's horses, That, holding the brown steeds like spoil for capture, the sage may on the final day be present.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For Kutsa, with thy thousand, thou at day-break didst hurl down greedy Susna, foe of harvest. Quickly with Kutsa's friend destroy the Dasyus, and roll the chariot-wheel of Sarya near us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou to the son of Vidathin, Rjisvan, gavest up mighty Mrgaya and Pipru. Thou smotest down the swarthy fifty thousand, and rentest forts as age consumes a garment.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What time thou settest near the Sun thy body, thy form, Immortal One, is seen expanding: Thou a wild elephant with might invested. like a dread lion as thou wieldest weapons.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wishes for wealth have gone to Indra, longing for him in war for light and at libation, Eager for glory, labouring with praisesongs: he is like home, like sweet and fair nutrition.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Call we for you that Indra, prompt to listen, him who hath done so much for men's advantage; Who, Lord of envied bounty, to a singer like me brings quickly booty worth the capture.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When the sharp-pointed arrow, O thou Hero, flieth mid any conflict of the people, When, Faithful One, the dread encounter cometh, then be thou the Protector of our body.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Further the holy thoughts of Vamadeva be thou a guileless Friend in fight for booty. We come to thee whose providence protects us: wide be thy sway for ever for thy singer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Indra, with these men who love thee truly, free givers, Maghavan, in every battle, May we rejoice through many autumns, quelling our foes, as days subdue the nights with splendour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now, as the Bhrgus wrought a car, for Indra the Strong, the Mighty, we our prayer have fashioned, That he may, ne'er withdraw from us his friendship, but be our bodies' guard and strong defender.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now, Indra! lauded, glorified with praises, let power swell. high like rivers for the singer. For thee a new hymn, Lord of Bays, is fashioned. May we, car-borne, through song be victors ever.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: GREAT art thou, Indra; yea, the earth, with gladness, and heaven confess to thee thine high dominion. Thou in thy vigour having slaughtered Vrtra didst free the floods arrested by the Dragon.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Heaven trembled at the birth of thine effulgence; Earth trembled at the fear of thy displeasure. The stedfast mountains shook in agitation . the waters flowed, and desert spots were flooded.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hurling his bolt with might he cleft the mountain, while, putting forth his strength, he showed his vigour. He slaughtered Vrtra with his bolt, exulting, and, their lord slain, forth flowed the waters swiftly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thy Father Dyaus esteemed himself a hero: most noble was the work of Indra's Maker, His who begat the strong bolt's Lord who roareth, immovable like earth from her foundation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who alone o'erthrows the world of creatures, Indra the peoples' King, invoked of many- Verily all rejoice in him, extolling the boons which Maghavan the God hath sent them.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: All Soma juices are his own for ever, most gladdening draughts are ever his, the Mighty, Thou ever wast the Treasure-Lord of treasures: Indra, thou lettest all folk share thy bounty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Moreover, when thou first wast born, O Indra, thou struckest terror into all the people. Thou, Maghavan, rentest with thy bolt the Dragon who lay against the waterfloods of heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The ever-slaying, bold and furious Indra, the bright bolt's Lord, infinite, strong and mighty, Who slayeth Vrtra and acquireth booty, giver of blessings, Maghavan the bounteous:
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Alone renowned as Maghavan in battles, he frighteneth away assembled armies. He bringeth us the booty that he winneth may we, well-loved, continue in his friendship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Renowned is he when conquering and when slaying: 'fis he who winneth cattle in the combat. When Indra hardeneth his indignation all that is fixed and all that moveth fear him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra hath won all kine, all gold, all horses, Maghavan, he who breaketh forts in pieces; Most manly with these men of his who help him, dealing out wealth and gathering the treasure.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What is the care of Indra for his Mother, what cares he for the Father who begat him? His care is that which speeds his might in conflicts, like wind borne onward by the clouds that thunder.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Maghavan makes the settled man unsettled: he scatters dust that he hath swept together, Breaking in pieces like Heaven armed with lightning: Maghavan shall enrich the man who lauds h;m.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He urged the chariot-wheel of Surya forward: Etasa, speeding on his way, he rested. Him the black undulating cloud bedeweth, in this mid-air's depth, at the base of darkness,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As in the night the sacrificing priest.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Eager for booty, craving strength and horses, we-singers stir Indra, the strong, for friendship, Who gives the wives we seek, whose succour fails not, to hasten, like a pitcher to the fountain.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Be thou our guardian, show thyself our kinsman, watching and blessing those who pour the Soma; As Friend, as Sire, most fatherly of fathers giving the suppliant vital strength and freedom.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Be helping Friend of those who seek thy friendship . give life, when lauded, Indra, to the singer. For, Indra, we the priests have paid thee worship, exalting thee with these our sacrifices.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Alone, when Indra Maghavan is lauded, he slayeth many ne'er-resisted Vrtras. Him in whose keeping is the well-loved singer never do Gods or mortals stay or hinder.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: E’en so let Maghavan, the loud-voiced Indra, give us true blessings, foeless, men's upholder. King of all creatures, give us glory amply, exalted glory due to him who lauds thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now, Indra! lauded, glorified with praises, let power swell high like rivers for the singer. For thee a new hymn, Lord of Bays! is fashioned. May we, car-borne, through song be victors ever.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THIS is the ancient and accepted pathway by which all Gods have come into existence. Hereby could one be born though waxen mighty. Let him not, otherwise, destroy his Mother.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Not this way go I forth: hard is the passage. Forth from the side obliquely will I issue. Much that is yet undone must I accomplish; one must I combat and the other question.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He bent his eye upon the dying Mother: My word I now withdraw. That way I follow. In Tvastar's dwelling India drank the Soma, a hundredworth of juice pressed from the mortar.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What strange act shall he do, he whom his Mother bore for a thousand months and many autumns? No peer hath he among those born already, nor among those who shall be born hereafter.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Deeming him a reproach, his mother hid him, Indra, endowed with all heroic valour. Then up he sprang himself, assumed his vesture, and filled, as soon as born, the earth and heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With lively motion onward flow these waters, the Holy Ones, shouting, as 'twere, together. Ask them to. tell thee what the floods are saying, what girdling rock the waters burst asunder.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Are they addressing him with words of welcome? Will the floods take on them the shame of Indra? With his great thunderbolt my Son hath slaughtered Vrtra, and set these rivers free to wander.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I cast thee from me, mine,-thy youthful mother: thee, mine own offspring, Kusava hath swallowed. To him, mine infant, were the waters gracious. Indra, my Son, rose up in conquering vigour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou art mine own, O Maghavan, whom Vyamsa struck to the ground and smote thy jaws in pieces. But, smitten through, the mastery thou wonnest, and with thy bolt the Dasa's head thou crushedst.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Heifer hath brought forth the Strong, the Mighty, the unconquerable Bull, the furious Indra. The Mother left her unlicked Calf to wander, seeking himself, the path that he would follow.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Then to her mighty Child the Mother turned her, saying, My son, these Deities forsake thee. Then Indra said, about to slaughter Vrtra, O my friend Vrtra, stride full boldly forward.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who was he then who made thy Mother widow? Who sought to stay thee lying still or moving? What God, when by the foot thy Sire thou tookest and slewest, was at hand to give thee comfort?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In deep distress I cooked a dog's intestines. Among the Gods I found not one to comfort. My consort I beheld in degradation. The Falcon then brought me the pleasant Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THEE, verily, O Thunder-wielding Indra, all the Gods here, the Helpers swift to listen, And both the worlds elected, thee the Mighty, High, waxen strong, alone to slaughter Vrtra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Gods, as worn witheld, relaxed their efforts: thou, Indra, born of truth, wast Sovran Ruler. Thou slewest Ahi who besieged the waters, and duggest out their all-supporting channels.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The insatiate one, extended, hard to waken, who slumbered in perpetual sleep, O Indra, The Dragon stretched against the seven prone rivers, where no joint was, thou rentest with thy thunder.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra with might shook earth and her foundation as the wind stirs the water with its fury. Striving, with strength he burst the firm asunder, and tore away the summits of the mountains.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They ran to thee as mothers to their offspring: the clouds, like chariots, hastened forth together. Thou didst refresh the streams and force the billows: thou, Indra, settest free obstructed rivers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou for the sake of Vayya and Turviti didst stay the great stream, flowing, allsustaining: Yea, at their prayer didst check the rushing river and make the floods easy to cross, O Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He let the young Maids skilled in Law, unwedded, like fountains, bubbling, flow forth streaming onward. He inundated thirsty plains and deserts, and milked the dry Cows of the mighty master.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Through many a morn and many a lovely autumn, having slain Vrtra, lie set free the rivers. Indra hath set at liberty to wander on earth the streams encompassed pressed together.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Lord of Bay Steeds, thou broughtest from the ant-hill the unwedded damsel's son whom ants were eating. The blind saw clearly, as he grasped the serpent, rose, brake the jar: his joints again united.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To the wise man, O Sage and Sovran Ruler, the man who knoweth all thine ancient exploits. Hath told these deeds of might as thou hast wrought them, great acts, spontaneous, and to man's advantage.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now, Indra! lauded, glorified with praises, let powers swell high, like rivers, for the singer. For thee a new hymn, Lord of Bays! is fashioned. May we, car-borne, through song be victors ever.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: FROM near or far away may mighty Indra giver of succour, come for our protection Lord of men, armed with thunder, with the Strongest, slaying his foes in conflict, in the battles.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Indra come to us with Tawny Coursers, inclined to us, to favour and enrich us. May Maghavan, loud-voiced and wielding thunder, stand by us at this sacrifice, in combat.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, honouring this our sacrifice, O Indra, shalt give us strength and fill us full of courage. To win the booty, Thunder-armed! like hunters may we with thee subdue in fight our foemen.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Loving us well, benevolent, close beside us, drink, Godlike Indra, of the well pressed Soma. Drink of the meath we offer, and delight thee with food that cometh from the mountain ridges.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him who is sung aloud by recent sages, like a ripe-fruited tree, a scythe-armed victor,- I, like a bridegroom thinking of his consort, call hither Indra, him invoked of many;
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him who in native strength is like a mountain, the lofty Indra born or old for conquest, Terrific wielder of the ancient thunder. filled full with splendour as a jar with water.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whom from of old there is not one to hinder, none to curtail the riches of his bounty. Pouring forth freely, O thou Strong and Mighty, vouchsafe us riches, God invoked of many!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Of wealth and homes of men thou art the ruler, and opener of the stable of the cattle. Helper of men, winner of spoil in combats, thou leadest to an ample heap of riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: By what great might is he renowned as strongest, wherewith the Lofty One stirs up wild battles? Best soother of the worshipper's great sorrow, he gives possessions to the man who lauds him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Slay us not; bring, bestow onus the ample gift which thou hast to give to him who offers. At this new gift, with this laud sung before thee, extolling thee, we, Indra, will declare it.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now, Indra! lauded, glorified with praises, let power swell high, like rivers, for the singer. A new hymn, Lord of Bays! for thee is fashioned. May we, car-born, through song be victors ever.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: MAY Indra come to us for our protection; here be the Hero, praised, our feast-companion. May he whose powers are many, waxen mighty, cherish, like Dyaus, his own supreme dominion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Here magnify his great heroic exploits, most glorious One, enriching men with bounties, Whose will is like a Sovran in assembly, who rules the people, Conqueror, all-surpassing.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hither let Indra come from earth or heaven, hither with speech from firmament or ocean; With Maruts, from the realm of light to aid us, or from a distance, from the seat of Order.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: That Indra will we laud in our assemblies, him who is Lord of great and lasting riches, Victor with Vayu where the herds are gathered, who leads with boldness on to higher fortune.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May the Priest, Lord of many blessings, striving,-who fixing reverence on reverence, giving Vent to his voice, inciteth men to worship with lauds bring Indra hither to our dwellings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When sitting pondering in deep devotion in Ausija's abode they ply the press-stone, May he whose wrath is fierce, the mighty bearer, come as the house-lord's priest within our chambers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Surely the power of Bharvara the mighty for ever helpeth to support the singer; That which in Ausija's abode lies hidden, to come forth for delight and for devotion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When he unbars the spaces of the mountains, and quickens with his floods the water-torrents, He finds in lair the buffalo and wild-ox when the wise lead him on to vigorous exploit.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Auspicious are thy hands, thine arms well fashioned which proffer bounty, Indra, to thy praiser. What sloth is this? Why dost thou not rejoice thee? Why dost thou not delight thyself with giving?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So Indra is the truthful Lord of treasure. Freedom he gave to man by slaying Vrtra. Much-lauded! help us with thy power to riches: may I be sharer of thy Godlike favour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now, Indra! lauded, glorified with praises, let power swell high, like rivers, for,the singer. For thee a new hymn, Lord of Bays! is fashioned. May we, care-borne, through song be victors ever.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THAT gift of ours which Indra loves and welcomes, even that he makes for us, the Great and Strong One. He who comes wielding in his might the thunder, Maghavan, gives prayer, praise, and laud, and Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bull, hurler of the four-edged rain-producer with both his arms, strong, mighty, most heroic; Wearing as wool Parusni for adornment, whose joints for sake of friendship he hath covered.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: God who of all the Gods was born divinest, endowed with ample strength and mighty powers, And bearing in his arms the yearning thunder, with violent rush caused heaven and earth to tremble.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Before the High God, at his birth, heaven trembled, earth, many floods and all the precipices. The Strong One bringeth nigh the Bull's two Parents: loud sing the winds, like men, in air's mid-region.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These are thy great deeds, Indra, thine, the Mighty, deeds to be told aloud at all libations, That thou, O Hero, bold and boldly daring, didst with thy bolt, by strength, destroy the Dragon.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: True are all these thy deeds, O Most Heroic. The Milch-kine issued from the streaming udder. In fear of thee, O thou of manly spirit, the rivers swiftly set themselves in motion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With joy, O Indra, Lord of Tawny Coursers, the Sisters then, these Goddesses, extolled thee, When thou didst give the prisoned ones their freedom to wander at their will in long succession.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Pressed is the gladdening stalk as 'twere a river: so let the rite, the toiler's power, attract thee To us-ward, of the Bright One, as the courser strains his. exceedingly strong leather bridle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ever by us perform thy most heroic, thine highest, best victorious deeds, O Victor. For us make Vrtras easy to be conquered: destroy the weapon of our mortal foeman.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Graciously listen to our prayer, O Indra, and strength of varied sort bestow thou on us. Send to us all intelligence arid wisdom O Maghavan, be he who gives us cattle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now, Indra! lauded, glorified with praises, let wealth swell high like rivers to the singer. For thee a new hymn, Lord of Bays, is fashioned. May we, car-borne, through song be victors ever.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: How, what priest's sacrifice hath he made mighty, rejoicing in the Soma and its fountain? Delighting in juice, eagerly drinking, the Lofty One hath waxed for splendid riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What hero hath been made his feast-companion? Who hath been partner in his loving-kindness? What know we of his wondrous acts? How often comes he to aid and speed the pious toiler?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: How heareth Indra offered invocation? How, hearing, marketh he the invoker's wishes? What are his ancient acts of bounty? Wherefore call they him One who filleth full the singer?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: How doth the priest who laboureth, ever longing, win for himself the wealth which he possesseth? May he, the God, mark well my truthful praises, having received the homage which he loveth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: How, and what bond of friendship with a mortal hath the God chosen as this morn is breaking? How, and what love hath he for those who love him, who have entwined in him their firm affection?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Is then thy friendship with thy friends most mighty? Thy brotherhood with us, -when may we tell it? The streams of milk move, as most wondrous sunlight, the beauty of the Lovely One for glory.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: About to stay the Indra-less destructive spirit he sharpens his keen arms to strike her. Whereby the Strong, although our debts' exactor, drives in the distant mornings that we know not.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Eternal Law hath varied food that strengthens; thought of eternal Law, removes transgressions. The praise-hymn of eternal Law, arousing, glowing, hath opened the deaf ears of the living.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Firm-seated are eternal Law's foundations in its fair form are many splendid beauties. By holy Law long lasting food they bring us; by holy Law have cows come to our worship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Fixing eternal Law he, too, upholds it swift moves the might of Law and wins the booty. To Law belong the vast deep Earth and Heaven: Milch-kine supreme, to Law their milk they render.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now, Indra! lauded,- glorified with praises, let power swell high like rivers to the singer. For thee a new hymn, Lord of Bays, is fashioned. May we, car-borne, through song be victors ever.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WHAT worthy praise will bring before us Indra, the Son of Strength, that he may grant us riches; For he the Hero, gives the singer treasures: he is the Lord who sends us gifts, ye people.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To be invoked and hymned in fight with Vrtra, that well-praised Indra gives us real bounties. That Maghavan brings comfort in the foray to the religious man who pours libations.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him, verily, the men invoke in combat; risking their lives they make him their protector, When heroes, foe to foe, give up their bodies, fighting, each side, for children and their offspring.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Strong God! the folk at need put forth their vigour, striving together in the whirl of battle. When warrior bands encounter one another some in the grapple quit themselves like Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hence many a one worships the might of Indra: hence let the brew succeed the meal-oblation. Hence let the Soma banish those who pour not: even hence I joy to pay the Strong One worship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra gives comfort to the man who truly presses, for him who longs for it, the Soma, Not disaffected, with devoted spirit this man he takes to be his friend in battles.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who this day for Indra presses Soma, prepares the brew and fries the grains of barley- Loving the hymns of that devoted servant, to him may Indra give heroic vigour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When the impetuous chief hath sought the conflict, and the lord looked upon the long-drawn battle, The matron calls to the Strong God whom pressers of Soma have encouraged into the dwelling.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He bid a small price for a thing of value: I was content, returning, still unpurchased. He heightened not his insufficient offer. Simple and clever, both milk out the udder.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who for ten milch-kine purchaseth from me this Indra who is mine? When he hath slain the Vrtras let the buyer give him back to me.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now, Indra! lauded, glorified with praises, let wealth swell high like rivers for the singer. For thee a new hymn, Lord of Bays, is fashioned. May we, car-borne, through song be victors ever.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WHAT friend of man, God-loving, hath delighted, yearning therefor, this day in Indra's friendship? Who with enkindled flame and flowing Soma laudeth him for his great protecting favour?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who hath with prayer bowed to the Soma-lover? What pious man endues the beams of morning? Who seeks bond, friendship, brotherhood with Indra? Who hath recourse unto the Sage for succour?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who claims to-day the Deities' protection, asks Aditi for light, or the Adityas? Of whose pressed stalk of Soma drink the Asvins, Indra, and Agni, well-inclined in spirit?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To him shall Agni Bharata give shelter: long shall he look upon the Sun up-rising, Who sayeth, Let us press the juice for Indra, man's Friend, the Hero manliest of heroes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him neither few men overcome, nor many to him shall Aditi give spacious shelter. Dear is the pious, the devout, to Indra dear is the zealous, dear the Soma-bringer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This Hero curbs the mighty for the zealous: the presser's brew Indra possesses solely: No brother, kin, or friend to him who pours not, destroyer of the dumb who would resist him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Not with the wealthy churl who pours no Soma doth Indra, Soma-drinker, bind alliance. He draws away his wealth and slays him naked, own Friend to him who offers, for oblation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Highest and lowest, men who stand between diem, going, returning, dwelling in contentment, Those who show forth their strength when urged to battle-these are the men who call for aid on Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I WAS aforetime Manu, I was Surya: I am the sage Kaksivan, holy singer. Kutsa the son of Arjuni I master. I am the sapient Usana behold me.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I have bestowed the earth upon the Arya, and rain upon the man who brings oblation. I guided forth the loudly-roaring waters, and the Gods moved according to my pleasure.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In the wild joy of Soma I demolished Sambara's forts, ninety-and-nine, together; And, utterly, the hundredth habitation, when helping Divodasa Atithigva.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Before all birds be ranked this Bird, O Maruts; supreme of falcons be this fleet-winged Falcon, Because, strong- pinioned, with no car to bear him, he brought to Manu the God loved oblation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When the Bird brought it, hence in rapid motion sent on the wide path fleet as thought he hurried. Swift he returned with sweetness of the Soma, and hence the Falcon hath acquired his glory.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bearing the stalk, the Falcon speeding onward, Bird bringing from afar the draught that gladdens, Friend of the Gods, brought, grasping fast, the Soma which be bad taken from yon loftiest heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Falcon took and brought the Soma, bearing thousand libations with him, yea, ten thousand. The Bold One left malignities behind him, wise, in wild joy of Soma, left the foolish.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I, As I lay within the womb, considered all generations of these Gods in order. A hundred iron fortresses confined me, but forth I flew with rapid speed a Falcon,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Not at his own free pleasure did he bear me: he conquered with his strength and manly courage. Straightway the Bold One left the fiends behind him and passed the winds as he grew yet more mighty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When with loud cry from heaven down sped the Falcon, thence hasting like the wind he bore the Bold One, Then, wildly raging in his mind, the archer Kṛiṣânu aimed and loosed the string to strike him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Falcon bore him from heaven's lofty summit as the swift car of Indra's Friend bore Bhujyu. Then downward hither fell a flying feather of the Bird hasting forward in his journey.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And now let Maghavan accept the beaker, white, filled with milk, filled with the shining liquid; The best of sweet meath which the priests have offered: that Indra to his joy may drink, the Hero, that he may take and drink it to his rapture.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The womb of the rain cloud. A hundred fortresses:cf 'Şambara's hundred ancient castles' (II, 14. 6.) Considered: or reviewed, in hope of finding a deliverer. The speaker is Agni, that is, the lightning which rends the cloud and brings down the sweet rain-the fleet Falcon who brings Soma from heaven. See Prof. Bloomfield, The Myth of Soma and the Eagle, Festgruss an Rudolf von Roth, 1893, pp 149-155. Of. Hymns of the Atharva-veda, VI. 48. 1.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Not at his own free pleasure: the falcon's mere will was not enough, says Soma; he had first to fight and conquer my keepers. The Bold One; Indra. See stanza 7 of the preceding hymn,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Bold One: meaning Soma. The construction of the first line is difficult. Krisdnu: one of the guards of the celestial Soma. See I. 155 2
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The allusion in the first line is to the rescue of Bhujyu, by the Asvins (see I. 112. 6), and we should therefore expect indravatoh, 'of Indra's two friends, instead of indravato. Feather: parnám, which became on earth the sacred Parpa or Palasa tree, the beautiful Butea Frondosa.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The metrical form and the ritual application indicate the comparatively recent addition of this stanza to the ancient hymn. The hymn has been discussed by Weber, Vedische Beiträge, pp. 4. ff.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: ALLIED with thee, in this thy friendship, Soma, Indra for man made waters flow together, Slew Ahi, and sent forth the Seven Rivers, and opened as it were obstructed fountains.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indu, with thee for his confederate, Indra swiftly with might pressed down the wheel of Surya. What rolled, all life's support, on heaven's high summit was separated from the great oppressor.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra smote down, Agni consumed, O Indu, the Dasyus ere the noontide in the conflict. Of those who gladly sought a hard-won dwelling he cast down many a thousand with his arrow.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Lower than all besides hast thou, O Indra, cast down the Dasyus, abject tribes of Dasas. Ye drave away, ye put to death the foemen, and took great vengeance with your murdering weapons.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So, of a truth, Indra and Soma, Heroes, ye burst the stable of the kine and horses, The stable which the bar or stone obstructed; and piercing through set free the habitations.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: COME, lauded, unto us with powers and succours, O Indra, with thy Tawny Steeds; exulting, Past even the foeman's manifold libations, glorified with our hymns, true Wealth-bestower.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Man's Friend, to this our sacrifice he cometh marking how he is called by Soma-pressers. Fearless, and conscious that his Steeds are noble, he joyeth with the Soma-pouring heroes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Make his cars hear, that he may show his vigour and may be joyful in the way he loveth. May mighty Indra pouring forth in bounty bestow on us good roads and perfect safety;
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who with succour comes to his implorer, the singer here who with his song invites him; He who himself sets to the pole swift Coursers, he who hath hundreds, thousands, Thunder-wielder.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Indra Maghavan, by thee protected may we be thine, princes and priests and singers, Sharing the riches sent from lofty heaven which yields much food, and all desire its bounty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O INDRA, Vrtra-slayer, none is better, mightier than thou: Verily there is none like thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like chariot-wheels these people all together follow after thee: Thou ever art renowned as Great.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Not even all the gathered Gods conquered thee, Indra, in the war, When thou didst lengthen days by night.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When for the sake of those oppressed, and Kutsa as he battled, Thou stolest away the Sun's car-wheel.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When, fighting singly, Indra. thou o'ercamest all the furious Gods, Thou slewest those who strove with thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When also for a mortal man, Indra, thou speddest forth the Sun, And holpest Etasa with might.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What? Vrtra-slayer, art not thou, Maghavan, fiercest in thy wrath? So hast thou quelled the demon too.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And this heroic deed of might thou, Indra, also hast achieved, That thou didst smite to death the Dame, Heaven's Daughter, meditating ill.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, Indra, Mighty One, didst crush Usas, though Daughter of the Sky. When lifting up herself in pride.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Then from her chariot Usas fled, affrighted, from her ruined car. When the strong God had shattered it.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So there this car of Usas lay, broken to pieces, in Vipas, And she herself fled far away.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, Indra, didst. with magic power resist the overflowing stream Who spread her waters o'er the land.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Valiantly didst thou seize and take the store which Susna had amassed, When thou didst crush his fortresses.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, Indra, also smotest down Kulitara's son Sambara, The Dasa, from the lofty hill.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Of Dasa Varcin's thou didst slay the hundred thousand and the five, Crushed like the fellies, of a car.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So Indra, Lord of Heroes, Powers, caused the unwedded damsel's son, The castaway, to share the lauds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So sapient Indra, Lord of Might, brought Turvaga and Yadu, those Who feared the flood, in safely o'er.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Arpa and Citraratha, both Aryas, thou, Indra, slewest swift, On yonder side of Sarayu,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, Vrtra-slayer, didst conduct those two forlorn, the blind, the lame. None may attain this bliss of thine.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For Divodasa, him who brought oblation, 1ndra overthrew A hundred fortresses of stone.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The thirty thousand Disas he with magic power and weapons sent To slumber, for Dabhiti's sake.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As such, O Vrtra-slayer, thou art general Lord of kine for all, Thou Shaker of all things that be.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, whatever deed of might thou hast this day to execute, None be there now to hinder it.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Watchful One, may Aryaman the God give thee all goodly things. May Risan, Bhaga, and the God Karulati give all things fair.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WITH what help will he come to us, wonderful, ever-waxing Friend; With what most mighty company?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What genuine and most liberal draught will spirit thee with juice to burst Open e'en strongly-guarded wealth?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Do thou who art Protector of us thy friends who praise thee With hundred aids approach us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like as a courser's circling wheel, so turn thee hitherward to us, Attracted by the hymns of men.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou seekest as it were thine own stations with swift descent of powers: I share thee even with the Sun.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What time thy courage and his wheels together, Indra, run their course With thee and with the Sun alike,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So even, Lord of Power and Might, the people call thee Maghavan, Giver, who pauses not to think.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And verily to him who toils and presses Soma juice for thee Thou quickly givest ample wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: No, not a hundred hinderers can check thy gracious bounty's flow, Nor thy great deeds when thou wilt act.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May thine assistance keep us safe, thy hundred and thy thousand aids: May all thy favours strengthen us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Do thou elect us this place for friendship and prosperity, And great celestial opulence.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Favour us, Indra, evermore with overflowing store of wealth: With all thy succours aid thou us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With new protections, Indra, like an archer, open thou for us The stables that are filled with kine.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Our chariot, Indra, boldly moves endued with splendour, ne'er repulsed, Winning for us both kine and steeds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Surya, make our fame to be most excellent among the Gods, Most lofty as the heaven on high.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O THOU who slewest Vrtra, come, O Indra, hither to our side, Mighty One with thy mighty aids.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Swift and impetuous art thou, wondrous amid the well-dressed folk: Thou doest marvels for our help.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Even with the weak thou smitest down him who is stronger, with thy strength The mighty, with the Friends thou hast.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Indra, we are close to thee; to thee we sing aloud our songs: Help and defend us, even us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As such, O Caster of the Stone, come with thy succours wonderful, Blameless, and irresistible.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May we be friends of one like thee, O Indra, with the wealth of kine, Comrades for lively energy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For thou, O Indra, art alone the Lord of strength that comes from kine So grant thou us abundant food.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They turn thee not another way, when, lauded, Lover of the Song, Thou wilt give wealth to those who praise.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Gotamas have sung their song of praise to thee that thou mayst give, Indra, for lively energy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We will declare thy hero deeds, what Disa forts thou brakest down, Attacking them in rapturous joy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The sages sing those manly deeds which, Indra, Lover of the Song, Thou wroughtest when the Soma flowed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, the Gotamas who bring thee praises have grown strong by thee. Give them renown with hero sons.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For, Indra, verily thou art the general treasure even of all . Thee, therefore, do we invocate.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Excellent Indra, turn to us: glad thee among us with the juice Of Somas, Soma-drinker thou.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May praise from us who think on thee, O Indra, bring thee near to us. Turn thy two Bay Steeds hitherward.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Eat of our sacrificial cake: rejoice thee in the songs we sing. Even as a lover in his bride.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To India for a thousand steeds well-trained and fleet of foot we pray, And hundred jars of Soma juice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We make a hundred of thy kine, yea, and a thousand, hasten nigh: So let thy bounty come to us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We have obtained, a gift from thee, ten water-ewers wrought of gold: Thou, Vrtra-slayer, givest much.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: A bounteous Giver, give us much, bring much and not a trifling gift: Much, Indra, wilt thou fain bestow.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Vrtra-slayer, thou art famed in many a place as bountiful Hero, thy bounty let us share.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I praise thy pair of Tawny Steeds, wise Son of him who giveth kine Terrify not the cows with these.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like two slight images of girls, unrobed, upon a new-wrought post, So shine the Bay Steeds in their course.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For me the Bays are ready when I start, or start not, with the dawn, Innocuous in the ways they take.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I SEND my voice as herald to the Rbhus; I crave the white cow for the overspreading. Wind-sped, the Skillful Ones in rapid motion have in an instant compassed round the heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What time the Rbus had with care and marvels done proper service to assist their Parents, They won the friendship of the Gods; the Sages carried away the fruit of their devotion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May they who made their Parents, who were lying like posts that moulder, young again for ever,- May Vaja, Vibhvan, Rbhu, joined with Indra , protect our sacrifice, the Soma-lovers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As for a year the Rbhus kept the Milch-cow, throughout a year fashioned and formed her body, And through a year's space still sustained her brightness, through these their labours they were made immortal.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Two beakers let us make,- thus said the eldest. Let us make three,- this was the younger's sentence. Four beakers let us make,- thus spoke the youngest. Tvastar approved this rede of yours, O Rbhus.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The men spake truth and even so they acted: this Godlike way of theirs the Rbhus followed. And Tvastar, when he looked on the four beakers resplendent as the day, was moved with envy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When for twelve days the Rbhus joyed reposing as guests of him who never may be hidden, Valley made fair fertile fields, they brought the rivers. Plants spread o'er deserts, waters filled the hollows.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May they who formed the swift car, bearing Heroes, and the Cow omniform and all-impelling, Even may they form wealth for us,-the Rbhus, dexterous-handed, deft in work and gracious.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So in their work the Gods had satisfaction, pondering it with thought and mental insight. The Gods' expert artificer was Vaja, Indra's Rbhuksan, Varuna's was Vibhvan.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They whole made glad with sacrifice and praises, wrought the two Bays, his docile Steeds, for Indra,- Rbhus, as those who wish a friend to prosper, bestow upon us gear and growth of riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This day have they set gladdening drink before you. Not without toil are Gods inclined to friendship. Therefore do ye who are so great, O Rbhus, vouchsafe us treasures at this third libation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To this our sacrifice come Rbhu, Vibhvan, Vaja, and Indra with the gift of riches, Because this day hath Dhisana the Goddess set drink for you: the gladdening draughts have reached you.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Knowing your birth and rich in gathered treasure, Rbhus, rejoice together with the Rtus. The gladdening draughts and wisdom have approached you: send ye us riches with good store of heroes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For you was made this sacrifice, O Rbhus, which ye, like men, won for yourselves aforetime. To you come all who find in you their pleasure: ye all were-even the two elder-Vajas.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now for the mortal worshipper, O Heroes, for him who served you, was the gift of riches. Drink, Vajas, Rbhus! unto you is offered, to gladden you, the third and great libation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come to us, Heroes, Vajas and Rbhuksans, glorified for the sake of mighty treasure. These draughts approach you as the day is closing, as cows, whose calves are newly-born, their stable.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come to this sacrifice of ours, ye Children of Strength, invoked with humble adoration. Drink of this meath, Wealth-givers, joined with Indra with whom ye are in full accord, ye Princes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Close knit with Varuna drink the Soma, Indra; close-knit, hymn-lover! with the Maruts drink it: Close-knit with drinkers first, who drink in season; close-knit with heavenly Dames who give us treasures.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Rejoice in full accord with the Adityas, in concord with the Parvatas, O Rbhus; In full accord with Savitar, Divine One; in full accord with floods that pour forth riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Rbhus, who helped their Parents and the Asvins, who formed the Milch-cow and the pair of horses, Made armour, set the heaven and earth asunder,-far- reaching Heroes, they have made good offspring.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye who have wealth in cattle and in booty, in heroes, in rich sustenance and treasure, Such, O ye Rbhus, first to drink, rejoicing, give unto us and those who laud our present.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye were not far: we have not left you thirsting, blameless in this our sacrifice, O Rbhus. Rejoice you with the Maruts and with Indra, with the Kings, Gods! that ye may give us riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come hither, O ye Sons of Strength, ye Rbhus; stay not afar, ye Children of Sudhanvan. At this libation is your gift of treasure. Let gladdening draughts approach you after Indra's.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hither is come the Rbhus' gift of riches; here was the drinking of the well-pressed Soma, Since by dexterity and skill as craftsmen ye made the single chalice to be fourfold
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye made fourfold the chalice that wag single: ye spake these words and said, O Friend, assist us; Then, Vajas! gained the path of life eternal, deft-handed Rbhus, to the Gods' assembly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Out of what substance was that chalice fashioned which ye made fourfold by your art and wisdom? Now for the gladdening draught press out the liquor, and drink, O Rbhus, of die meath of Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye with your cunning made your Parents youthful; the cup, for Gods to drink, ye formed with cunning; With cunning, Rbhus, rich in treasure, fashioned the two swift Tawny Steeds who carry Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whoso pours out for you, when days are closing, the sharp libation for your joy, O Vajas, For him, O mighty Rbhus, ye, rejoicing, have fashioned wealth with plenteous store of heroes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Lord of Bay Steeds, at dawn the juice thou drankest: thine, only thine, is the noonday libation. Now drink thou with the wealth-bestowing Rbhus, whom for their skill thou madest friends, O Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye, whom your artist skill hath raised to Godhead have set you down above in heaven like falcons. So give us riches, Children of Sudhanvan, O Sons of Strength; ye have become immortal.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The third libation, that bestoweth treasure, which ye have won by skill, ye dexterous-handed,- This drink hath been effused for you, O Rbhus . drink it with high delight, with joy like Indra's.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This car that was not made for horses or for reins, three-wheeled, worthy of lauds, rolls round the firmament. That is the great announcement of your Deity, that, O ye Rbhus, ye sustain the earth and heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye Sapient Ones who made the lightly-rolling car out of your mind, by thought, the car that never errs, You, being such, to drink of this drink offering, you, O ye Vajas, and ye Rbhus, we invoke.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Vajas, Rbhus, reaching far, among the Gods this was your exaltation gloriously declared, In that your aged Parents, worn with length of days, ye wrought again to youth so that they moved at will.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The chalice that wag single ye have made fourfold, and by your wisdom brought the Cow forth from the hide. So quickly, mid the Gods, ye gained immortal life. Vajas and Rbhus, your great work must be extolled.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wealth from the Rbhus is most glorious in renown, that which the Heroes, famed for vigour, have produced. In synods must be sung the car which Vibhvan wrought: that which ye favour, Gods! is famed among mankind.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Strong is the steed, the man a sage in eloquence, the bowman is a hero hard to beat in fight, Great store of wealth and manly power hath he obtained whom Vaja, Vibhvan, Rbhus have looked kindly on.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To you hath been assigned the fairest ornament, the hymn of praise: Vajas and Rbhus, joy therein; For ye have lore and wisdom and poetic skill: as such, with this our prayer we call on you to come.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: According to the wishes of our hearts may ye, who have full knowledge of all the delights of men, Fashion for us, O Rbhus, power and splendid wealth, rich in high courage, excellent, and vital strength.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bestowing on us here riches and offspring, here fashion fame for us befitting heroes. Vouchsafe us wealth of splendid sort, O Rbhus, that we may make us more renowned than others.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: COME to our sacrifice, Vajas, Rbhuksans, Gods, by the paths which Gods are wont to travel, As ye, gay Gods, accept in splendid weather the sacrifice among these folk of Manus.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May these rites please you in your heart and spirit; may the drops clothed in oil this day approach you. May the abundant juices bear you onward to power and strength, and, when imbibed, delight you.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Your threefold going near is God-appointed, so praise is given you, Vajas and Rbhuksans. So, Manus-like, mid younger folk I offer, to you who are aloft in heaven, the Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Strong, with fair chains of gold and jaws of iron, ye have a splendid car and well-fed horses. Ye Sons of Strength, ye progeny of Indra, to you the best is offered to delight you.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Rbhuksans! him, for handy wealth, the mightiest comrade in the fight, Him, Indra's equal, we invoke, most bounteous ever, rich in steeds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The mortal man whom, Rbhus, ye and Indra favour with your help, Must be successful, by his thoughts, at sacrifice and with the steed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Vajas and Rbhuksans, free for us the paths to sacrifice, Ye Princes, lauded, that we may press forward to each point of heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Vajas and Rbhuksans, ye Nasatyas, Indra, bless this wealth, And, before other men's, the steed, that ample riches may be won.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: FROM you two came the gifts in days aforetime which Trasadasyu granted to the Purus. Ye gave the winner of our fields and plough-lands, and the strong smiter who subdued the Dasytis.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And ye gave mighty Dadhikras, the giver of many gifts, who visiteth all people, Impetuous hawk, swift and of varied colour, like a brave King whom each true man must honour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whom, as 'twere down a precipice, swift rushing, each Puru praises and his heart rejoices,- Springing forth like a hero fain for battle, whirling the car and flying like the tempest.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who gaineth precious booty in the combats and moveth, winning spoil, among the cattle; Shown in bright colour, looking on the assemblies, beyond the churl, to worship of the living.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Loudly the folk cry after him in battles, as 'twere a thief who steals away a garment; Speeding to glory, or a herd of cattle, even as a hungry falcon swooping downward.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And, fain to come forth first amid these armies, this way and that with rows of cars he rushes, Gay like a bridesman, making him a garland, tossing the dust, champing the rein that holds him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And that strong Steed, victorious and faithful, obedient with his body in the combat, Speeding straight on amid the swiftly pressing, casts o'er his brows the dust he tosses upward.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And at his thunder, like the roar of heaven, those who attack tremble and are affrighted; For when he fights against embattled thousands, dread is he in his striving; none may stay him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The people praise the overpowering swiftness of this fleet Steed who giveth men abundance. Of him they say when drawing back from battle. Dadhikras hath sped forward with his thousands.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Dadhikras hath o'erspread the Fivefold People with vigour, as the Sun lightens the waters. May the strong Steed who winneth hundreds, thousands, requite with sweetness these my words and praises.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now give we praise to Dadhikras the rapid, and mention in our laud the Earth and Heaven. May the Dawns flushing move me to exertion, and bear me safely over every trouble.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I praise the mighty Steed who fills my spirit, the Stallion Dadhikravan rich in bounties, Whom, swift of foot and shining bright as Agni, ye, Varuna and Mitra, gave to Purus.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him who hath honoured, when the flame is kindled at break of dawn, the Courser Dadhikrivan, Him, of one mind with Varuna and Mitra may Aditi make free from all transgression.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When we remember mighty Dadhikravan our food and strength, then the blest name of Maruts, Varuna, Mitra, we invoke for welfare, and Agni, and the thunder-wielding Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Both sides invoke him as they call on Indra when they stir forth and turn to sacrificing. To us have Varuna and Mitra granted the Courser Dadhikris, a guide for mortals.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So have I glorified with praise strong Dadhikravan, conquering Steed. Sweet may he make our mouths; may he prolong the days we have to live.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: LET us recite the praise of Dadhikravan: may all the Mornings move me to exertion; Praise of the Lord of Waters, Dawn, and Agni, Brhaspati Son of Angiras, and Surya.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Brave, seeking war and booty, dwelling with the good and with the swift, may he hasten the food of Dawn. May he the true, the fleet, the lover of the course, the bird-like Dadhikravan, bring food, strength, and light.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: His pinion, rapid runner, fans him m his way, as of a bird that hastens onward to its aim, And, as it were a falcon's gliding through the air, strikes Dadhikravan's side as he speeds on with might.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bound by the neck and by the flanks and by the mouth, the vigorous Courser lends new swiftness to his speed. Drawing himself together, as his strength allows, Dadhikras springs along the windings of the paths.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Hamsa homed in light, the Vasu in mid-air, the priest beside the altar, in the house the guest, Dweller in noblest place, mid men, in truth, in sky, born of flood, kine, truth, mountain, he is holy Law.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WHAT laud, O Indra-Varuna, with oblation, hath like the Immortal Priest obtained your favour? Hath our effectual laud, addressed with homage, touched you, O Indra-Varuna, in spirit?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who with dainty food hath won you, Indra and Varuna, Gods, as his allies to friendship, Jayeth the Vrtras and his foes in battles, and through your mighty favours is made famous.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra and Varuna are most liberal givers of treasure to the men who toil to serve them, When they, as Friends inclined to friendship, honoured with dainty food, delight in flowing Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra and Varuna, ye hurl, O Mighty, on him your strongest flashing bolt of thunder Who treats us ill, the robber and oppressor: measure on him your overwhelming vigour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Indra-Varuna, be ye the lovers of this my song, as steers who love the milch-Cow. Milk may it yield us as, gone forth to pasture, the great Cow pouring out her thousand rivers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For fertile fields, for worthy sons and grandsons, for the Sun's beauty and for steer-like vigour, May Indra-Varuna with gracious favours work marvels for us in the stress of battle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For you, as Princes, for your ancient kindness, good comrades of the man who seeks for booty, We choose to us for the dear bond of friendship, most liberal Heroes bringing bliss like parents.
