verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O AGNI, be our nearest Friend, be thou a kind deliverer and a gracious Friend.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Excellent Agni, come thou nigh to us, and give us wealth most splendidly renowned.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So hear us, listen to this call of ours, and keep us far from every sinful man.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To thee then, O Most Bright, O Radiant God, we come with prayer for happiness for our friends.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I WILL sing near, for grace, your God Agni, for he is good to us. Son of the Brands, may he give gifts, and, righteous, save us from the foe.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For be is true, whom men of old enkindled, and the Gods themselves, The Priest with the delicious tongue, rich with the light of glorious beams.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With wisdom that surpasseth all, with gracious will most excellent, O Agni, worthy of our choice, shine wealth on us through hymns of praise.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni is King, for he extends to mortals and to Gods alike. Agni is bearer of our gifts. Worship ye Agni with your thoughts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni gives to the worshipper a son, the best, of mightiest fame, Of deep devotion, ne'er subdued, bringer of glory to his sire.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni bestows the hero-lord who conquers with the men in fight. Agni bestows the fleet-foot steed, the victor never overcome.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The mightiest song is Agni's: shine on high, thou who art rich in light. Like the Chief Consort of a King, riches and strength proceed -from thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Resplendent are thy rays of light: loud is thy voice like pressing-stones. Yea, of itself thy thunder goes forth like the roaring of the heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thus, seeking riches, have we paid homage to Agni Conqueror. May he, most wise, as with a ship, carry us over all our foes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O AGNI, Holy and Divine, with splendour and thy pleasant tongue Bring hither and adore the Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We pray thee, thou who droppest oil, bright-rayed! who lookest on the Sun, Bring the Gods hither to the feast.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We have enkindled thee, O Sage, bright caller of the Gods to feast. O Agni, great in Sacrifice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Agni, come with all the Gods, come to our sacrificial gift: We choose thee as Invoking Priest.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bring, Agni, to the worshipper who pours the juice, heroic strength: Sit with the Gods upon the grass.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Victor of thousands, Agni, thou, enkindled, cherishest the laws, Laud-worthy, envoy of the Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Set Agni Jatavedas down, the bearer of our sacred gifts, Most Youthful, God and Minister.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Duly proceed our sacrifice, comprising all the Gods, to-day: Strew holy grass to be their seat.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So may the Maruts sit thereon, the Asvins, Mitra, Varuna: The Gods with all their company.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THE Godlike hero, famousest of nobles, hath granted me two oxen with a wagon. Trvrsan's son Tryaruna hath distinguished himself, Vaisvanara Agni! with ten thousands.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Protect Tryaruna, as thou art waxing strong and art highly praised, Vaisvanara Agni! Who granteth me a hundred kine and twenty, and two bay horses, good at draught, and harnessed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So Trasadasyu served thee, God Most Youthful, craving thy favour for the ninth time, Agni; Tryaruya who with attentive spirit accepteth many a song from me the mighty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who declares his wish to me, to Asvamedha, to the Prince, Pays him who with his verse seeks gain, gives power to him who keeps the Law.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: From whom a hundred oxen, all of speckled hue, delight my heart, The gifts of Asvamedha, like thrice-mingled draughts of Soma juice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To Asvamedha who bestows a hundred gifts grant hero power, O Indra-Agni! lofty rule like the unwasting Sun in heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: AGNI inflamed hath sent to heaven his lustre: he shines forth widely turning unto Morning. Eastward the ladle goes that brings all blessing, praising the Godswith homage and oblation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Enkindled, thou art King of the immortal world: him who brings offerings thou attendest for his weal. He whom thou urgest on makes all possessions his: he sets before thee, Agni, gifts that guests may claim.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Show thyself strong for mighty bliss, O Agni, most excellent be thine effulgent splendours. Make easy to maintain our household lordship, and overcome the might of those who hate us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thy glory, Agni, I adore, kindled, exalted in thy strength. A Steer of brilliant splendour, thou art lighted well at sacred rites.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, invoked and kindled, serve the Gods, thou skilled in sacrifice: For thou art bearer of our gifts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Invoke and worship Agni while the sacrificial rite proceeds: For offering-bearer choose ye him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: MAN'S worship of the Gods hath three great lustres, and three celestial lights have they established The Maruts gifted with pure strength adore thee, for thou, O Indra, art their sapient Rsi.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What time the Maruts sang their song to Indra, joyous when he had drunk of Soma juices, He grasped his thunderbolt to slay the Dragon, and loosed, that they might flow, the youthful Waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And, O ye Brahmans, Maruts, so may Indra drink draughts of this my carefully pressed Sorna; For this oblation found for man the cattle, and Indra, having quaffed it, slew the Dragon.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Then heaven and earth he sundered and supported: wrapped even in these he struck the Beast with terror. So Indra forced the Engulfer to disgorgement, and slew the Danava. panting against him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thus all the Gods, O Maghavan, delivered to thee of their free will the draught of Soma; When thou for Etasa didst cause to tarry the flying mares of Surya racing forward.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When Maghavan with the thunderbolt demolished his nine-and-ninety castles all together, The Maruts, where they met, glorified Indra: ye with the Trstup hymn obstructed heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As friend to aid a friend, Agni dressed quickly three hundred buffaloes, even as he willed it. And Indra, from man's gift, for Vrtra's slaughter, drank of at once three lakes of pressed-out Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When thou three hundred buffaloes' flesh hadst eaten, and drunk, as Maghavan, three lakes of Soma, All the Gods raised as 'twere a shout of triumph to Indra praise because he slew the Dragon.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What time ye came with strong steeds swiftly speeding, O Usana and Indra, to the dwelling, Thou camest thither -conquering together with Kutsa and the Gods: thou slewest Susna.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: One car-wheel of the Sun thou rolledst forward, and one thou settest free to move for Kutsa. Thou slewest noseless Dasyus with thy weapon, and in their home o'erthrewest hostile speakers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The lauds of Gauriviti made thee mighty to Vidathin's son, as prey, thou gavest Pipru. Rjisivan drew thee into friendship dressing the sacred food, and thou hast drunk his Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Navagvas and Dasgvas with libations of Soma juice sing hymns of praise to Indra. Labouring at their task the men laid open the stall of Kine though firmly closed and fastened.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: How shall I serve thee, Maghavan, though knowing full well what hero deeds thou hast accomplished? And the fresh deeds which thou wilt do, Most Mighty! these, too, will we tell forth in sacred synods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Resistless from of old through hero courage, thou hast done all these many acts, O Indra. What thou wilt do in bravery, Thunder-wielder! none is there who may hinder this thy prowess.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, accept the prayers which now are offered, accept the new prayers, Mightiest! which we utter. Like fair and well-made robes, I, seeking riches, as a deft craftsman makes a car, have wrought them.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WHERE is that Hero? Who hath looked on Indra borne on light-rolling car by Tawny Coursers, Who, Thunderer, seeks with wealth the Soma-presser, and to his house goes, much-invoked, to aid him?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I have beheld his strong and secret dwelling, longing have sought the Founder's habitation. I asked of others, and they said in answer, May we, awakened men, attain to Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We will tell, Indra, when we pour libation, what mighty deeds thou hast performed to please us. Let him who knows not learn, who knows them listen: hither rides Maghavan with all his army.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, when born, thou madest firm thy spirit: alone thou seekest war to fight with many. With might thou clavest e'en the rock asunder, and foundest out the stable of the Milch-kine.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When thou wast born supremest at a distance, bearing a name renowned in far-off regions, Since then e'en Gods have been afraid of Indra: he conquered all the floods which served the Dasa.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These blissful Maruts sing their psalm to praise thee, and pour to thee libation of the Soma. Indra with wondrous powers subdued the Dragon, the guileful lurker who beset the waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, Maghavan, from the first didst scatter foemen, speeding, while joying in the milk, the Giver. There, seeking man's prosperity, thou torest away the head of Namuci the Dasa.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Pounding the head of Namuci the Dasa, me, too thou madest thine associate, Indra! Yea, and the rolling stone that is in heaven both worlds, as on a car, brought to the Maruts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Women for weapons hath the Dasa taken, What injury can his feeble armies To me? Well he distinguished his two different voices, and Indra then advanced to fight the Dasyu.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Divided from their calves the Cows went lowing around, on every side, hither and thither. These Indra re-united with his helpers, what time the well-pressed Soma made him joyful.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What time the Somas mixed by Babhru cheered him, loud the Steer bellowed in his habitations. So Indra drank thereof, the Fort-destroyer, and gave him guerdon, in return, of milch-kine.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This good deed have the Rusamas done, Agni! that they have granted me four thousand cattle. We have received Rnancaya's wealth, of heroes the most heroic, which was freely offered.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Rusamas, O Agni, sent me homeward with fair adornment and with kine in thousands. The strong libations have made Indra joyful, when night, whose course was ending, changed to morning.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Night, well-nigh ended, at Rnancaya's coming, King of the Rusamas, was changed to morning. Like a strong courser, fleet of foot, urged onward, Babhru hath gained four thousand as his guerdon.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We have received four thousand head of cattle presented by the Rusamas, O Agni. And we, the singers, have received the caldron of metal which was heated for Pravargya.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: MAGHAVAN Indra turns his chariot downward, the strength-displaying car which he hath mounted. Even as a herdsman driveth forth his cattle, he goeth, first, uninjured, fain for treasure.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Haste to us, Lord of Bays; be not ungracious: visit us, lover of gold-hued oblation. There is naught else better than thou art, Indra: e'en to the wifeless hast thou given spouses.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When out of strength arose the strength that conquers, Indra displayed all powers that he possesses. Forth from the cave he drove the milky mothers, and with the light laid bare investing darkness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Anus have wrought a chariot for thy Courser, and Tvastar, Much-invoked! thy bolt that glitters. The Brahmans with their songs exalting Indra increased his strength that he might slaughter Ahi.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When heroes sang their laud to thee the Hero, Indra! and stones and Aditi accordant, Without or steed or chariot were the fellies which, sped by Indra, rolled upon the Dasytis.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I will declare thine exploits wrought aforetime, and, Maghavan, thy deeds of late achievement, When, Lord of Might, thou sunderedst earth and heaven, winning for man the moistly-gleaming waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This is thy deed, e'en this, Wonderful! Singer! that, slaying Ahi, here thy strength thou showedst, Didst check and stay e'en Susna's wiles and magic, and, drawing nigh, didst chase away the Dasytis.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, Indra, on the farther bank for Yadu and Turvaga didst stay the gushing waters. Ye both assailed the fierce: thou barest Kutsa: when Gods and Usana came to you together.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let the steeds bring you both, Indra and Kutsa, borne on the chariot within hearing-distance. Ye blew him from the waters, from his dwelling, and chased the darkness from the noble's spirit.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Even this sage hath come looking for succour even to Vata's docile harnessed horses. Here are the Maruts, all, thy dear companions: prayers have increased thy power and might, O Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When night was near its close he carried forward e'en the Sun's chariot backward in its running. Etaga brought his wheel and firmly stays it: setting it eastward he shall give us courage.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This Indra, O ye men, hath come to see you, seeking a friend who hath expressed the Soma. The creaking stone is laid upon the altar, and the Adhvaryus come to turn it quickly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let mortals who were happy still be happy; let them not come to sorrow, O Immortal. Love thou the pious, and to these thy people-with whom may we be numbered-give thou vigour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: 1.THE well thou clavest, settest free the fountains, and gavest rest to floods that were obstructed. Thou, Indra, laying the great mountain open, slaying the Danava, didst loose the torrents.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The fountain-depths obstructed in their seasons, thou, Thunderer! madest flow, the mountain's udder. Strong Indra, thou by slaying e'en the Dragon that lay extended there hast shown thy vigour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra with violence smote down the weapon, yea, even of that wild and mighty creature. Although he deemed himself alone unequalled, another had been born e'en yet more potent.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him, whom the heavenly food of these delighted, child of the mist, strong waxing, couched in darkness, Him the bolt-hurling Thunderer with his lightning smote down and slew, the Danava's wrath-fire, Susna.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Though he might ne'er be wounded still his vitals felt that, the God's bolt, which his powers supported, When, after offered draughts, Strong Lord, thou laidest him, fain to battle, in the pit in darkness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him as he lay there huge in length extended, still waxing in the gloom which no sun lightened, Him, after loud-voiced threats, the Hero Indra, rejoicing in the poured libation, slaughtered.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When 'gainst the mighty Danava his weapon Indra uplifted, power which none could combat, When at the hurling of his bolt he smote him, he made him lower than all living creatures.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The fierce God seized that huge and restless coiler, insatiate, drinker of the sweets, recumbent, And with his mighty weapon in his dwelling smote down the footless evil-speaking ogre.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who may arrest his strength or cheek his vigour? Alone, resistless, he bears off all riches. Even these Twain, these Goddesses, through terror of Indra's might, retire from his dominion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: E'en the Celestial Axe bows down before him, and the Earth, lover-like, gives way to Indra. As he imparts all vigour to these people, straightway the folk bend them to him the Godlike.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I hear that thou wast born sole Lord of heroes of the Five Races, famed among the people. As such my wishes have most lately grasped him, invoking Indra both at eve and morning.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So, too, I hear of thee as in due season urging to action and enriching singers. What have thy friends received from thee, the Brahmans who, faithful, rest their hopes on thee, O Indra?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: GREAT praise to Indra, great and strong mid heroes, I ponder thus, the feeble to the Mighty, Who with his band shows favour to this people, when lauded, in the fight where spoil is gathered.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So made attentive by our hymns, Steer! Indra! thou fastenedst the girth of thy Bay Coursers, Which, Maghavan, at thy will thou drivest hither. With these subdue for us the men who hate us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They were not turned to us-ward, lofty Indra! while yet through lack of prayer they stood unharnessed. Ascend this chariot, thou whose hand wields thunder, and draw the rein, O Lord of noble horses.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, because many lauds are thine, O Indra, wast active warring in the fields for cattle. For Surya in his own abode thou, Hero, formedst in fights even a Dasa's nature.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thine are we, Indra; thine are all these people, conscious of might, whose cars are set in motion. Some hero come to us, O Strong as Ahi beauteous in war, to be invoked like Bhaga.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Strength much to be desired is in thee, Indra: the Immortal dances forth his hero exploits. Such, Lord of Treasure, give us splendid riches. I praise the Friend's gift, his whose wealth is mighty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thus favour us, O Indra, with thy succour; Hero, protect the bards who sing thy praises. Be friendly in the fray to those who offer the skin of beautiful and well-pressed Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And these ten steeds which Trasadasyu gives me, the gold rich chief, the son of Purukutsa, Resplendent in their brightness shall convey me. Gairiksita willed it and so came I hither.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And these, bestowed as sacrificial guerdon, the powerful tawny steeds of Marutasva; And thousands which kind Cyavatana gave me, abundantly bestowed for my adornment.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And these commended horses, bright and active, by Dhvanya son of Laksmana presented, Came unto me, as cows into the Rsi Samvarana's stall, with magnitude of riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: BOUNDLESS and wasting not, the heavenly food of Gods goes to the foeless One, doer of wondrous deeds. Press out, make ready, offer gifts with special zeal to him whom many laud, accepter of the prayer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who filled full his belly with the Soma's juice, Maghavan, was delighted with the meath's sweet draught, When Usana, that he might slay the monstrous beast, gave him the mighty weapon with a thousand points.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Illustrious is the man whoever presseth out Soma for him in sunshine or in cloud and rain. The mighty Maghavan who is the sage's Friend advanceth more and more his beauteous progeny.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Strong God doth not flee away from him whose sire, whose mother or whose brother he hath done to death. He, the Avenger, seeketh this man's offered gifts: this God, the source of riches, doth not flee from sin.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He seeks no enterprise with five or ten to aid, nor stays with him who pours no juice though prospering well. The Shaker conquers or slays in this way or that, and to the pious gives a stable full of kine.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Exceeding strong in war he stays the chariot wheel, and, hating him who pours not, prospers him who pours. Indra the terrible, tamer of every man, as Arya leads away the Dasa at his will.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He gathers up for plunder all the niggards gear: excellent wealth he gives to him who offers gifts. Not even in wide stronghold may all the folk stand firm who have provoked to anger his surpassing might.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When Indra Maghavan hath marked two wealthy men fighting for beauteous cows with all their followers, He who stirs all things takes one as his close ally, and, Shaker, with his Heroes, sends the kine to him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni! I laud the liberal Agnivesi, Satri the type and standard of the pious. May the collected waters yield him plenty, and his be powerful and bright dominion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: INDRA, for our assistance bring that most effectual power of thine, Which conquers men for us, and wins the spoil, invincible in fight.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, whatever aids be thine, four be they, or, O Hero, three, Or those of the Five Tribes of men, bring quickly all that help to us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The aid most excellent of thee the Mightiest hitherward we call, For thou wast born with hero might, conquering, Indra, with the Strong.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Mighty to prosper us wast thou born, and mighty is the strength thou hast. In native power thy soul is firm: thy valour, Indra, slays a host.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Satakratu, Lord of Strength, O Indra, Caster of the Stone. With all thy chariot's force assail the man who shows himself thy foe.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For, Mightiest Vrtra-slayer, thee, fierce, foremost among many, folk Whose sacred grass is trimmed invite to battle where the spoil is won.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, do thou protect our car that mingles foremost in the fights, That bears its part in every fray, invincible and seeking spoil.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come to us, Indra, and protect our car with thine intelligence. May we, O Mightiest One, obtain excellent fame at break of day, and meditate our hymn at dawn.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: MAY Indra come to us, he who knows rightly to give forth treasures from his store of riches. Even as a thirsty steer who roams the deserts may he drink eagerly the milked-out Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Lord of Bay Horses, Hero, may the Soma rise to thy cheeks and jaws like mountain-ridges. May we, O King, as he who driveth coursers, all joy in thee with hymns, invoked of many!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Invoked of many, Caster of the Stone my heart quakes like a rolling wheel for fear of penury. Shall not Puruvasu the singer give thee praise, O ever-prospering Maghavan, mounted on thy car?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like the press-stone is this thy praiser, Indra. Loudly he lifts his voice with strong endeavour. With thy left hand, O Maghavan, give us riches: with thy right, Lord of Bays, be not reluctant.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May the strong Heaven make thee the Strong wax stronger: Strong, thou art borne by thy two strong Bay Horses. So, fair of cheek, with mighty chariot, mighty, uphold us, strong-willed, thunder armed, in battle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Maruts, let all the people in obeisance bow down before this youthful Srutaratha, Who, rich in steeds, gave me two dark red horses together with three hundred head of cattle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: BEDEWED with holy oil and meetly worshipped, the Swift One vies with Surya's beam in splendour. For him may mornings dawn without cessation who saith, Let us press Soma out for Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With kindled fire and strewn grass let him worship, and, Soma-presser, sing with stones adjusted: And let the priest whose press-stones ring forth loudly, go down with his oblation to the river.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This wife is coming near who loves her husband who carries to his home a vigorous consort. Here may his car seek fame, here loudly thunder, and his wheel make a thousand revolutions.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: No troubles vex that King in whose home Indra drinks the sharp Soma juice with milk commingled. With heroes he drives near, he slays the foeman: Blest, cherishing that name, he guards his people.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May he support in peace and win in battle: he masters both the hosts that meet together. Dear shall he be to Surya, dear to Agni, who with pressed Soma offers gifts to India.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WIDE, Indra Satakratu, spreads the bounty of thine ample grace: So, Lord of fair dominion, Friend of all men, give us splendid wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The food which, Mightiest Indra, thou possessest worthy of renown Is bruited as most widely famed, invincible, O Golden-hued!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Darter of the Stone, the powers which readily obey thy will,- Divinities, both thou and they, ye rule, to guard them, earth and heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And from whatever power of thine, O Vrtra-slayer, it may be, Bring thou to us heroic strength: thou hast a man's regard for us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In thy protection, with these aids of thine, O Lord of Hundred Powers, Indra, may we be guarded well, Hero, may we be guarded well.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: STONE-DARTING Indra. Wondrous One, what wealth is richly given from thee, That bounty, Treasure-Finder! bring filling both thy hands, to us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bring what thou deemest worth the wish, O Indra, that which is in heaven. So may we know thee as thou art, boundless in thy munificence.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thy lofty spirit, far-renowned as fain to give and prompt to win,- With this thou rendest e'en the firm, Stone-Darter! so to gain thee strength.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Singers with many songs have made Indra propitious to their fame, Him who is King of human kind, most liberal of your wealthy ones.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To him, to Indra must be sung the poet's word, the hymn of praise. To him, accepter of the prayer, the Atris raise their songs on high, the Atris beautify their songs.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: COME thou to what the stones have pressed, drink Soma, O thou Soma's Lord, Indra best Vrtra-slayer Strong One, with the Strong.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Strong is the stone, the draught is strong, strong is this Soma that is pressed, Indra, best Vrtra-slayer, Strong One with the Strong.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As strong I call on thee the Strong, O Thunder-armed, with various aids, Indra, best Vrtra-slayer, Strong One with the Strong.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Impetuous, Thunderer, Strong, quelling the mighty, King, potent, Vrtra-slayer, Soma-drinker, May he come hither with his yoked Bay Horses; may Indra gladden him at the noon libation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Surya, when the Asura's descendant Svarbhanu, pierced thee through and through with darkness, All creatures looked like one who is bewildered, who knoweth not the place where he is standing.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What time thou smotest down Svarbhanu's magic that spread itself beneath the sky, O Indra, By his fourth sacred prayer Atri discovered Surya concealed in gloom that stayed his function.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let not the oppressor with this dread, through anger swallow me up, for I am thine, O Atri. Mitra art thou, the sender of true blessings: thou and King Varuna be both my helpers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Brahman Atri, as he set the press-stones, serving the Gods with praise and adoration, Established in the heaven the eye of Surya, and caused Svarbhanu's magic arts to vanish.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Atris found the Sun again, him whom Svarbhanu of the brood Of Asuras had pierced with gloom. This none besides had power to do.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WHO, Mitra-Varuna, is your pious servant to give you gifts from earth or mighty heaven? Preserve us in the seat of holy Order, and give the offerer power that winneth cattle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Mitra, Varuna, Aryaman, and Ayu, Indra Rbhuksan, and the Maruts, love us, And they who of one mind with bounteous Rudra accept the hymn and laud with adorations.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: You will I call to feed the car-horse, Asvins, with the wind's flight swiftest of those who travel: Or also to the Asura of heaven, Worshipful, bring a hymn as 'twere libation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The heavenly Victor, he whose priest is Kanva, Trta with Dyaus accordant, Vata, Agni, All-feeding Pusan, Bhaga sought the oblation, as they whose steeds are fleetest seek the contest.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bring ye your riches forward borne on horses: let thought be framed for help and gain of treasure. Blest he the priest of Ausija through courses, the courses which are yours the fleet, O Maruts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bring hither him who yokes the car, your Vayu, who praises with his songs, the God and Singer; And, praying and devout, noble and prudent, may the Gods' Spouses in their thoughts retain us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I speed to you with powers that should be honoured, with songs distinguishing Heaven's mighty Daughters, Morning and Night, the Two, as 'twere all-knowing: these bring the sacrifice unto the mortal.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: You I extol, the nourishers of heroes bringing you gifts, Vastospati and Tvastar- Rich Dhisana accords through our obeisance - andTrees and Plants, for the swift gain of riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ours be the Parvatas, even they, for offspring, free-moving, who are Heroes like the Vasus. May holy Aptya, Friend of man, exalted, strengthen our word for ever and be near us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Trta praised him, germ of the earthly hero, with pure songs him the Offspring of the Waters. Agn; with might neighs loudly like a charger: he of the flaming hair destroys the forests.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: How shall we speak to the great might of Rudra? How speak to Bhaga who takes thought for riches? May Plants, the Waters, and the Sky preserve us, and Woods and Mountains with their trees for tresses.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May the swift Wanderer, Lord of refreshments listen to our songs, who speeds throuih cloudy heaven: And may the Waters, bright like castles, hear us, as they flow onward from the cloven mountain.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We know your ways, ye Mighty Ones receiving choice meed, ye Wonderful, we will proclaim it. Even strong birds descend not to the mortal who strives to reach them with swift blow and weapons.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Celestial and terrestrial generations, and Waters will I summon to the feasting. May days with bright dawns cause my songs to prosper, and may the conquered streams increase their waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Duly to each one hath my laud been offered. Strong be Varutri with her powers to succour. May the great Mother Rasa here befriend us, straight-handed, with the princes, striving forward.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: How may we serve the Liberal Ones with worship, the Maruts swift of course in invocation, the Maruts far-renowned in invocation? Let not the Dragon of the Deep annoy us, and gladly may he welcome our addresses.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thus thinking, O ye Gods, the mortal wins you to give him increase of his herds of cattle: the mortal wins him, O ye Gods, your favour. Here he wins wholesome food to feed this body: as for mine old age, Nirrti consume it
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Gods, may we obtain from you this favour, strengthening food through the Cow's praise, ye Vasus. May she who gives good gifts, the gracious Goddes. s, come speeding nigh to us for our well-being.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Ila, Mother of the herds of cattle, and Urvasi with all the streams accept us; May Urvasi in lofty heaven accepting, as she partakes the oblation of the living,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Visit us while she shares Urjavya's food.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now may our sweetest song with deep devotion reach Varuna, Mitra, Aditi, and Bhaga. May the Five Priests' Lord, dwelling in oblations, bliss-giving Asura, hear, whose paths are open.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Aditi welcome, even as a mother her dear heart-gladdening son, my song that lauds her. The prayer they love, bliss-giving, God-appointed, I offer unto Varuna and Mitra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In spirit him, the Sagest of the Sages; with sacrificial oil and meath bedew him So then let him, God Savitar, provide us excellent, ready, and resplendent treasures.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With willing mind, Indra, vouchsafe us cattle, prosperity, Lord of Bays! and pious patrons; And, with the sacred prayer by Gods appointed, give us the holy Deities' lovingkindness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: God Bhaga, Savitar who deals forth riches, Indra, and they who conquer Vrtra's treasures, And Vaja and Rbhuksan and Purandhi, the Mighty and Immortal Ones, protect us!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let us declare his deeds, the undecaying unrivalled Victor whom the Maruts follow. None of old times, O Maghavan, nor later, none of these days hath reached thy hero prowess.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Praise him the Chief who gives the boon of riches, Brhaspati distributor of treasures, Who, blessing most the man who sings and praises, comes with abundant wealth to his invoker.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Tended, Brhaspati, with thy protections, the princes are unharmed and girt by heroes. Wealth that brings bliss is found among the givers of horses and of cattle and of raiment.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Make their wealth flee who, through our hymns enjoying their riches, yield us not an ample guerdon. Far from the sun keep those who hate devotion, the godless, prospering in their vocation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With wheelless chariots drive down him, O Maruts, who at the feasts of Gods regards the demons. May he, though bathed in sweat, form empty wishes, who blames his sacred rite who toils to serve you.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Praise him whose bow is strong and sure his arrow, him who is Lord of every balm that bealeth. Worship thou Rudra for his great good favour: adore the Asura, God, with salutations.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May the House-friends, the cunning-handed Artists, may the Steer's Wives, the streams carved out by Vibhvan, And may the fair Ones honour and befriend us, Sarasvati, Brhaddiva, and Raka.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: My newest song, thought that now springs within me, I offer to the Great, the Sure Protector, Who made for us this All, in fond love laying each varied form within his Daughter's bosom.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now, even now, may thy fair praise, O Singer, attain Idaspati who roars and thunders, Who, rich in clouds and waters with his lightning speeds forth bedewing both the earth and heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May this my laud attain the troop of Maruts, those who are youths in act, the Sons of Rudra. The wish calls me to riches and well-being: praise the unwearied Ones whose steeds are dappled.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May this my laud reach earth and air's mid-region, and forest trees and plants to win me riches. May every Deity be swift to listen, and Mother Earth with no ill thought regard me.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Gods, may we dwell in free untroubled bliss.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May we obtain the Asvins' newest favour, and gain their health-bestowing happy guidance. Bring riches hither unto us, and heroes, and all felicity and joy, Immortals!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: MAY the Milch-cows who hasten to their object come harmless unto us with liquid sweetness. The Singer, lauding, calls, for ample riches, the Seven Mighty Ones who bring enjoyment.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With reverence and fair praise will I bring hither, for sake of strength, exhaustless Earth and Heaven. Father and Mother, sweet of speech, fairhanded, may they, far-famed, in every fight protect us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Adhvaryus, make the sweet libations ready, and bring the beautiful bright juice to Vayu. God, as our Priest, be thou the first to drink it: we give thee of the mead to make thee joyful.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Two arms-the Soma's dexterous immolators-and the ten fingers set and fix the press-stone. The stalk hath poured, fair with its spreading branches, the mead's bright glittering juice that dwells on mountains.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Soma hath been pressed for thee, its lover, to give thee power and might and high enjoyment. Invoked, turn hither in thy car, O Indra, at need, thy two well-trained and dear Bay Horses.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bring by God-traversed paths, accordant, Agni, the great Aramati, Celestial Lady, Exalted, worshipped with our gifts and homage, who knoweth holy Law, to drink sweet Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As on his father's lap the son, the darling, so on the fire is set the sacred caldron, Which holy singers deck, as if extending and heating that which holds the fatty membrane.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hither, as herald to invite the Asvins, come the great lofty song, most sweet and pleasant! Come in one car, joy-givers! to the banquet, like the bolt binding pole and nave, come hither.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I have declared this speech of adoration to mightiest Pusan and victorious Vayu, Who by their bounty are the hymns' inspirers, and of themselves give power as a possession.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Invoked by us bring hither, Jatavedas the Maruts all under their names and figures. Come to the sacrifice with aid all Maruts, all to the songs and praises of the singer!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: From high heaven may Sarasvati the Holy visit our sacrifice, and from the mountain. Eager, propitious, may the balmy Goddess hear our effectual speech, our invocation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Set in his seat the God whose back is dusky, Brhaspati the lofty, the Disposer. Him let us worship, set within the dwelling, the red, the golden-hued, the all resplendent.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May the Sustainer, high in heaven, come hither, the Bounteous One, invoked, with all his favours, Dweller with Dames divine, with plants, unwearied, the Steer with triple horn, the life-bestower.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The tuneful eloquent priests of him who liveth have sought the Mother's bright and loftiest station. As living men, with offered gifts and homage they deck the most auspicious Child to clothe him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, great vital power is thine, the mighty: pairs waxing old in their devotion seek thee. May every Deity be swift to listen, and Mother Earth with no ill thought regard me.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Gods, may we dwell in free untroubled bliss.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May we obtain the Asvins' newest favour, and gain their health-bestowing happy guidance. Bring riches hither unto us, and heroes, and all felicity and joy, Immortals!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As in the first old times, as all were wont, as now, he draweth forth the power turned hitherward with song, The Princedom throned on holy grass, who findeth light, swift, conquering in the' plants wherein he waxeth strong.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Shining to him who leaves heaven's regions undisturbed, which to his sheen who is beneath show fair in light, Good guardian art thou, not to be deceived, Most Wise! Far from deceits thy name dwelleth in holy Law.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Truth waits upon oblation present and to come: naught checks him in his way, this vic tory- bringing Priest: The Mighty Child who glides along the sacred grass, the undecaying Youth set in the midst of plants.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These come, well-yoked, to you for furtherance in the rite: down come the twinborn strengtheners of Law for him, With reins easily guided and commanding all. In the deep fall the hide stealeth away their names.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, moving beauteously in visibly pregnant ones, snatching with trees the branching plant that grasps the juice, Shinest, true Singer! mid the upholders of the voice. Increase thy Consorts thou, lively at sacrifice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like as he is beheld such is he said to be. They with effectual splendour in the floods have made Earth yield us room enough and amply wide extent, great might invincible, with store of hero sons.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Surya the Sage, as if unwedded, with a Spouse, in battle-loving spirit moveth o'er the foes. May he, self-excellent, grant us a sheltering home, a house that wards the fierce heat off on every side.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thy name, sung forth by Rsis in these hymns of ours, goes to the loftier One with this swift mover's light. By skill he wins the boon whereon his heart is set: he who bestirs himself shall bring the thing to pass.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The chief and best of these abideth in the sea, nor doth libation fail wherein it is prolonged. The heart of him who praiseth trembleth not in fear there where the hymn is found connected with the pure.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For it is he: with though to of Ksatra, Manasa, of Yajata, and Sadhri, and Evavada, With Avatsara's sweet songs will we strive to win the mightiest strength which even he who knows should gain.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Hawk is their full source, girth-stretching rapturous drink of Visvavara, of Mayin, and Yajata. They ever seek a fresh draught so that they may come, know when thy time to halt and drink thy fill is near.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sadaprna the holy, Tarya, Srutavit, and Bahuvrkta, joined with you, have slain the foes. He gains his wish in both the worlds and brightly shines-when he adores the host with well-advancing steeds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The worshipper's defender is Sutambhara, producer and uplifter of all holy thoughts. The milch-cow brought, sweet-flavoured milk was dealt around. Who speaks the bidding text knows this, not he who sleeps.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The sacred hymns love him who wakes and watches: to him who watches come the Sama verses. This Soma saith unto the man who watches, I rest and have my dwelling in thy friendship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni is watchful, and the gcas love him; Agni is watchful, Sama verses seek him. Agni is watchful, to him saith this Soma, I rest and have my dwelling in thy friendship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: BARDS of approaching Dawn who know the heavens are come with hymns to throw the mountain open. The Sun hath risen and open the stable portals: the doors of men, too, hath the God thrown open.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Surya hath spread his light as splendour: hither came the Cows' Mother, conscious, from the stable, To streams that flow with biting waves to deserts; and heaven is stablished like a firm-set pillar.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This laud hath won the burden of the mountain. To aid the ancient birth of mighty waters The mountain parted, Heaven performed his office. The worshippers were worn with constant serving.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With hymns and God-loved words will I invoke you, Indra and Agni, to obtain your favour, For verily sages, skilled in sacrificing, worship the Maruts and with lauds invite them.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This day approach us: may our thoughts be holy, far from us let us cast away misfortune. Let us keep those who hate us at a distance, and haste to meet the man who sacrifices.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come, let us carry out, O friends, the purpose wherewith the Mother threw the Cow's stall open, That wherewith Manu conquered Visisipra, wherewith the wandering merchant gained heaven's water.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Here, urged by hands, loudly hath rung the press-stone wherewith Navagvas through ten months sang praises. Sarama went aright and found the cattle. Angiras gave effect to all their labours.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When at the dawning of this mighty Goddess, Angirases all sang forth with the cattle,- Their spring is in the loftiest place of meeting,-Sarama found the kine by Order's pathway.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Borne by his Coursers Seven may Surya visit the field that spreadeth wide for his long journey. Down on the Soma swooped the rapid Falcon. Bright was the young Sage moving mid his cattle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Surya hath mounted to the shining ocean when he hath yoked his fair-backed Tawny Horses. The wise have drawn him like a ship through water: the floods obedient have descended hither.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I lay upon the Floods your hymn, light winning, wherewith Navagvas their ten months completed. Through this our hymn may we have Gods to guard us: through this our hymn pass safe beyond affliction.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WELL knowing I have bound me, horselike, to the pole: I carry that which bears as on and gives us help. I seek for no release, no turning back therefrom. May he who knows the way, the Leader, guide me straight.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Agni, Indra, Varuna, and Mitra, give, O ye Gods, and Marut host, and Visnu. May both Nasatyas, Rudra, heavenly Matrons, Pusan, Sarasvati, Bhaga, accept us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra and Agni, Mitra, Varuna, Aditi, the Waters, Mountains, Maruts, Sky, and Earth and Heaven, Visnu I call, Pusan, and Brahmanaspati, and Bhaga, Samsa, Savitar that they may help.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Visnu also and Vata who injures none, and Soma granter of possessions give us joy; And may the Rbhus and the Asvins, Tvastar and Vibhvan remember us so that we may have wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So may the band of Maruts dwelling in the sky, the holy, come to us to sit on sacred grass; Brhaspati and Pusan grant us sure defense, Varuna, Mitra, Aryaman guard and shelter us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And may the Mountains famed in noble eulogies, and the fair-gleaming Rivers keep us safe from harm. May Bhaga the Dispenser come with power and grace, and far-pervading Aditi listen to my call.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May the Gods' Spouses aid us of their own freewill, aid us to offspring and the winning of the spoil. Grant us protection, O ye gracious Goddesses, ye who are on the earth or in the waters' realm.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May the Dames, wives of Gods, enjoy our presents, Rat, Asvini, Agnayi, and Indrani. May Rodasi and Varunani hear us, and Goddesses come at the Matrons' season.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: URGING to toil and making proclamation, seeking Heaven's Daughter comes the Mighty Mother: She comes, the youthful Hymn, unto the Fathers, inviting to her home and loudly calling.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Swift in their motion, hasting to their duty, reaching the central point of life immortal, On every side about the earth and heaven go forth the spacious paths without a limit.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Steer, Sea, Red Bird with strong wings, he hath entered the dwelling-place of the Primeval Father. A gay-hued Stone set in the midst of heaven, he hath gone forth and guards mid-air's two limits.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Four bear him up and give him rest and quiet, and ten invigorate the Babe for travel. His kine most excellent, of threefold nature, pass swiftly round the boundaries of heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wondrous, O people, is the mystic knowledge that while the waters stand the streams are flowing: That, separate from his Mother, Two support him, closely-united, twins, here made apparent.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For him they lengthen prayers and acts of worship: the Mothers weave garments for him their offspring. Rejoicing, for the Steer's impregning contact, his Spouses move on paths or heaven to meet him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Be this our praise, O Varuna and Mitra may this be health and force to us, O Agni. May we obtain firm ground and room for resting: Glory to Heaven, the lofty habitation!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WHAT may we meditate for the beloved Power, mighty in native strength and glorious in itself, Which as a magic energy seeking waters spreads even to the immeasurable middle region's cloud?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O'er all the region with their uniform advance these have spread out the lore that giveth heroes strength. Back, with their course reversed, the others pass away: the pious lengthens life with those that are before.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With pressing-stones and with the bright beams of the day he hurls his broadest bolt against the Guileful One. Even he whose hundred wander in his own abode, driving the days afar and bringing them again.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I, to enjoy the beauty of his form, behold that rapid rush of his as 'twere an axe's edge, What time he gives the man who calls on him in fight wealth like a dwelling-house filled full with store of food.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Four-faced and nobly clad, Varuna, urging on the pious to his task, stirs himself with the tongue. Naught by our human nature do we know of him, him from whom Bhaga Savitar bestows the boon.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THIS day I bring God Savitar to meet you, and Bhaga who allots the wealth of mortals. You, Asvins, Heroes rich in treasures, daily seeking your friendship fain would I turn hither.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Knowing full well the Asura's time of coming, worship God Savitar with hymns and praises. Let him who rightly knoweth speak with homage to him who dealeth out man's noblest treasure.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Not for reward doth Pusan send his blessings, Bhaga, or Aditi: his garb is splendour. May Indra, Visniu, Varuna, Mitra, Agni produce auspicious days, the Wonder-Workers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sending the shelter which we ask, the foeless Savitar and the Rivers shall approach us. When I, the sacrifice's priest, invite them, may we he lords of wealth and rich possessions.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They who devote such worship to the Vasus, singing their hymns to Varuna and Mitra, Vouchsafe them ample room, far off be danger. Through grace of Heaven and Earth may we be happy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: LET every mortal man elect the friendship of the guiding God. Each one solicits him for wealth and seeks renown to prosper him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These, leading God, are thine, and these here ready to speak after us. As such may we attain to wealth and wait with services on thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So further honour as our guests the Hero Gods and then the Dames. May he remove and keep afar our foes and all who block our path.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Where fire is set, and swiftly runs the victim dwelling in the trough, He wins, with heroes in his home, friendly to man, like constant streams.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May these thy riches, Leader God! that rule the car, be blest to us, Yea, blest to us for wealth and weal. This will we ponder praising strength, this ponder as we praise the God.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WITH all assistants, Agni, come hither to drink the Soma-juice; With Gods unto our sacred gifts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come to the sacrifice, O ye whose ways are right, whose laws are true, And drink the draught with Agni's tongue.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Singer, with the singers, O Gracious, with those who move at dawn, Come to the Soma-draught with Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To Indra and to Vayu dear, this Soma, by the mortar pressed, Is now poured forth to fill the jar.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Vayu, come hither to the feast, well pleased unto our sacred gifts: Drink of the Soma juice effused come to the food.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye, Indra, Vayu, well deserve to drink the juices pressed by us. Gladly accept them, spotless Pair come to the food.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For Indra and for Vayu pressed are Soma juices blent with curd, As rivers to the lowland flow: come to the food.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Associate with all the Gods, come, with the Asvins and with Dawn, Agni, as erst with Atri, so enjoy the juice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Associate with Varuna, with Mitra, Soma, Visnu, come, Agni, as erstwith Atri, so enjoy the juice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Associate with Vasus, with Adityas, Indra, Viyu, come, Agni as erst with Atri, so enjoy the juice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Bhaga and the Asvins grant us health and wealth, and Goddess Adid and he whom none resist. The Asura Pusan grant us all prosperity, and Heaven and Earth most wise vouchsafe us happiness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let us solicit Vayu for prosperity, and Soma who is Lord of all the world for weal; For weal Brhaspati with all his company. May the Adityas bring us health and happiness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May all the Gods, may Agni the beneficent, God of all men, this day be with us for our weal. Help us the Rbhus, the Divine Ones, for our good. May Rudra bless and keep us from calamity.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Prosper us, Mitra, Varuna. O wealthy Pathya, prosper us. Indra and Agni, prosper us; prosper us thou, O Aditi.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like Sun and Moon may we pursue in full prosperity our path, And meet with one who gives again, -who knows us well and slays us not.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: SING boldly forth, Syavasva, with the Maruts who are loud in song, Who, holy, as their wont is, joy in glory that is free from guile.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For in their boldness they are friends of firm and sure heroic strength. They in their course, bold-spirited, guard all men of their own accord.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like steers in rapid motion they advance and overtake the nights; And thus the Maruts' power in heaven and on the earth we celebrate.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With boldness to your Maruts let us offer laud and sacrifice: Who all, through ages of mankind, guard mortal man from injury.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Praiseworthy, givers of good gifts, Heroes with full and perfect strength - To Maruts, Holy Ones of heaven, will I extol the sacrifice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The lofty Heroes cast their spears and weapons bright with gleaming gold. After these Maruts followed close, like laughing lightning from the sky, a splendour of its own accord.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They who waxed mighty, of the earth, they who are in the wide mid-air, Or in the rivers' compass, or in the abode of ample heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Praise thou the Maruts' company, the valorous and truly strong, The Heroes, hasting, by themselves have yoked their deer for victory.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Fair-gleaming, on Parusni they have clothed themselves in robes of wool, And with their chariot tires they cleave the rock asunder in their might.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whether as wanderers from the way or speeders on or to the path, Under these names the spreading band tend well the sacrifice for me.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To this the Heroes well attend, well do their teams attend to this. Visible are their varied forms. Behold, they are Paravatas.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hymn-singing, seeking water, they, praising, have danced about the spring. What are they unto me? No thieves, but helpers, splendid to behold.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sublime, with lightnings for their spears, Sages and Orderers are they. Rsi, adore that Marut host, and make them happy with thy song.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Rsi, invite the Marut band with offerings, as a maid her friend. From heaven, too, Bold Ones, in your might haste hither glorified with songs.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thinking of these now let him come, as with the escort of the Gods, And with the splendid Princes, famed for rapid courses, to the gifts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Princes, who, when I asked their kin, named Prsni as their Mother-cow, And the impetuous Rudra they, the Mighty Ones, declared their Sire.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The mighty ones, the seven times seven, have singly given me hundred gifts. I have obtained on Yamuna famed wealth in kine and wealth in steeds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who knows the birth of these, or who lived in the Maruts' favour in the days of old What time their spotted deer were yoked?
