verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who, when they stood upon their cars, hath heard them tell the way they went? Who was the bounteous man to whom their kindred rains flowed down with food of sacrifice?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To me they told it, and they came with winged steeds radiant to the draught, Youths, Heroes free from spot or stain: Behold us here and praise thou us;
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who shine self-luminous with ornaments and swords, with breastplates, armlets, and with wreaths, Arrayed on chariots and with bows.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O swift to pour your bounties down, ye Maruts, with delight I look upon your cars, Like splendours coming through the rain.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Munificent Heroes, they have cast heaven's treasury down for the worshipper's behoof: They set the storm-cloud free to stream through both the worlds, and rain floods flow o'er desert spots.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The bursting streams m billowy flood have spread abroad, like milch-kine, o'er the firmament. Like swift steeds hasting to their journey's resting-place, to every side run glittering brooks.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hither, O Maruts, come from heaven, from mid-air, or from near at hand Tarry not far away from us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So let not Rasa, Krumu, or Anitabha, Kubha, or Sindhu hold you back. Let not the watery Sarayti obstruct your way. With us be all the bliss ye give.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: That brilliant gathering of your cars, the company of Maruts, of the Youthful Ones, The rain-showers, speeding on, attend.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With eulogies and hymns may we follow your army, troop by troop, and band by band, And company by company.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To what oblation-giver, sprung of noble ancestry, have sped The Maruts on this course to-day?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Vouchsafe to us the bounty, that which we implore, through which, for child and progeny, Ye give the seed of corn that wasteth not away, and bliss that reacheth to all life.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May we in safety pass by those who slander us, leaving behind disgrace and hate. Maruts, may we be there when ye, at dawn, in rest and toil, rain waters down and balm.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Favoured by Gods shall he the man, O Heroes, Maruts! and possessed of noble sons, Whom ye protect. Such may we be.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Praise the Free-givers. At this liberal patron's rite they joy like cattle in the mead. So call thou unto them who come as ancient Friends: hymn those who love thee with a song.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THIS hymn will I make for the Marut host who bright in native splendour cast the mountains down. Sing the great strength of those illustrious in renown, who stay the heat, who sacrifice on heights of heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Maruts, rich in water, strengtheners of life are your strong bands with harnessed steeds, that wander far. Trita roars out at him who aims the lightning-flash. The waters sweeping round are thundering on their way.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They gleam with lightning, Heroes, Casters of the Stone, wind-rapid Maruts, overthrowers of the bills, Oft through desire to rain coming with storm of hail, roaring in onset, violent and exceeding strong.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When, mighty Rudras, through the nights and through the days, when through the sky and realms of air, shakers of all, When over the broad fields ye drive along like ships, e'en to strongholds ye come, Maruts, but are not harmed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Maruts, this hero strength and majesty of yours hath, like the Sun, extended o'er a lengthened way, When in your course like deer with splendour unsubdued ye bowed the hill that gives imperishable rain.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bright shone your host, ye Sages, Maruts, when ye smote the waving tree as when the worm consumeth it. Accordant, as the eye guides him who walks, have ye led our devotion onward by an easy path.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Never is he, O Maruts, slain or overcome, never doth he decay ne'er is distressed or harmed; His treasures, his resources, never waste away, whom. whether he be prince or Rsi, ye direct.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With harnessed team like heroes overcoming troops, the friendly Maruts, laden with their water-casks, Let the spring flow, and when impetuous' they roar they inundate the earth with floods of pleasant meath.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Free for the Maruts is the earth with sloping ways, free for the rushing Ones is heaven with steep descents. The paths of air's mid-region are precipitous, precipitous the mountains with their running streams.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When, as the Sun hath risen up, ye take delight, O bounteous radiant Maruts, Heroes of the sky, Your coursers weary not when speeding on their way, and rapidly ye reach the end of this your path.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Lances are on your shoulders, anklets on your feet, gold chains are on your breasts, gems, Maruts, on your car. Lightnings aglow with flame are flashing in your hands, and visors wrought of gold are laid upon your heads.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Maruts, in eager stir ye shake the vault of heaven, splendid beyond conception, for its shining fruit. They gathered when they let their deeds of might flash forth. The Pious Ones send forth a far-resounding shout.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sage Maruts, may we be the drivers of the car of riches full of life that have been given by you. O Maruts, let that wealth in thousands dwell with us which never vanishes like Tisya from the sky.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Maruts, ye further wealth with longed for heroes, further the Rsi skilled in chanted verses. Ye give the Bharata as his strength, a charger, and ye bestow a king who quickly listens.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Of you, most swift to succour! I solicit wealth wherewith we may spread forth mid men like as the Sun. Accept, O Maruts, graciously this hymn of mine that we may live a hundred winters through its power.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WITH gleaming lances, with their breasts adorned with gold, the Maruts, rushing onward, hold high power of life. They hasten with swift steeds easy to be controlled. Their cars moved onward as they went to victory.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye, as ye wist, have gained of your own selves your power: high, O ye Mighty Ones, and wide ye shine abroad. They with their strength have even measured out the sky. Their cars moved onward as they went to victory.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Strong, born together, they together have waxed great: the Heroes more and more have grown to majesty Resplendent as the Sun's beams in their light are they. Their cars moved onward as they went to victory.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Maruts, your mightiness deserves to be adored, sight to be longed for like the shining of the Sun. So lead us with your aid to immortality. Their cars moved onward as they went to victory.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Maruts, from the Ocean ye uplift the rain, and fraught with vaporous moisture pour the torrents down. Never, ye Wonder-Workers, are your Milch-kine dry. Their cars moved onward as they went to victory.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When to your car-poles ye have yoked your spotted deer to be your steeds, and put your golden mantles on, O Maruts, ye disperse all enemies abroad. Their cars moved onward as they went to victory.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Neither the mountains nor the rivers keep you back: whither ye have resolved thither ye, Maruts, go. Ye compass round about even the heaven and earth. Their cars moved onward as they went to victory. Whate'er is ancient, Maruts, what of recent time, whate'er is spoken, Vasus, what is chanted forth, They who take cognizance of all of this are ye. Their cars moved onward as they went to victory.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Be gracious unto us, ye Maruts, slay us not extend ye unto us shelter of many a sort. Pay due regard unto our friendship and our praise. Their cars moved onward as they went to victory.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Maruts, lead us on to higher fortune deliver us, when lauded, from afflictions. Accept, ye Holy Ones, the gifts we bring you. May we be masters of abundant riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: AGNI, that valorous company adorned with ornaments of gold, The people of the Maruts, I call down to-day even from the luminous realm of heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Even as thou thinkest in thy heart, thither my wishes also tend. Those who have come most near to thine invoking calls, strengthen them fearful to behold.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Earth, like a bounteous lady, liberal of her gifts, struck down and shaken, yet exultant, comes to us. Impetuous as a bear, O Maruts, is you rush terrible as a dreadful bull..
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They who with mighty strength o'erthrow like oxen difficult to yoke, Cause e'en the heavenly stone to shake ' yea, shake the rocky mountain as they race along.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Rise up! even now with lauds I call the very numerous company, Unequalled, of these Maruts, like a herd of kine, grown up together in their strength.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bind to your car the bright red mares, yoke the red coursers to your car. Bind to the pole, to draw, the fleet-foot tawny steeds, the best at drawing, to the pole.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yea, and this loudly-neighing bright red vigorous horse who hath been stationed, fair to see, Let him not cause delay, O Maruts,, in your course, urge ye him onward in your cars.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Maruts' chariot, ever fain to gather glory, we invoke, Which Rodasi hath mounted, bringing pleasant gifts, with Maruts in her company.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I call that brilliant band of yours, adorable, rapid on the car Whereon the bounteous Dame, auspicious, nobly born, shows glorious with the Marut host.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: OF one accord, with Indra, O ye Rudras, come borne on your golden car for our prosperity. An offering from us, this hymn is brought to you, as, unto one who thirsts for water, heavenly springs.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Armed with your daggers, full of wisdom, armed with spears, armed with your quivers, armed with arrows, with good bows, Good horses and good cars have ye, O Prsni's Sons: ye, Maruts, with good weapons go to victory.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: From hills and heaven ye shake wealth for the worshipper: in terror at your coming low the woods bow down. Ye make the earth to tremble, Sons of Prsni, when for victory ye have yoked, fierce Ones! your spotted deer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bright with the blasts of wind, wrapped in their robes of rain, like twins of noble aspect and of lovely form, The Maruts, spotless, with steeds tawny hued and red, strong in their mightiness and spreading wide like heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Rich in adornment, rich in drops, munificent, bright in their aspect, yielding bounties that endure, Noble by birth, adorned with gold upon their breasts, the Singers of the sky have won immortal fame.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Borne on both shoulders, O ye Maruts, are your spears: within your arms is laid your energy and 3trength. Bold thoughts are in your heads, your weapons in your cars, all glorious majesty is moulded on your forms.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Vouchsafe to us, O Maruts, splendid bounty in cattle and in steeds, in cars and heroes. Children of Rudra, give us high distinction: may I enjoy your Godlike help and favour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ho! Maruts, Heroes, skilled in Law, immortal, be gracious unto us, ye rich in treasures, Ye hearers of the truth, ye sage and youthful, grown mighty, dwelling on the lofty mountains.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now do I glorify their mighty cohort, the company of these the youthful Maruts, Who ride impetuous on with rapid horses, and radiant in themselves, are Lords of Amrta.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The mighty glittering band, arm-bound with bracelets, givers of bliss, unmeasured in their greatness, With magical powers, bountiful, ever-roaring,-these, liberal Heroes, venerate thou singer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This day may all your water-bringers, Maruts, they who impel the falling rain, approach us. This fire, O Maruts, hath been duly kindled; let it find favour with you, youthful Sages.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye raise up for the folk an active ruler whom, Holy Ones! a Master's hand hath fashioned. Ye send the fighter hand to hand, armmighty, and the brave hero, Maruts with good horses.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They spring forth more and more, strong in their glories, like days, like spokes where none are last in order. Highest and mightiest are the Sons of Prsni. Firm to their own intention cling the Maruts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When ye have hastened on with spotted coursers, O Maruts, on your cars with strong-wrought fellies, The waters are disturbed, the woods are shattered. Let Dyaus the Red Steer send his thunder downward.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Even Earth hath spread herself wide at their coming, and they as husbands have with power impregned her. They to the pole have yoked the winds for coursers: their sweat have they made rain, these Sons of Rudra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ho! Maruts, Heroes, skilled in Law, immortal, be gracious unto us, ye rich in treasures, Ye hearers of the truth, ye sage and youthful, grown mighty, dwelling on the lofty mountains.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: YOUR spy hath called to you to give prosperity. I sing to Heaven and Earth and offer sacrifice. They bathe their steeds and hasten through the firmament: they spread abroad their radiance through the sea of cloud.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Earth shakes and reels in terror at their onward rush, like a full ship which, quivering, lets the water in. Marked on their ways are they, visible from afar: the Heroes press between in mighty armament.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As the exalted horn of bulls for splendid might, as the Sun's eye set in the firmament's expanse, Like vigorous horses ye are beauteous to behold, and for your glory show like bridegrooms, O ye Men.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who, O ye Maruts, may attain the mighty lore of you the mighty, who may reach your manly deeds? Ye, verily, make earth tremble like a ray of light what time ye bring your boons to give prosperity,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like steeds of ruddy colour, scions of one race, as foremost champions they have battled in the van. The Heroes have waxed strong like we.1grown manly youths; with floods of rain they make the Sun's eye fade away,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Having no eldest and no youngest in their band, no middlemost, preeminent they have waxed in might, These Sons of Prsni, sprung of noble ancestry: come hitherward to us, ye bridegrooms of the sky.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like birds of air they flew with might in lengthened lines from heaven's high ridges to the borders of the sky. The steeds who carry them, as Gods and mortals know, have caused the waters of the mountains to descend.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Dyaus, the Infinite, roar for our banquet: may Dawns toil for us, glittering with moisture. Lauded by thee, these Maruts, Sons o Rudra, O Rsi, have sent down the heavenly treasure.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I LAUD with reverence the gracious Agni: here may he sit and part our meed among us. As with spoil-seeking cars I bring oblation: turned rightward I will swell the Marut's, praise-song.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Maruts, yea, the Rudras, who have mounted their famous spotted deer and cars swift-moving,- Before you, fierce Ones! woods bow down in terror: Earth, even the mountain, trembles at your coming.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Though vast and tall, the mountain is affrighted, the height of heaven is shaken at your roaring When, armed with lances, ye are sporting, Maruts, and rush along together like the waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They, like young suitors, sons of wealthy houses, have with their golden natures decked their bodies. Strong on their cars, the lordly Ones, for glory, have set their splendours on their forms for ever.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: None being eldest, none among them youngest, as brothers they have grown to happy fortune. May their Sire Rudra, young and deft, and Prsni pouring much milk, bring fair days to the Maruts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whether, O blessed Maruts, ye be dwelling in highest, midmost, or in lowest heaven, Thence, O ye Rudras, and thou also, Agni, notice the sacrificial food we offer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Maruts, Lords of all, when Agni and when ye drive downward from sublimest heaven along the heights, Shakers of all, rejoicing, slayers of the foe, give riches to the Soma-pressing worshipper.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Agni, with the Maruts as they gleam and sing, gathered in troop, rejoicing drink the Soma juice; With these the living ones who cleanse and further all, joined with thy banner, O Vaisvanara, from of old.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O HEROES lordliest of all, who are ye that have singly come Forth from a region most remote?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Where are your horses, where the reins? How came ye? how had ye the power? Rein was on nose and seat on back.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The whip is laid upon the flank. The heroes stretch their thighs apart, Like women when the babe is born.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Go ye, O Heroes, far away, ye bridegrooms with a lovely Spouse That ye may warm you at the fire.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May she gain cattle for her meed, hundreds of sheep and steeds and kine, Who threw embracing arms around the hero whom Gyavaiva praised.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yea, many a woman is more firm and better than the man who turns Away from Gods, and offers not.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: She who discerns the weak and worn, the man who thirsts and is in want She sets her mind upon the Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And yet full many a one, unpraised, mean niggard, is entitled man: Only in were gild is he such.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And she, the young, the joyous-spirited, divulged the path to Syava, yea, to me. Two red steeds carried me to Purumilha's side, that sage of far-extended fame,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him who, like Vaidadasvi, like Taranta, hath bestowed on me A hundred cows in liberal gift.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They who are borne by rapid steeds, drinking the meath that gives delight, They have attained high glories here.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They by whose splendour both the worlds are over-spread they shine on cars As the gold gleams above in heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: That Marut band is ever young, borne on bright cars, unblamable, Moving to victory, checked by none.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who knoweth, verily, of these where the All-shakers take delight, Born, spotless, after sacred Law?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Guides are ye, lovers of the song to mortal man through holy hymn, And hearers when he cries for help.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Do ye, destroyers of the foe, worshipful and exceeding bright, Send down the treasures that we crave.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: OUrmya, bear thou far away to Darbhya this my hymn of praise, Songs, Goddess, as if chariot-borne.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: From me to Rathaviti say, when he hath pressed the Soma juice, The wish I had departeth not.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This wealthy Rathaviti dwells among the people rich in kine, Among the mountains, far withdrawn.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: BY your high Law firm order is established there where they loose for travel Surya's horses. Ten hundred stood together: there I looked on this the most marvellous Deities' one chief glory.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This, Mitra-Varuna, is your special greatness: floods that stood there they with the days attracted. Ye cause to flow all voices of the cow pen: your single chariot felly hath rolled hither.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Mitra-Varuna, ye by your greatness, both Kings, have firmly stablished earth and heaven, Ye caused the cows to stream, the plants to flourish, and, scattering swift drops, sent down the rain-flood.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let your well-harnessed horses bear you hither: hitherward let them come with reins drawn tightly. A covering cloud of sacred oil attends you, and your streams flow to us from days aforetime.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To make the lustre wider and more famous, guarding the sacred grass with veneration, Ye, Mitra-Varuna, firm, strong, awe-inspiring, are seated on a throne amid oblations.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With hands that shed no blood, guarding the pious, whom, Varuni3, ye save amid oblations. Ye Twain, together, Kings of willing spirit, uphold dominion based on thousand pillars.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Adorned with gold, its columns are of iron. in heaven it glitters like a whip for horses; Or stablished on a field deep-spoiled and fruitful. So may we share the meath that loads your car-seat.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye mount your car gold-hued at break of morning, and iron-pillared when the Sun is setting, And from that place, O Varuna and Mitra, behold infinity and limitation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bountiful guardians of the world! the shelter that is impenetrable, strongest, flawless, Aid us with that, O Varuna and Mitra, and when we long to win may we be victors.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: GUARDIANS of Order, ye whose Laws are ever true, in the sublimest heaven your chariot ye ascend. O Mitra-Varuna whomsoe'er ye: favour, here, to him the rain with sweetness streameth down from heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This world's imperial Kings, O Mitra-Varuna, ye rule in holy synod, looking on the light. We pray for rain, your boon, and immortality. Through heaven and over earth the thunderers take their way.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Imperial Kings, strong, Heroes, Lords of earth and heaven, Mitra and Varuna, ye ever active Ones, Ye wait on thunder with the many-tinted clouds, and by the Asura's magic power cause Heaven to rain.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Your magic, Mitra-Varuna, resteth in the heaven. The Sun, the wondrous weapon, cometh forth as light. Ye hide him in the sky with cloud and flood of rain, and water-drops, Parjanya! full of sweetness flow.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Maruts yoke their easy car for victory, O Mitra-Varuna, as a hero in the wars. The thunderers roam through regions varied in their hues. Imperial Kings, bedew us with the milk of heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Refreshing is your voice, O Mitra-Varuna: Parjanya sendeth out a wondrous mighty voice. With magic power the Maruts clothe them with the clouds. Ye Two cause Heaven to rain, the red, the spotless One.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wise, with your Law and through the Asura's magic power ye guard the ordinances, Mitra-Varuna. Ye by eternal Order govern all the world. Ye set the Sun in heaven as a refulgent car.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: You, foeman-slaying Varuna and Mitra, we invoke with song, Who, as with penfold of your arms, encompass round the realm of light.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Stretch out your arms with favouring love unto this man who singeth hymns, For in all places is sung forth your ever gracious friendliness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: That I may gain a refuge now, may my steps be on Mitra's path. Men go protected in the charge of this dear Friend who harms us not.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Mitra and Varuna, from you may I, by song, win noblest meed. That shall stir envy in the homes of wealthy chiefs and those who praise.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With your fair splendours, Varuna and Mitra, to our gathering come, That in their homes the wealthy chiefs and they who are your friends may thrive.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With those, moreover, among whom ye hold your high supremacy, Vouchsafe us room that we may win strength for prosperity and wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When morning flushes, Holy Ones! in the Gods' realm where white Cows shine, Supporting Arcananas, speed, ye Heroes, with your active feet hither to my pressed Soma juice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: FULL wise is he who hath discerned: let him speak to us of the Gods,— The man whose praise-songs Varuṇa the beautiful, or Mitra, loves.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For they are Kings of noblest might, of glorious fame most widely spread; Lords of the brave, who strengthen Law, the Holy Ones with every race.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Approaching you with prayer for aid, together I address you first We who have good steeds call on you, Most Sage, to give us strength besides.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: E’en out of misery Mitra gives a way to dwelling at our case, For he who worships hath the grace of Mitra, fighter in the van. '
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In Mitra's shelter that extends to utmost distance may we dwell, Unmenaced, guarded by the care, ever as sons of Varuṇa.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye, Mitra, urge this people on, and to one end direct their ways. Neglect not ye the wealthy chiefs, neglect not us the Ṛṣis: be our guardians when ye quaff the milk.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O SAPIENT man, call the Two Gods, the very wise, who slay the foe. For Varuna, whose form is Law, place offerings for his great delight.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For they have won unbroken sway in full perfection, power divine. And, like high laws, the world of man hath been made beautiful as light.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Therefore we praise you that your cars may travel far in front of ours- You who accept the eulogy of Ratahavya with his hymns.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And ye show whom, Wondrous Gods with fulness of intelligence. By men's discernment are ye marked, O ye whose might is purified.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This is the Law sublime, O Earth: to aid the Rsis' toil for fame The Two, wide-spreading, are prepared. They come with ample overflow.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Mitra, ye Gods with wandering eyes, would that the worshippers and we Might strive to reach the realm ye rule, most spacious and protected well,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: YE Gods, Adityas, Varuna, Aryaman, Mitra, verily Have here obtained supremest sway, high, holy, set apart for you.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When, Varuna and Mitra, ye sit in your golden dwelling-place, Ye Twain, supporters of mankind, foe slayers, give felicity.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: All these, possessors of all wealth, Varuna, Mitra, Aryaman, Follow their ways, as if with feet, and guard from injury mortal man.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For they are true, they cleave to Law, held holy among every race, Good leaders, bounteous in their gifts, deliverers even from distress.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Which of your persons, Varuna or Mitra, merits not our praise? Therefore our thought is turned to you, the Atris' thought is turned to you.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: SING forth unto your Varuna and Mitra with a song inspired. They, Mighty Lords, are lofty Law
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Full springs of fatness, Sovran Kings, Mitra. and Varuna, the Twain, Gods glorified among the Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So help ye us to riches, great terrestrial and celestial wealth: Vast is your sway among the Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Carefully tending Law with Law they have attained their vigorous might. The two Gods wax devoid of guile.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With rainy skies and streaming floods, Lords of the strength that bringeth gifts, A lofty seat have they attained.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THREE spheres of light, O Varuna, three heavens, three firmaments ye comprehend, O Mitra: Waxed strong, ye keep the splendour of dominion, guarding the Ordinance that lasts for ever.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye, Varuna, have kine who yield refreshment; Mitra, your floods pour water full of sweetness. There stand the Three Steers, splendid in their brightness, who fill the three world-bowls with genial moisture.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I call at dawn on Aditi the Goddess, I call at noon and when the Sun is setting. I pray, O Mitra-Varuna, for safety, for wealth and progeny, in rest and trouble.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye who uphold the region, sphere of brightness, ye who support earth's realm Divine Adityas, The Immortal Gods, O Varuna and Mitra, never impair your everlasting statutes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: EVEN far and wide, O Varuna and Mitra, doth your grace extend. May I obtain your kind good-will.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: From you, benignant Gods, may we gain fully food for sustenance. Such, O ye Rudras, my we be.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Guard us, O Rudras. with your guard save us, ye skilled to save, my we Subdue the Dasyus, we ourselves,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Or ne'er may we, O Wondrous Strong, enjoy another's solemn feast, Ourselves, our sons, or progeny.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Varuna and Mitra, ye who slay the foemen, come with might To this our goodly sacrifice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For, Varuna and Mitra, ye Sages are Rulers over all. Fill full our songs, for this ye can.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come to the juice that we have pressed. Varuna, Mitra, come to drink This Soma of the worshipper.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To Varuna and Mitra we offer with songs, as Atri did. Sit on the sacred grass to drink the Soma juice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: By Ordinance and Law ye dwell in peace secure, bestirring men. Sit on the sacred grass to drink the Soma juice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Varuna and Mitra, for our help, accept the sacrifice. Sit on the sacred grass to drink the Soma juice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WHETHER, O Asvins, ye this day be far remote or near at hand, In many spots or in mid-air, come hither, Lords of ample wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These here, who show o'er widest space, bringing full many a wondrous act, Resistless, lovingly I seek, I call the Mightiest to enjoy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Another beauteous wheel have ye fixed there to decorate your car. With others through the realms ye roam in might unto the neighbouring tribes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: That deed of yours that is extolled, Visvas! hath all been done with this. Born otherwise, and spotless, ye have entered kinship's bonds with us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When Surya mounted on your car that rolls for ever rapidly, Birds of red hue were round about and burning splendours compassed you.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Atri bethinks himself of you, O Heroes, with a friendly mind, What time, Nasatyas, with his mouth he stirs the spotless flame for you.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Strong is your swiftly moving steed, famed his exertion in the course When by your great deeds, Asvins, Chiefs, Atri is brought to us again.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Lovers of sweetness, Rudras, she who streams with sweetness waits on you. When ye have travelled through the seas men bring you gifts of well-dressed food.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Asvins, with truth they call you Twain bestowers of felicity; At sacrifice most prompt to hear, most gracious ye at sacrifice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Most pleasing to the Asvins be these prayers which magnify their might, Which we have fashioned, even as cars high reverence have we spoken forth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WHERE in the heavens are ye to-day, Gods, Asvins, rich in constancy? Hear this, ye excellent as Steers: Atri inviteth you to come.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Where are they now? Where are the Twain, the famed Nasatyas, Gods in heaven? Who is the man ye strive to reach? Who of your suppliants is with you?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whom do ye visit, whom approach? to whom direct your harnessed car? With whose devotions are ye pleased? We long for you to further us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye, Strengtheners, for Paura stir the filler swimming in the flood, Advancing to be captured like a lion to the ambuscade.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye from Cyavana worn with age removed his skin as 'twere a robe. So, when ye made him young again, he stirred the longing of a dame.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Here is the man who lauds you both: to see your glory are we here. Now bear me, come with saving help, ye who are rich in store of wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who among many mortal men this day hath won you to himself? What bard, accepters of the bard? Who, rich in wealth! with sacrifice?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Asvins, may your car approach, most excellent of cars for speed. Through many regions may our praise pass onward among mortal men.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May our laudation of you Twain, lovers of meath! be sweet to you. Fly hitherward, ye wise of heart, like falcons with your winged steeds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Asvins, when at any time ye listen to this call of mine, For you is dainty food prepared: they mix refreshing food for you.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To meet your treasure-bringing car, the mighty car most dear to us, Asvins, the Rsi is prepared, your raiser, with his song of praise. Lovers of sweetness, hear my call.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Pass, O ye Asvins, pass away beyond all tribes of selfish men, Wonderful, with your golden paths, most gracious, bringers of the flood. Lovers of sweetness, hear my call.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come to us, O ye Asvin Pair, bringing your precious treasures, come Ye Rudras, on your paths of gold, rejoicing, rich in store of wealth. Lovers of sweetness, hear my call.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O strong and Good, the voice of him who lauds you well cleaves to your car. And that great beast, your chariot-steed, fair, wonderful, makes dainty food. Lovers of sweetness, hear my call.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Watchful in spirit, born on cars, impetuous, listing to his cry, Asvins, with winged steeds ye speed down to Cyavana void of guile. Lovers of sweetness, hear my call.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hither, O Heroes, let your steeds, of dappled hue, yoked at the thought, Your flying steeds, O Asvins, bring you hitherward, with bliss, to drink. Lovers of sweetness, hear my call.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Asvins, hither come to us; Nasatyas, be not disinclined. Through longing for the pious turn out of the way to reach our home. Lovers of sweetness, bear my call.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye Lords of Splendour, free from guile, come, stand at this our sacrifice. Beside the singer, Asvins, who longs for your grace and lauds you both. Lovers of sweetness, hear my call.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Dawn with her white herd hath appeared, and in due time hath fire been placed. Harnessed is your immortal car, O Wonder Workers, strong and kind. Lovers of sweetness, bear my call.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: AGNI, the bright face of the Dawns, is shining; the singers' pious voices have ascended. Borne on your chariot, Asvins, turn you hither and come unto our full and rich libation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Most frequent guests, they scorn not what is ready: even now the lauded Asvins are beside us. With promptest aid they come at morn and evening, the worshipper's most blessed guards from trouble.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yea, come at milking-time, at early morning, at noon of day and when the Sun is setting, By day, by night, with favour most auspicious. Not only now the draught hath drawn the Asvins.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For this place, Asvins, was of old your dwelling, these were your houses, this your habitation. Come to us from high heaven and from the mountain. Come from the waters bringing food and vigour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May we obtain the Asvins' newest favour, and gain their health-bestowing happy guidance. Bring riches hither unto us, and heroes, and all felicity and joy, Immortals!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: FIRST worship those who come at early morning: let the Twain drink before the giftless niggard. The Asvins claim the sacrifice at daybreak: the sages yielding the first share extol them.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Worship at dawn and instigate the Asvins: nor is the worshipper at eve rejected. Besides ourselves another craves and worships: each first in worship is most highly favoured.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Covered with gold, meath-tinted, dropping fatness, your chariot with its freight of food comes hither, Swift as thought, Asvins, rapid as the tempest, wherewith ye travel over all obstructions.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who hath served most often the Nasatyas, and gives the sweetest food at distribution, Furthers with his own holy works his offspring, and ever passes those whose flames ascend not.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May we obtain the Asvins' newest favour, and gain their health-bestowing happy guidance. Bring riches hither unto us, and heroes, and all felicity and joy, Immortals!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: YE Asvins, hither come to us: Nasatyas, be not disinclined. Fly hither like two swans unto the juice we shed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Asvins, like a pair of deer, like two wild cattle to the mead: Fly hither like two swans unto the juice we shed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Asvins rich in gifts, accept our sacrifice to prosper it: Fly hither like two swans unto the juice we shed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As Atri when descending to the cave called on you loudly like a wailing woman. Ye came to him, O Asvins, with the freshest and most auspicious fleetness of a falcon.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Tree, part asunder like the side of her who bringeth forth a child. Ye Asvins, listen to my call: loose Saptavadhri from his bonds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For Saptavadhri, for the seer affrighted when he wept and waffled, Ye, Asvins, with your magic powers rent up the tree and shattered it.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like as the wind on every side ruffles a pool of lotuses, So stir in thee the babe unborn, so may the ten-month babe descend.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like as the wind, like as the wood, like as the sea is set astir, So also, ten-month babe, descend together with the after-birth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The child who hath for ten months' time been lying in his mother's side,- May he come forth alive, unharmed, yea, living from the living dame.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O HEAVENLY Dawn, awaken us to ample opulence to-day Even as thou hast wakened us with Satyasravas, Vayya's son, high-born! delightful with thy steeds!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Daughter of Heaven, thou dawnedst on Sunitha Sucadratha's son, So dawn thou on one mightier still, on Satyasravas, Vayya's son, high-born! delightful with thy steeds!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So, bringing treasure, dawn to-day on us thou Daughter of the Sky, As thou, O mightier yet. didst shine for Satyatravas, Vayya's son, high-born! delightful with thy steeds!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Here round about thee are the priests who laud thee, Bright One, with their hymns, And men with gifts, O Bounteous Dame, splendid with wealth and offering much, high-born! delightful with thy steeds!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whatever these thy bands perform to please thee or to win them wealth, E'en fain they gird us round and give rich gifts which ne'er are left away, high-born! delightful with thy steeds!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Give to these wealthy patrons fame, O affluent Dawn, with hero sons, To these our princes who have brought rich gifts ne'er to be left away, highborn! delightful with thy steeds!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bring lofty and resplendent fame, O thou munificent Dawn, to these Our wealthy patrons who bestow rich gifts on us of steeds and kine, high-born! delightful with thy steeds!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bring us, O Daughter of the Sky, subsistence in our herds of kine, Together with the sunbeams, with the shine of pure refulgent flames, highborn! delightful with thy steeds!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Daughter of the Sky, shine forth; delay not to perform thy task. Let not the Sun with fervent heat consume thee like a robber foe, high-born! delightful with the steeds!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So much, and more exceedingly, O Dawn, it suits thee to bestow, Thou Radiant One who ceasest not to shine for those who sing thy praise, highborn! delightful with thy steeds!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THE singers welcome with their hymns and praises the Goddess Dawn who bringeth in the sunlight, Sublime, by Law true to eternal Order, bright on her path, red-tinted, far-refulgent.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: She comes in front, fair, rousing up the people, making the pathways easy to be travelled. High, on her lofty chariot, all-impelling, Dawn gives her splendour at the days' beginning.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: She, harnessing her car with purple oxen. injuring none, hath brought perpetual riches. Opening paths to happiness, the Goddess shines, praised by all, giver of every blessing.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With changing tints she gleams in double splendour while from the eastward she displays her body. She travels perfectly the path of Order, nor fails to reach, as one who knows, the quarters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As conscious that her limbs are bright with bathing, she stands, as 'twere, erect that we may see her. Driving away malignity and darkness, Dawn, Child of Heaven, hath come to us with lustre.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Daughter of the Sky, like some chaste woman, bends, opposite to men, her forehead downward. The Maid, disclosing boons to him who worships, hath brought again the daylight as aforetime.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THE priests of him the lofty Priest well-skilled in hymns harness their spirit, yea, harness their holy thoughts. He only knowing works assigns their priestly tasks. Yea, lofty is the praise of Savitar the God.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Sapient One arrays himself in every form: for quadruped and biped he hath brought forth good. Excellent Savitar hath looked on heaven's high vault, and shineth after the outgoing of the Dawn.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Even he, the God whose going-forth and majesty the other Deities have followed with their might, He who hath measured the terrestrial regions out by his great power, he is the Courser Savitar.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To the three spheres of light thou goest, Savitar, and with the rays of Sidrya thou combinest thee. Around, on both sides thou encompassest the night: yea, thou, O God, art Mitra through thy righteous laws.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Over all generation thou art Lord alone: Pusan art thou, O God, in all thy goings-forth. Yea, thou hast domination over all this world. Syavasva hath brought praise to thee, O Savitar,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WE crave of Savitar the God this treasure much to be enjoyed. The best, all-yielding, conquering gift of Bhaga we would gladly win.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Savitar's own supremacy, most glorious and beloved of all, No one diminisheth in aught.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For Savitar who is Bhaga shall send riches to his worshipper. That wondrous portion we implore.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Send us this day, God Savitar, prosperity with progeny. Drive thou the evil dream away.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Savitar, God, send far away all sorrows and calamities, And send us only what is good.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sinless in sight of Aditi through the God Savitar's influence, May we obtain all lovely things.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We with our hymns this day elect the general God, Lord of the good, Savitar whose decrees are true.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who for ever vigilant precedes these Twain, the Day and Night, Is Savitar the thoughtful God.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who gives glory unto all these living creatures with the song, And brings them forth, is Savitar.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: SING with these songs thy welcome to the Mighty, with adoration praise and call Parjanya. The Bull, loud roaring, swift to send his bounty, lays in the plants the seed. for germination.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He smites the trees apart, he slays the demons: all life fears him who wields the mighty weapon. From him exceeding strong faces e'en the guiltless, when thundering Parjanya smites the wicked.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like a car-driver whipping on his horses, he makes the messengers of rain spring forward. Far off resounds the roaring of the lion, what time Parjanya fills the sky with rain-cloud.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Forth burst the winds, down come the lightning-flashes: the plants shoot up, the realm of light is streaming. Food springs abundant for all living creatures, what time Parjanya quickens earth with moisture.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou at whose bidding earth bows low before thee, at whose command hoofed cattle fly in terror, At whose behest the plants assume all colours, even thou Parjanya, yield us great protection.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Send down for us the rain of heaven, ye Maruts, and let the Stallion's flood descend in torrents. Come hither with this thunder while thou pourest the waters down, our heavenly Lord and Father.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thunder and roar: the germ of life deposit. Fly round us on thy chariot waterladen. Thine opened water-skin draw with thee downward, and let the hollows and the heights be level.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Lift up the mighty vessel, pour down water, and let the liberated streams rush forward. Saturate both the earth and heaven with fatness, and for the cows let there be drink abundant.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When thou, with thunder and with roar, Parjanya, smitest sinners down, This universe exults thereat, yea, all that is upon the earth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou hast poured down the rain-flood now withhold it. Thou hast made desert places fit for travel. Thou hast made herbs to grow for our enjoyment: yea, thou hast won thee praise from living creatures.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THOU, of a truth, O Prthivi, bearest the tool that rends the hills: Thou rich in torrents, who with might quickenest earth, O Mighty One.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To thee, O wanderer at will, ring out the lauds with beams of day, Who drivest, like a neighing steed, the swelling cloud, O bright of hue.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who graspest with thy might on earth. e'en the strong sovrans of the wood, When from the lightning of thy cloud the rain-floods of the heaven descend.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: SING forth a hymn sublime and solemn, grateful to glorious. Varuna, imperial Ruler, Who hath struck out, like one who slays the victim, earth as a skin to spread in front of Surya.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In the tree-tops the air he hath extended, put milk in kine and vigorous speed in horses, Set intellect in hearts, fire in the waters, Surya in heaven and Soma on the mountain.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Varuna lets the big cask, opening downward, flow through the heaven and earth and air's mid-region. Therewith the universe's Sovran waters earth as the shower of rain bedews the barley.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When Varuna is fain for milk he moistens the sky, the land, and earth to her foundation. Then straight the mountains clothe them in the rain-cloud: the Heroes, putting forth their vigour, loose them.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I will declare this mighty deed of magic, of glorious Varuna the Lord Immortal, Who standing in the firmament hath meted the earth out with the Sun as with a measure.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: None, verily, hath ever let or hindered this the most wise God's mighty deed of magic, Whereby with all their flood, the lucid rivers fill not one sea wherein they pour their waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: If we have sinned against the man who loves us, have ever wronged a brother, friend, or comrade, The neighbour ever with us, or a stranger, O Varuna, remove from us the trespass.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: If we, as gamesters cheat at play, have cheated, done wrong unwittingly or sinned of purpose, Cast all these sins away like loosened fetters, and, Varuna let us be thine own beloved.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THE mortal man whom ye, the Twain, Indra and Agni, help in fight, Breaks through e'en strongly-guarded wealth as Trta burst his way through reeds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Twain invincible in war, worthy to be renowned in frays, Lords of the Fivefold. People, these, Indra and Agni, we invoke.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Impetuous is their strength, and keen the lightning of the mighty Pair, Which from their arms speeds with the car to Vrtra's slayer for the kine.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra and Agni, we invoke you both, as such, to send your cars: Lords of quick-coming bounty, ye who know, chief lovers of the song.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These who give increase day by day, Gods without guile for mortal man, Worthy themselves, I honour most, Two Gods as partners, for my horse.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The strength-bestowing offering thus to Indra-Agni hath been paid, as butter, purified by stones. Deal to our princes high renown, deal wealth to those who sing your praise, deal food to those who sing your praise.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To Visnu, to the Mighty whom the Maruts follow let your hymns born in song go forth, Evayamarut; To the impetuous, strong band, adorned with bracelets, that rushes on in joy and ever roars for vigour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They who with might were manifest, and who willingly by their own knowledge told it forth, Evayamarut. Maruts, this strength of yours no wisdom comprehendeth: through their gifts' greatness they are moveless as the mountains.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who by the psalm they sing are heard, from lofty heaven, the strong, the brightly shining Ones, Evayamarut; In whose abode there is no mightier one to move them, whose lightnings are as fires, who urge the roaring rivers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He of the Mighty Stride forth strode, Evayamarut, out of the spacious dwelling-place, their home in common. When he, himself, hath yoked his emulous strong horses on heights, he cometh forth, joy-giving, with the Heroes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like your tremendous roar, the rainer with light flashing, strong, speeding, hath made all tremble, Evayamarut, Wherewith victorious ye, self-luminous, press onward, with strong reins, decked with gold, impetuous and well-weaponed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Unbounded is your greatness, ye of mighty power: may your bright vigour be our aid, Evayamarut; For ye are visible helpers in the time of trouble: like fires, aglow with light, save us from shame and insult.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So may the Rudras, mighty warriors, Evayamarut, with splendid brilliancy, like fires, be our protectors; They whose terrestrial dwelling-place is wide-extended, whom none suspect of sin, whose bands have lofty courage.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come in a friendly spirit, come to us, O Maruts, and hear his call who praises you, Evayamarut. Like car-borne men, one-minded with the mighty Visnu, keep enmity far from us with your deeds of wonder.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come to our sacrifice, ye Hnly Ones, to bless it, and, free from demons, hear our call, Evayamarut.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THOU, first inventor of this prayer, O Agni, Worker of Marvels, hast become our Herald. Thou, Bull, hast made us strength which none may conquer, strength that shall overcome all other prowess.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As Priest thou sattest at the seat of worship, furthering us, best Offerer, meet for honour. So first to thee have pious men resorted, turning thy mind to thoughts of ample riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In thee, still watching, they have followed riches, who goest with much wealth as with an army, The radiant Agni, lofty, fair to look on, worshipped with marrow, evermore resplendent.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They who approached the God's abode with homage, eager for glory, won them perfect glory: Yea, they gained even sacrificial titles, and found delight in thine auspicious aspect.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: On earth the people magnify thee greatly, thee their celestial and terrestrial riches. Thou, Helper, must be known as our Preserver, Father and Mother of mankind for ever.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Dear priest among mankind, adorable Agni hath seated him, joy-giver, skilled in worship. Let us approach thee shining in thy dwelling, kneeling upon our knees, with adoration.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Longing for bliss, pure-minded, God-devoted, Agni, we seek thee, such, meet to be lauded. Thou, Agni, leddest forth our men to battle, refulgent with the heaven's exalted splendour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sage of mankind, all peoples' Lord and Master, the Bull of men, the sender down of blessings, Still pressing on, promoting, purifying, Agni the Holy One, the Lord of riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, the mortal who hath toiled and worshipped, brought thee oblations with his kindled fuel, And well knows sacrifice with adoration, gains every joy with thee to guard and help him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Mightily let us worship thee the Mighty, with reverence, Agni! fuel and oblations, With songs, O Son of Strength, with hymns, with altar: so may we strive for thine auspicious favour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou who hast covered heaven and earth with splendour and with thy glories, glorious and triumphant. Continue thou to shine on us, O Agni, with strength abundant, rich, and long enduring.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Vouchsafe us ever, as man needs, O Vasu, abundant wealth of kine for son and offspring. Food noble, plenteous, far from sin and evil, he with us, and fair fame to make us happy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May I obtain much wealth in many places by love of thee and through thy grace, King Agni; For in thee Bounteous One, in thee the Sovran, Agni, are many boons for him who serves thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THOU, Agni, even as Mitra, hast a princely glory of thine own. Thou, active Vasu, makest fame increase like full prosperity.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For, verily, men pray to thee with sacrifices and with songs. To thee the Friendly Courser, seen of all, comes speeding through the air.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Of one accord men kindle thee Heaven's signal of the sacrifice, When, craving bliss, this race of man invites thee to the solemn rite.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let the man thrive who travails sore, in prayer, far thee the Bountiful. He with the help of lofty Dyaus comes safe through straits of enmity.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The mortal who with fuel lights thy flame and offers unto thee, Supports a house with many a branch, Agni, to live a hundred years.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thy bright smoke lifts itself aloft, and far-extended shines in heaven. For, Purifier! like the Sun thou beamest with thy radiant glow.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For in men's houses thou must be glorified as a well-loved guest, Gay like an elder in a fort, claiming protection like a son.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, Agni, like an able steed, art urged by wisdom in the wood. Thou art like wind; food, home art thou, like a young horse that runs astray.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: E'en things imperishable, thou, O Agni, like a gazing ox, Eatest, when hosts, Eternal One! of thee the Mighty rend the woods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, thou enterest as Priest the home of men who sacrifice. Lord of the people, prosper them. Accept the ofrering, Angiras!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Agni, God with Mitra's might, call hither the favour of the Gods from earth and heaven. Bring weal from heaven, that men may dwell securely. May we o'ercome the foe's malign oppressions, may we o'ercome them, through thy help o'ercome them.
