verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: TRUE, guardian of the Law, thy faithful servant wins ample light and dwells in peace, O Agni, Whom thou, as Varuna in accord with Mitra, guardest, O God, by banishing his trouble.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He hath paid sacrifices, toiled in worship, and offered gifts to wealth-increasing Agni. Him the displeasure of the famous moves not, outrage and scorn affect not such a mortal.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bright God, whose look is free from stain like Surya's, thou, swift, what time thou earnestly desirest, Hast gear to give us. Come with joy at evening, where, Child of Wood, thou mayest also tarry.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Fierce is his gait and vast his wondrous body: he champeth like a horse with bit and bridle, And, darting forth his tongue, as 'twere a hatchet, burning the woods, smelteth them like a smelter.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Archer-like, fain toshoot, he sets his arrow, and whets his splendour like the edge of iron: The messenger of night with brilliant pathway, like a tree-roosting bird of rapid pinion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In beams of morn he clothes him like the singer, and bright as Mitra with his splendour crackles. Red in the night, by day the men's possession: red, he belongs to men by day, Immortal.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like Heaven's when scattering beams his voice was uttered: among the plants the radiant Hero shouted, Who with his glow in rapid course came hither to fill both worlds, well-wedded Dames, with treasure.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who, with supporting streams and rays that suit him, hath flashed like lightning with his native vigour. Like the deft Maker of the band of Maruts, the bright impetuous One hath shone refulgent.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As at man's service of the Gods, Invoker, thou, Son of Strength, dost sacrifice and worship, So bring for us to-day all Gods together, bring willingly the willing Gods, O Agni.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Agni, radiant Herald of the morning, meet to be known, accept our praise with favour. Dear to all life, mid mortal men Immortal, our guest, awake at dawn, is Jatavedas.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whose might the very heavens regard with wonder: bright as the Sun he clothes himself with lustre. He who sends forth,, Eternal Purifier, hath shattered e'en the ancient works of Asna.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou art a Singer, Son! our feast-companion: Agni at birth prepared his food and pathway. Therefore vouchsafe us strength, O Strength-bestower. Win like a King: foes trouble not thy dwelling.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Even he who cats his firm hard food with swiftness,and overtakes the nights as Vayu kingdoms. May we o'ercome those who resist thine orders, like a steed casting down the flying foemen.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like Surya with his fulgent rays, O Agni, thou overspreadest both the worlds with splendour. Decked with bright colour he dispels the darkness, like Ausija, with clear flame swifily flying.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We have elected thee as most delightful for thy beams' glow: hear our great laud, O Agni. The best men praise thee as the peer of Indra in strength, mid Gods, like Viyu in thy bounty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now, Agni, on the tranquil paths of riches come to us for our weal: save us from sorrow. Grant chiefs and bard this boon. May we live happy, with hero children, through a hundred winters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I INVOCATE your Son of Strength, the Youthful, with hymns, the Youngest God, whose speech is guileless; Sage who sends wealth comprising every treasure, bringer of many boons, devoid of malice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: At eve and morn thy pious servants bring thee their precious gifts, O Priest of many aspects, On whom, the Purifier, all things living as on firm. ground their happiness have stablished.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou from of old hast dwelt among these people, by mental power the charioteer of blessings. Hence sendest thou, O sapient Jatavedas, to him who serves thee treasures in succession.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, whoever secretly attacks us, the neighbour, thou with Mitra's might! who harms us, Burn him with thine own Steers for ever youthful, burning with burning heat, thou fiercest burner.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who serves thee with sacrifice and fuel, with hymn, O Son of Strength, and chanted praises, Shines out, Immortal! in the midst of mortals, a sage, with wealth, with splendour and with glory.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Do this, O Agni, when we urge thee, quickly, triumphant in thy might subdue our foemen. When thou art praised with words and decked with brightness, accept this chanted hymn, the singer's worship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Help us, that we may gain this wish, O Agni, gain riches, Wealthy One! with store of heroes. Desiring strength from thee may we be strengthened, and win, Eternal! thine eternal glory.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: HE who seeks furtherance and grace to help him goes to the Son of Strength with newest worship, Calling the heavenly Priest to share the banquet, who rends the wood, bright, with his blackened pathway.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: White-hued and thundering he dwells in splendour, Most Youthful, with the loudvoiced and eternal- Agni, most variform, the Purifier, who follows crunching many ample forests.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Incited by the wind thy flames, O Agni, move onward, Pure One! pure, in all directions. Thy most destructive heavenly Navagvas break the woods down and devastate them boldly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thy pure white horses from their bonds are loosened: O Radiant One, they shear the ground beneath them, And far and wide shines out thy flame, and flickers rapidly moving over earth's high ridges.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Forth darts the Bull's tongue like the sharp stone weapon discharged by him who fights to win the cattle. Agni's fierce flame is like a hero's onset: dread and resistless he destroys the forests.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou with the sunlight of the great Impeller hast boldly over-spread the earth's expanses. So drive away with conquering might all perils. fighting out foemen burn up those who harm us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wondrous! of wondrous power! give to the singer wealth wondrous, marked, most wonderful, life-giving. Wealth bright, O Bright One, vast, with many heroes, give with thy bright flames to the man who lauds thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him, messenger of earth and head of heaven, Agni Vaisvanara, born in holy Order, The Sage, the King, the guest of men, a vessel fit for their mouths, the Gods have generated.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him have they praised, mid-point of sacrifices, great cistern of libations, seat of riches. Vaisvanara, conveyer of oblations, ensign of worship, have the Gods engendered.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: From thee, O Agni, springs the mighty singer, from thee come heroes who subdue the foeman. O King, Vaisvanara, bestow thou on us excellent treasures worthy to belonged fo r.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To thee, Immortal! when to life thou springest, all the Gods sing for joy as to their infant. They by thy mental powers were made immortal, Vaisvanara, when thou shonest from thy Parents.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni Vaisvanara, no one hath ever resisted these thy mighty ordinances, When thou, arising from thy Parents' bosom, foundest the light for days' appointed courses.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The summits of the heaven are traversed through and through by the Immortal's light, Vaisvanara's brilliancy. All creatures in existence rest upon his head. The Seven swift-flowing Streams have grown like branches forth,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Vaisvanara, who measured out the realms of air, Sage very wise who made the lucid spheres of heaven, The Undeceivable who spread out all the worlds, keeper is he and guard of immortality.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: AT Jatavedas' holy gathering I will tell aloud the conquering might of the swift red-hued Steer. A pure and fresher hymn flows to Vaisvanara, even as for Agni lovely Soma is made pure.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: That Agni, when in loftiest heaven he sprang to life, Guardian of Holy Laws, kept and observed them well. Exceeding wise, he measured out the firmament. Vaisvanara attained to heaven by mightiness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wonderful Mitra propped the heaven and earth apart, and covered and concealed the darkness with his light. He made the two bowls part asunder like two skins. Vaisvanara put forth all his creative power.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Migbty seized him in the bosom of the floods: the people waited on the King who should be praised. As envoy of Vivasvan MatariSvan brought Agni Vaisvanara hither from far away.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In every age bestow upon the singers wealth, worthy of holy synods, glorious, ever new. King, undecaying, as it were with sharpened bolt, smite down the sinner like a tree with lightning-flash.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Do thou bestow, O Agni, on our wealthy chiefs, rule, with good heroes, undecaying, bending not. So may we win for us strength. O Vaisvanara, hundredfold, thousandfold, O Agni, by thy help.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O thou who dwellest in three places, Helper, keep with effective guards our princely patrons. Keep our band, Agni, who have brought thee presents. Lengthen their lives, Vaisvanara, when lauded.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: ONE half of day is dark, and bright the other: both atmospheres move on by sage devices. Agni Vaisvanara, when born as Sovran, hath with his lustre overcome the darkness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I know not either warp or woof, I know not the web they weave when moving to the contest. Whose son shall here speak words that must be spoken without assistance from the Father near him?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For both the warp and woof he understandeth, and in due time shall speak what should be spoken, Who knoweth as the immortal world's Protector, descending, seeing with no aid from other.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He is the Priest, the first of all: behold him. Mid mortal men he is the light immortal. Here was he born, firm-seated in his station Immortal, ever waxing in his body.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: A firm light hath been set for men to look on: among all things that fly the mind is swiftest. All Gods of one accord, with one intention, move unobstructed to a single purpose.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Mine ears unclose to hear, mine eye to see him; the light that harbours in my spirit broadens. Far roams my mind whose thoughts are in the distance. What shall I speak, what shall I now imagine?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: All the Gods bowed them down in fear before thee, Agni, when thou wast dwelling in the darkness. Vaisvanara be gracious to assist us, may the Immortal favour us and help us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: INSTALL at sacrifice, while the rite advances, your pleasant, heavenly Agni, meet for praises. With hymns-for he illumines us-install him. He, Jatavedas, makes our rites successful.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hear this laud, Radiant Priest of many aspects, O Agni with the fires of man enkindled, Laud which bards send forth pure as sacred butter, strength to this man, as 'twere for self-advantage.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Mid mortal men that singer thrives in glory who offers gifts with hymns of praise to Agni, And the God, wondrous bright, with wondrous succours helps him to win a stable filled with cattle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He, at his birth, whose path is black behind him, filled heaven and earth with far-apparent splendour: And he himself hath been. through night's thick darkness, made manifest by light, the Purifier.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With thy most mighty aid, confer, O Agni, wonderful wealth on us and on our princes, Who stand preeminent, surpassing others in liberal gifts, in fame, and hero virtues.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, accept this sacrifice with gladness, which, seated here, the worshipper presenteth. Fair hymns hadst thou among the Bharadvajas, and holpest them to gain abundant vigour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Scatter our foes, increase our store. May we he glad a hundred winters with brave sons.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: EAGERLY Sacrifice thou, most skilful, Agni! Priest, pressing on as if the Maruts sent thee. To our oblation bring the two Nasatyas, Mitra and Varuna and Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou art our guileless, most delightful Herald, the God, among mankind, of holy synods. A Priest with purifying tongue, O Agni, sacrifice with thy mouth to thine own body.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For even the blessed longing that is in thee would bring the Gods down to the singer's worship, When the Angirases' sagest Sage, the Poet, sings the sweet measure at the solemn service.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bright hath he beamed, the wise, the far-refulgent. Worship the two widespreading Worlds, O Agni, Whom as the Living One rich in oblations the Five Tribes, bringing gifts, adorn with homage.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When I with reverence clip the grass for Agni, when the trimmed ladle, fullof oil, is lifted, Firm on the seat of earth is based the altar: eye-like, the sacrifice is directed Sun-ward.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Enrich us, O thou Priest of many aspects, with the Gods, Agni, with thy fires, enkindled. O Son of Strength, clad in the robe of riches, may we escape from woe as from a prison.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: KING of trimmed grass, Herald within the dwelling, may Agni worship the Impeller's World-halves. He, Son of Strength, the Holy, from a distance hath spread himself abroad with light like Surya.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In thee, most wise, shall Dyaus, for full perfection, King! Holy One! pronounce the call to worship. Found in three places, like the Speeder's footstep, come to present men's riches as oblations!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whose blaze most splendid, sovran in the forest, shines waxing on his way like the - Impeller. He knows himself, like as a guileless smelter, not to be stayed among the plants, Immortal.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Our friends extol him like a steed for vigour even Agni in the dwelling, jatave~as. Trce-fed, he fights with power as doth a champion, like Dawn's Sire to be praised with sacrifices.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Men wonder at his shining glows when, paring the woods with case, o'er the broad earth he goeth, And, like a rushing flood, loosed quickly, burneth, swift as a guilty thief, o'er desert places.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So mighty thou protectest us from slander, O Champion, Agni! with all fires enkindled. Bring opulence and drive away affliction. May brave sons gladden us through a hundred winters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: FROM thee, as branches from a tree, O Agni, from thee, Auspicious God! spring all our blessings- Wealth swiftly, strength in battle with our foemen, the rain besought of heaven, the flow of waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou art our Bhaga to send wealth thou dwellest, like circumambient air, with wondrous splendour. Friend art thou of the lofty Law, like Mitra, Controller, Agni! God! of many a blessing.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni! the hero slays with might his foeman; the singer bears away the Pani's booty- Even he whom thou, Sage, born in Law, incitest by wealth, accordant with the Child of Waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The man who, Son of Strength one with sacrifices, hymns, lauds, attracts thy fervour to the altar, Enjoys each precious thing, O God, O Agni, gains wealth of corn and is the lord of treasures.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Grant, Son of Strength, to men for their subsistence such things as bring high fame and hero children. For thou with might givest much food in cattle even to the wicked wolf when he is hungry.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Eloquent, Son of Strength, Most Mighty, Agni, vouchsafe us seed and offspring, full of vigour. May I by all my songs obtain abundance. May brave sons gladden us through a hundred winters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WHOSO to Agni hath endeared his thought and service by his hymns, That mortal eats before the rest, and finds sufficiency of food.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, in truth, is passing wise, most skilled in ordering, a Seer. At sacrifices Manus' sons glorify Agni as their Priest.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The foeman's wealth in many a place, Agni, is emulous to help. Men fight the fiend, and seek by rites to overcome the riteless foe.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni bestows the hero chief, winner of waters, firm in fray. Soon as they look upon his might his enemies tremble in alarm.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For with his wisdom Agni, God, protects the mortal from reproach, Whose conquering wealth is never checked, is never checked in deeds of might.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Agni, God with Mitra's might call hither the favour of the Gods from earth and heaven. Bring weal from heaven that men may dwell securely. May we o'ercome the foe's malign oppressions, may we o'ercome them, through thy help o'ercome them.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WITH this my song I strive to reach this guest of yours, who wakes at early morn, the Lord of all the tribes. Each time he comes from heaven, the Pure One from of old: from ancient days the Child eats everlasting food.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whom, well disposed, the Bhrgus stablished as a friend, whom men must glorify, high-flaming in the wood. As such, most friendly, thou art every day extolled in lauds by Vitahavya, O thou wondrous God.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Be thou the foeless helper of the skilful man, subduer of the enemy near or far away. Bestow a wealthy home on men, O Son of Strength. Give Vitahavya riches spreading far and wide, give Bharadvaja wide-spread wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him, your refulgent guest, Agni who comes from heaven, the Herald of mankind, well-skilled in sacred rites, Who, like a holy singer, utters heavenly words, oblation-bearer, envoy, God, I seek with hymns.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who with his purifying, eye-attracting form hath shone upon the earth as with the light of Dawn; Who speeding on, as in the fight of Etaia, cometh, untouched by age, as one athirst in heat.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Worship ye Agni, Agni, with your log of wood; praise your beloved, your beloved guest with songs. Invite ye the Immortal hither with your hymns. A God among the Gods, he loveth what is choice, loveth our service, God mid Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni inflamed with fuel in my song I sing, pure, Cleanser, steadlast, set in tront at sacrifice. Wise Jatavedas we implore with prayers for bliss the Priest, the holy Singer, bounteous, void of guile.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Men, Agni, in each age have made thee, Deathiess One, their envoy, offering-bearer, guard adorable. With reverence Gods and mortals have established thee, the ever-watchful, omnipresent Household Lord.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, Agni, ordering the works and ways of both, as envoy of the Gods traversest both the worlds. When we lay claim to thy regard and gracious fare, be thou to us a thriceprotecting friendly guard.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him fair of face, rapid, and fair to look on, him very wise may we who know not follow. Let him who knows all rules invite for worship, Agru announce our offering to the Immortals.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him, Agni, thou deliverest and savest who brings him prayer to thee the Wise, O Hero, The end of sacrifice or its inception; yea, thou endowest him with power and riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Guard us from him who would assail us, Agni; preserve us, O thou Victor, from dishonour. Here let the place of darkening come upon thee: may wealth be ours, desirable in thousands.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, the Priest, is King, Lord of the homestead, he, Jatayedas, knows all generations. Most skilful worshipper mid Gods and mortals, may he begin the sacrifice, the Holy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whate'er to-day thou, bright-flamed Priest, enjoyest from the man's rite-for thou art sacrificer- Worship, for duly dost thou spread in greatness: bear off thine ofrerings of to-day, Most Youthful.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Look thou upon the viands duly laid for thee. Fain would he set thee here to worship Heaven and,Earth. Help us, O liberal Agni, in the strife for spoil, so that we may o'ercome all things that trouble us, o'ercome, o'ercome them with thy help.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Together with all Gods, O fair-faced Agni, be seated first upon the woollined altar, Nest-like, bedewed with oil. Bear this our worship to Savitar who sacrifices rightly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Here the arranging priests, as did Atharvan, rub this Agni forth, Whom, not bewildered, as he moved in winding ways, they brought from gloom.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For the Gods' banquet be thou born, for full perfection and for weal. Bring the Immortal Gods who strengthen holy Law: so let our sacrifice reach the Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Agni, Lord and Master of men's homesteads, with kindled fuel we have made thee mighty. Let not our household gear be found defective. Sharpen us with thy penetrating splendour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: PRIEST of all sacrifices hast thou been appointed by the Gods, Agni, amid the race of man.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So with thy joyous tongues for us sacrifice nobly in this rite. Bring thou the Gods and worship them.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For well, O God, Disposer, thou knowest, straight on, the paths and ways, Agni, most wise in sacrifice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thee, too, hath Bharata of old, with mighty men, implored for bliss. And worshipped thee the worshipful.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou givest these abundant boons to Divodasa pouring forth, To Bharadvaja offering gifts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Do thou, Immortal Messenger, bring hither the Celestial Folk; Hearing the singer's eulogy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Mortals with pious thought implore thee, Agni, God, at holy rites, To come unto the feast of Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I glorify thine aspect and the might of thee the Bountilul. All those who love shall joy in thee,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Invoker placed by Manus, thou, Agni, art near, the wisest Priest: Pay worship to the Tribes of Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come, Agni, lauded, to the feast; come to the offering of the gifts. As Priest be seated on the grass.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So, Angiras, we make thee strong with fuel and with holy oil. Blaze high, thou youngest of the Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For us thou winnest, Agni, God, heroic strength exceeding great, Far-spreading and of high renown.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, Atharvan brought thee forth, by rubbing, from the lotus-flower, The head of Visva, of the Priest.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thee. Vrtra's slayer, breaker down of castles, hath Atharvan's son, Dadhyac the Rsi, lighted up.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The hero Pathya kindled thee the Dasyus'. most destructive foe, Winner of spoil in every fight.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come, here, O Agni, will I sing verily other songs to thee, And with these drops shalt thou grow strong.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Where'er tby mind applies itself, vigour preeminent bast thou: There wilt thou gain a dwelling-place.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Not for a moment only lasts thy bounty, good to many a one! Our service therefore shalt thou gain.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, the Bharata, hath been sought, the Vrtra-slayer, marked of all, Yea, Divodasa's Hero Lord.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For he gave riches that surpass in greatness all the things of earth, Fighting untroubled, unsubdued.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, Agni, as in days of old, with recent glory, gathered light, Hast overspread the lofty heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bring to your Agni, O my friends, boldly your laud and sacrifice: Give the Disposer praise and song.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For as sagacious Herald he hath sat through every age of man, Oblation-bearing messenger.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bring those Two Kings whose ways are pure, Adityas, and the Marut host, Excellent God! and Heaven and Earth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For strong and active mortal man, excellent, Agni, is the look Of thee Immortal, Son of Strength
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Rich through his wisdom, noblest be the giver serving thee to-day: The man hath brought his hymn of praise.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These, Agni, these are helped by thee, who strong and active all their lives, O'ercome the malice of the foe, fight down the malice of the foe.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Agni with his pointed blaze cast down each fierce devouring fiend May Agni win us wealth by war.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O active Jatavedas, bring riches with store of hero sons: Slay thou the demons, O Most Wise.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Keep us, O Jatavedas, from the troubling of the man of sin: Guard us thou Sage who knowest prayer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whatever sinner, Agni, brings oblations to procure our death, Save us from woe that he would work.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Drive from us with thy tongue, O God, the man who doeth evil deeds, The mortal who would strike us dead.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Give shelter reaching far and wide to Bharadvaja, conquering Lord! Agni, send wealth most excellent.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Agni slay the Vrtras,-fain for riches, through the lord of song, Served with oblation, kindled, bright.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: His Father's Father, shining in his Mother's everlasting side, Set on the seat of holy Law.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O active Jatavedas, bring devotion that wins progeny, Agni, that it may shine to heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Child of Strength, to thee whose look is lovely we with dainty food, O Agni, have poured forth our songs.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To thee for shelter are we come, as to the shade from fervent heat Agni, who glitterest like gold.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Mighty as one who slays with shafts, or like a bull with sharpened horn, Agni, thou breakest down the forts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whom, like an infant newly born, devourer, in their arms they bear, Men's Agni, skilled in holy rites.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bear to the banquet of the Gods the God best finder-out of wealth, Let him he seated in his place.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In Jatavedas kindle ye the dear guest who hath now appeared In a soft place, the homestead's Lord.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Harness, O Agni, O thou God, thy steeds which are most excellent: They bear thee as thy spirit wills.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come hither, bring the Gods to us to taste the sacrificial feast, To drink the draught of Soma juice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Agni of the Bharatas, blaze high with everlasting might, Shine forth and gleam, Eternal One.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The mortal man who serves the God with banquet, and, bringing gifts at sacrifice, lauds Agni, May well attract, with prayer and hands uplifted, the Priest of Heaven and Earth, true Sacrificer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, we bring thee, with our hymn, oblation fashioned in the heart. Let these be oxen unto thee, let these be bulls and kine to thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Gods enkindle Agni, best slayer of Vrtra, first in rank, The Mighty, One who brings us wealth and crushes down the Raksasas.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: DRINK Soma, Mighty One, for which, when lauded, thou breakest through the cattle-stall, O Indra; Thou who, O Bold One, armed with thunder smotest Vrtra with might, and every hostile being.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Drink it thou God who art impetuous victor, Lord of our hymns, with beauteousjaws, the Hero, Render of kine-stalls, car-borne, thunder-wielding, so pierce thy way to wondrous strength, O Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Drink as of old, and let the draught delight thee. hear thou our prayer and let our songs exalt thee. Make the Sun visible, make food abundant, slaughter the foes, pierce through and free the cattle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These gladdening drops, O Indra, Self-sustainer, quaffed shall augment thee in thy mighty splendour. Yea, let the cheering drops delight thee greatly, great, perfect, strong, powerful, all-subduing.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Gladdened whereby, bursting the firm enclosures, thou gavest splendour to the Sun and Morning. The mighty rock that compassed in the cattle, ne'er moved, thou shookest from its seat, O Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou with thy wisdom, power, and works of wonder, hast stored the ripe milk in the raw cows' udders Unbarred the firm doors for the kine of Morning, and, with the Angirases, set free the cattle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou hast spread out wide earth, a mighty marvel, and, high thyself, propped lofty heaven, O Indra. Both worlds, whose Sons are Gods, thou hast supported, young, Mothers from old time ofholy Order.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yea, Indra, all the Deities installed thee their one strong Champion in the van for battle. What time the godless was the Gods' assailant, Indra they chose to win the light of heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yea, e'en that heaven itself of old bent backward before thy bolt, in terror of its anger, When Indra, life of every living creature, smote down within his lair the assailing Dragon.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yea, Strong One! Tvastar turned for thee, the Mighty, the bolt with thousand spikes and hundred edges, Eager and prompt at will, wherewith thou crushedst the boasting Dragon, O impetuous Hero.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He dressed a hundred buffaloes, O Indra, for thee whom all accordant Maruts strengthen. He, Pusan Visnu, poured forth three great vessels to him, the juice that cheers, that slaughters Vrtra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou settest free the rushing wave of waters, the floods' great swell encompassed and obstructed. Along steep slopes their course thou tumedst, Indra, directed downward, speeding to the ocean.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So may our new prayer bring thee to protect us, thee well-armed Hero with thy bolt of thunder, Indra, who made these worlds, the Strong, the ty, who never groweth old, the victory-giver.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So, Indra, form us brilliant holy singers for strength, for glory, and for food and riches. Give Bharadvaja hero patrons, Indra Indra, be ours upon the day of trial.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With this may we obtain strength God-appointed, and brave sons gladden us through a hundred winters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: GLORIFY him whose might is all-surpassing, Indra the much-invoked who fights uninjured. Magnify with these songs the never-vanquished, the Strong, the Bull of men, the Mighty Victor.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He, Champion, Hero, Warrior, Lord of battles, impetuous, loudly roaring, great destroyer, Who whirls the dust on high, alone, oerthrower, hath made all races of mankind his subjects.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, thou alone, hast tamed the Dasyus; singly thou hast subdued the people for the Arya. In this, or is it not, thine hero exploit, Indra? Declare it at the proper season.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For true, I deem, thy strength is, thine the Mighty, thine, O Most Potent, thine the Conquering Victor; Strong, of the strong, Most Mighty, of the mighty, thine, driver of the churl to acts of bounty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Be this our ancient bond of friendship with you and with Angirases here who speak of Vala. Thou, Wondrous, Shaker of things firm, didst smite him in his fresh strength, and force his doors and castles.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With holy thoughts must he be called, the Mighty, showing his power in the great fight with Vrtra. He must be called to give us seed and offspring, the Thunderer must he moved and sped to battle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He in his might, with name that lives for ever, hath far surpassed all human generations. He, most heroic, hath his home with splendour, with glory and with riches and with valour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Stranger to guile, who ne'er was false or faithless, bearing a name that may be well remembered, Indra crushed Cumuri, Dhuni, Sambara, Pipru, and Susna, that their castles fell in ruin.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With saving might that must be praised and lauded, Indra, ascend thy car to smite down Vrtra. In thy right hand hold fast thy bolt of thunder, and weaken, Bounteous Lord, his art and magic.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As Agni, as the dart burns the dry forest, like the dread shaft burn down the fiends, O Indra; Thou who with high deep-reaching spear hast broken, hast covered over mischief and destroyed it.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With wealth, by thousand paths come hither, Agni, paths that bring ample strength, O thou Most Splendid. Come, Son of Strength, o'er whom, Invoked of many! the godless hath no power to keep thee distant.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: From heaven, from earth is bruited forth the greatness of him the firm, the fiery, the resplendent. No foe hath he, no counterpart, no refuge is there from him the Conqueror full of wisdom
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This day the deed that thou hast done is famous, when thou, for him, with many thousand others Laidest low Kutsa, Ayu, Atithigva, and boldly didst deliver Turvayana.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In thee, O God, the wisest of the Sages, all Gods were joyful when thou slewest Ahi. When lauded for thyself, thou gavest freedom to sore-afflicted Heaven and to the people.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This power of thine both heaven and earth acknowledge, the deathless Gods acknowledge it, O Indra. Do what thou ne'er hast done, O Mighty Worker: beget a new hymn at thy sacrifices.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: GREAT, hero-like controlling men is Indra, unwasting in his powers, doubled in vastness. He, turned to us, hath grown to hero vigour: broad, wide, he hath been decked by those who serve him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The bowl made Indra swift to gather booty, the High, the Lofty, Youthful, Undecaying, Him who hath waxed by strength which none may conquer, and even at once grown to complete perfection.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Stretch out those hands of thine, extend to us-ward thy wide capacious arms, and grant us glory. Like as the household herdsman guards the cattle, so move thou round about us in the combat.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now, fain for strength, let us invite your Indra hither, who lieth hidden with his Heroes,- Free from all blame, without reproach, uninjured, e'en as were those who sang, of old, his praises.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With steadfast laws, wealth-giver, strong through Soma, he hath much fair and precious food to feed us. In him unite all paths that lead to riches, like rivers that commingle with the ocean.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bring unto us the mightiest might, O Hero, strong and most potent force, thou great Subduer! All splendid vigorous powers of men vouchsafe us, Lord of Bay Steeds, that they may make us joyful.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bring us, grown mighty in its strength, O Indra, thy friendly rapturous joy that wins the battle, Wherewith by thee assisted and triumphant, we may laud thee in gaining seed and offspring.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, bestow on us the power heroic skilled and exceeding strong, that wins the booty, Wherewith, by thine assistance, we may conquer our foes in battle, be they kin or stranger.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let thine heroic strength come from behind us, before us, from above us or below us. From every side may it approach us, Indra. Give us the glory of the realm of splendour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With most heroic aid from thee, like heroes Indra, may we win wealth by deeds glory. Thou, King, art Lord of earthly, heavenly treasure: vouchsafe us riches vast, sublime, and lasting.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Bull, whose strength hath waxed, whom Maruts follow, free-giving Indra, the Celestial Ruler, Mighty, all-conquering, the victory-giver, him let us call to grant us new protection.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Give up the people who are high and haughty to these men and to me, O Thunder-wielder! Therefore upon the earth do we invoke thee, where heroes win, for sons and kine and waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Through these thy friendships, God invoked of many! may we be victors over every foeman. Slaying both kinds of foe, may we, O Hero, be happy, helped by thee, with ample riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: GIVE us wealth, Indra, that with might, as heaven o'ertops the earth, o'ercomes our foes in battle Wealth that brings thousands and that wins the corn-lands, wealth, Son of Strength! that vanquishes the foeman.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Even as the power of Dyaus, to thee, O Indra, all Asura sway was by the Gods entrusted, When thou, Impetuous! leagued with Visnu, slewest Vrtra the Dragon who enclosed the waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, Strong, Victor, Mightier than the mighty, addressed with prayer and perfect in his splendour, Lord of the bolt that breaketh forts in pieces, became the King of the sweet juice of Soma..
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: There, Indra, while the light was won, the Panis f1ed, 'neath a hundred blows, for wise Dasoni, And greedy Susna's magical devices nor left he any of their food remaining.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What time the thunder fell and Susna perished, all life's support from the great Druh was taken. Indra made room for his car-drivcr Kutsa who sate beside him, when he gained the sunlight.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As the Hawk rent for him the stalk that gladdens, he wrenched the head from Namuci the Dasa. He guarded Nam, Sayya's son, in slumber, and sated him with food, success, and riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, thunder-armed, with thy great might hast shattered Pipru's strong forts who knew the wiles of serpents. Thou gavest to thy worshipper Rjisvan imperishable Wealth, O Bounteous Giver.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The crafty Vetasu, the swift Dasni, and Tugra speedily with all his servants, Hath Indra, gladdening with strong assistance, forced near as 'twere to glorify the Mother.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Resistless, with the hosts he battles, bearing in both his arms the Vrtra-slaying thunder. He mounts his Bays, as the car-seat an archer: yoked at a word they bear the lofty Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May we, O Indra, gain by thy new favour: so Parus laud thee, with their sacrifices, That thou hast wrecked seven autumn forts, their shelter, slain Dasa tribes and aided Purukutsa.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Favouring Usana the son of Kavi, thou wast his ancient strengthener, O Indra. Thou gavest Navavastva. as a present, to the great father gavest back his grandson.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, roaring Indra, drovest on the waters that made a roaring sound like rushing rivers, What time, O Hero, o'er the sea thou broughtest, in safety broughtest Turvasa and Yadu.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This Indra, was thy work in war: thou sentest Dhuni and Cumuri to sleep and slumber. Dabhiti lit the flame for thee, and worshipped with fuel, hymns, poured Soma, dressed oblations.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THESE the most constant singer's invocations call thee who art to be invoked, O Hero;
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I praise that Indra, known to all men, honoured with songs, extolled with hymns at sacrifices, Whose majesty, rich in wondrous arts, surpasseth the magnitude of earth, and heaven in greatness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He hath made pathways, with the Sun to aid him, throughout the darkness that extended pathless. Mortals who yearn to worship ne'er dishonour, O Mighty God, thy Law who art Immortal.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And he who did these things, where is that Indra? among what tribes? what people doth he visit? What sacrifice contents thy mind , and wishes? What priest among them all? what hymn, O Indra?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yea, here were they who, born of old, have served thee, thy friends of ancient time, thou active Worker. Bethink thee now of these, Invoked of many! the midmost and the recent, and the youngest.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Inquiring after him, thy later servants, Indra, have gained thy former old traditions. Hero, to whom the prayer is brought, we praise thee as great for that wherein we know thee mighty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The demon's strength is gathered fast against thee: great as that strength hath grown, go forth to meet it. With thine own ancient friend and companion, the thunderbolt, brave Champion! drive it backward.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hear, too, the prayer of this thy present beadsman, O Indra, Hero, cherishing the singer. For thou wast aye our fathers' Friend aforetime, still swift to listen to their supplication.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bring to our help this day, for our protection, Varuna, Mitra , Indra, and the Maruts, Pusan and Visnu, Agni and Purandhi, Savitar also, and the Plants and Mountains.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The singers here exalt with hymns and praises thee who art very Mighty and Most Holy. Hear, when invoked, the invoker's invocation. Beside thee there is nonelike thee, Immortal!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now to my words come quickly thou who knowest, O Son of Strength, with all who claim our worship, Who visit sacred rites, whose tongue is Agni, Gods who made Manu stronger than the Dasyu.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: On good and evil ways be thou our Leader, thou who art known to all as Path-preparer. Bring power to us, O Indra, with thy Horses, Steeds that are best to draw, broad-backed, unwearied.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WITH these my hymns I glorify that Indra who is alone to be invoked by mortals, The Lord, the Mighty One, of manly vigour, victorious, Hero, true, and full of wisdom.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Our sires of old,. Navagvas, sages seven, while urging him to show his might, extolled him, Dwelling on heights, swift, smiting down opponents, guileless in word, and in his thoughts most mighty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We seek that Indra to obtain his riches that bring much food, and men, and store of heroes. Bring us, Lord of Bay Steeds, to make us joyful, celestial wealth, abundant, undecaying.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Tell thou us this, if at thy hand aforetime the earlier singers have obtained good fortune, What is thy share and portion, Strong Subduer, Asura-slayer, rich, invoked of many?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who for car-borne Indra, armed with thunder, hath a hymn, craving, deeply-piercing, fluent, Who sends a song effectual, firmly-grasping, and strength-bestowing, he comes near the mighty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Strong of thyself, thou by this art hast shattered, with thought-swift Parvata, him who waxed against thee, And, Mightiest! roaring! boldly rent in pieces things that were firmly fixed and never shaken.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him will we fit for you with new devotion, the strongest Ancient One, in ancient manner. So may that Indra, boundless, faithful Leader, conduct us o'er all places hard to traverse.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou for the people who oppress hast kindled the earthly firmament and that of heaven. With heat, O Bull, on every side consume them: heat earth and flood for him who hates devotion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Of all the Heavenly Folk, of earthly creatures thou art the King, O God of splendid aspect. In thy right hand, O Indra, grasp die thunder: Eternal! thou destroyest all enchantments.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Give us confirmed prosperity, O Indra, vast and exhaustless for the foe's subduing. Strengthen therewith the Arya's hate and Dasa's, and let the arms of Nahusas be mighty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come with thy team which brings all blessings hither, Disposer, much-invoked, exceeding holy. Thou whom no fiend, no God can stay or hinder, come swittly with these Steeds in my direction.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THOU art attached to pressed-out Soma, Indra, at laud, at prayer, and when the hymn is chanted; Or when with yoked Bays, Maghavan, thou comest, O Indra, bearing in thine arms the thunder.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Or when on that decisive day thou holpest the presser of the juice at Vrtra's slaughter; Or when thou, while the strong one feared, undaunted, gavest to death, Indra, the daring Dasyus.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let Indra drink the pressed-out Soma, Helper and mighty Guide of him who sings his praises. He gives the hero room who pours oblations, and treasure even to the lowly singer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: E'en humble rites with his Bay steeds he visits: he wields the bolt, drinks Soma, gives us cattle. He makes the valiant rich in store of heroes, accepts our praise and hears the singer's calling.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What he hath longed for we have brought to Indra, who from the days of old hath done us service. While Soma flows we will sing hymn, and laud him, so that our prayer may streng. then Indra's vigour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou hast made prayer the means of thine exalting, therefore we wait on thee with hymns, O Indra. May we, by the pressed Soma, Somadrinker! bring thee, with sacrifice, blissful sweet refreshment.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Mark well our sacrificial cake, delighted Indra, drink Soma and the milk commingled. Here on the sacrificer's grass be seated: give ample room to thy devoted servant.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Mighty One, be joyful as thou willest. Let these our sacrifices reach and find thee; And may this hymn and these our invocations turn thee, whom many men invoke, to help us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Friends, when thejuices flow, replenish duly your own, your bounteous Indra with the Soma. Will it not aid him to support us? Indra. spares him who sheds the juice to win his favour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: While Soma flowed, thus Indra hath been lauded, Ruler of nobles, mid the Bharadvajas, That Indra may become the singer's patron and give him wealth in every kind of treasure.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: STRONG rapturous joy, praise, glory are with Indra: impetuous God, he quaffs the juice of Soma: That Maghavan whom men must laud with singing, Heaven-dweller, King of songs, whose help is lasting.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He, Friend of man, most wise, victorious Hero, hears, with far-reaching aid, the singer call him. Excellent, Praise of Men, the bard's Supporter, Strong, he gives strength, extolled in holy synod.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The lofty axle of thy wheels, O Hero, is not surpassed by heaven and earth in greatness. Like branches of a tree, Invoked of many manifold aids spring forth from thee, O Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Strong Lord, thine energies, endowed with vigour, are like the paths of kine converging homeward. Like bonds of cord, Indra, that bind the younglings, no bonds are they, O thou of boundless bounty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: One act to-day, another act tomorrow oft Indra makes what is not yet existent. Here have we Mitra, Varuna, and Pusan to overcome the foeman's domination.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: By song and sacrifice men brought the waters from thee, as from a mountain's ridge, O Indra. Urging thy might, with these fair lauds they seek thee, O theme of song, as horses rush tobattle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: That Indra whom nor months nor autumn seasons wither with age, nor fleeting days enfeeble,- Still may his body Wax, e'en now so mighty, glorified by the lauds and hymns that praise him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Extolled, he bends not to the strong, the steadfast, nor to the bold incited by the Dasyu. High mountains are as level plains to Indra: even in the deep he finds firm ground to rest on.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Impetuous Speeder through all depth and distance, give strengthening food, thou drinker of the juices. Stand up erect to help us, unreluctant, what time the gloom of night brightens to morning.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hasting to help, come hither and protect him, keep him from harm when he is here, O Indra. At home, abroad, from injury preserve him. May brave sons gladden us through a hundred winters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WITH thine assistance, O thou Mighty Indra, be it the least, the midmost, or the highest,- Great with those aids and by these powers support us, Strong God! in battle that subdues our foemen.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With these discomfit hosts that fight against us, and check the opponent's wrath, thyself uninjured. With these chase all our foes to every quarter: subdue the tribes of Dasas to the Arya.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Those who array themselves as foes to smite us, O Indra, be they kin or be they strangers,- Strike thou their manly strength that it be feeble, and drive in headlong flight our foemen backward.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With strength of limb the hero slays the hero, when bright in arms they range them for the combat. When two opposing hosts contend in battle for seed and offspring, waters, kine, or corn-lands.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yet no strong man hath conquered thee, no hero, no brave, no warrior trusting in his valour. Not one of these is match for thee, O Indra. Thou far surpassest all these living creatures.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He is the Lord of both these armies' valour when the commanders call them to the conflict: When with their ranks expanded they are fighting with a great foe or for a home with heroes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And when the people stir themselves for battle, be thou their saviour, Indra, and protector, And theirs, thy manliest of our friends, the pious, the chiefs who have installed us priests, O Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To thee for high dominion hath been for evermore, for slaughtering the Vrtras, All lordly power and might, O Holy Indra, given by Gods for victory in battle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So urge our hosts together in the combats: yield up the godless bands that fight against us. Singing, at morn may we find thee with favour, yea, Indra, and e'en now, we Bharadvajas.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O INDRA, hear us. Raining down the Soma, we call on thee to win us mighty valour. Give us strong succour on the day of trial, when the tribes gather on the field of battle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The warrior, son of warrior sire, invokes thee, to gain great strength that may be won as booty: To thee, the brave man's Lord, the fiends' subduer, he looks when fighting hand to hand for cattle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou didst impel the sage to win the daylight, didst ruin Susna for the pious Kutsa. The invulnerable demon's head thou clavest when thou wouldst win the praise of Atithigva.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The lofty battle-car thou broughtest forward; thou holpest Dasadyu the strong when fighting. Along with Vetasu thou slewest Tugra, and madest Tuji strong, who praised thee, Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou madest good the laud, what time thou rentest a hundred thousand fighting foes, O Hero, Slewest the Dasa Sambara of the mountain, and with strange aids didst succour Divodasa.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Made glad with Soma-draughts and faith, thou sentest Cumuri to his sleep, to please Dabhiti. Thou, kindly giving Raji to Pithinas, slewest with might, at once, the sixty thousand.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May I too, with the liberal chiefs, O Indra, acquire thy blin supreme and domination, When, Mightiest! Hero-girt! Nahusa heroes boast them in thee, the triply-strong Defender.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So may we he thy friends, thy best beloved, O Indra, at this holy invocation. Best be Pratardani, illustrious ruler, in slaying foemen and in gaining riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WHAT deed hath Indra done in the wild transport, in quaffing or in friendship with, the Soma? What joys have men of ancient times or recent obtained within the chamber of libation?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In its wild joy Indra hath proved him faithful, faithful in quaffing, faithful in its friendship. His truth is the delight that in this chamber the men of old and recent times have tasted.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: All thy vast power, O Maghavan, we know not, know not the riches of thy full abundance. No one hath seen that might of thine, productive of bounty every day renewed, O Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This one great power of thine our eyes have witnessed, wherewith thou slewest Varasikha's children, When by the force of thy descending thunder, at the mere sound, their boldest was demolished.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In aid of Abhyavartin Cayamana, Indra destroyed the seed of Varasikha. At Hariyupiya he smote the vanguard of the Vrcivans, and the rear fled frighted.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Three thousand, mailed, in quest of fame, together, on the Yavyavati, O much-sought Indra, Vrcivan's sons, falling before the arrow, like bursting vessels went to their destruction.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He, whose two red Steers, seeking goodly pasture, plying their tongues move on 'twixt earth and heaven, Gave Turvasa to Srnjaya, and, to aid him, gave the Vrcivans up to Daivavata.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Two wagon-teams, with damsels, twenty oxen, O Agni, Abhydvartin Cayamana, The liberal Sovran, giveth me. This guerdon of Prthu's seed is hard to win from others.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THE Kine have come and brought good fortune: let them rest in the cow-pen and be happy near us. Here let them stay prolific, many-coloured, and yield through many morns their milk for Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra aids him who offers sacrifice and gifts: he takes not what is his, and gives him more thereto. Increasing ever more and ever more his wealth, he makes the pious dwell within unbroken bounds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These are ne'er lost, no robber ever injures them: no evil-minded foe attempts to harass them. The master of the Kine lives many a year with these, the Cows whereby he pours his gifts and serves the Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The charger with his dusty brow o'ertakes them not, and never to the shambles do they take their way. These Cows, the cattle of the pious worshipper, roam over widespread pasture where no danger is.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To me the Cows seem Bhaga, they seem Indra, they seem a portion of the first-poured Soma. These present Cows, they, O ye Indra. I long for Indra with my heart and spirit.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Cows, ye fatten e'en the worn and wasted, and make the unlovely beautiful tolook on. Prosper my house, ye with auspicious voices. Your power is glorified in our assemblies.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Crop goodly pasturage and be prolific drink pure sweet water at good drinking places. Never be thief or sinful man your matter, and may the dart of Rudra still avoid you.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now let this close admixture be close intermigled with these Cows, Mixt with the Steer's prolific flow, and, Indra, with thy hero might.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: YOUR men have followed Indra for his friendship, and for his loving-kindness glorified him. For he bestows great wealth, the Thunder-wielder: worship him, Great and Kind, to win his favour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him to whose hand, men closely cling, and drivers stand on his golden chariot firmly stationed. With his firm arms he holds the reins; his Horses, the Stallions, are yoked ready for the journey.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thy devotees embrace thy feet for glory. Bold, thunder-armed, rich, through thy strength, in guerdon, Robed in a garment fair as heaven to look on, thou hast displayed thee like an active dancer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: That Soma when effused hath best consistence, for which the food is dressed and grain is mingled; By which the men who pray, extolling Indra chief favourites of Gods, recite their praises.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: No limit of thy might hath been appointed, which by its greatness sundered earth and heaven. These the Prince filleth full with strong endeavour, driving, as 'twere, with help his flocks to waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So be the lofty Indra prompt to listen, Helper unaided, golden-visored Hero. Yea, so may he, shown forth in might unequalled, smite down the many Vrtras and the Dasyus.
