verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: INDRA hath waxed yet more for hero prowess, alone, Eternal, he bestoweth treasures. Indra transcendeth both the worlds in greatness: one half of him equalleth earth and heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yea, mighty I esteem his Godlike nature: none hindereth what he hath once determined. Near and afar he spread and set the regions, and every day the Sun became apparent.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: E'en now endures thine exploit of the Rivers, when, Indra, for their floods thou clavest passage. Like men who sit at meat the mountains settled: by thee, Most Wise! the regions were made steadfast.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This is the truth, none else is like thee, Indra, no God superior to thee, no mortal. Thou slewest Ahi who besieged the waters, and lettest loose the streams to hurry seaward.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, thou breakest up the floods and portals on all sides, and the firmness of the mountain. Thou art the King of men, of all that liveth, engendering at once Sun, Heaven, and Morning.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: SOLE Lord of wealth art thou, O Lord of riches: thou in thine hands hast held the people, Indra! Men have invoked thee with contending voices for seed and waters, progeny and sunlight.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Through fear of thee, O Indra, all the regions of earth, though naught may move them, shake and tremble. All that is firm is frightened at thy coming, -the earth, the heaven, the mountain, and the forest.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With Kutsa, Indra! thou didst conquer Susna, voracious, bane of crops, in fight for cattle. In the close fray thou rentest him: thou stolest the Sun's wheel and didst drive away misfortunes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou smotest to the ground the hundred castles, impregnable, of Sambara the Dasyu, When, Strong, with might thou holpest Divodasa who poured libations out, O Soma-buyer, and madest Bharadvaja rich who praised thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As such, true Hero, for great joy of battle mount thy terrific car, O Brave and Manly. Come with thine help to me, thou distant Roamer, and, glorious God, spread among men my glory.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I WITH my lips have fashioned for this Hero words never matched, most plentiful and auspicious, For him the Ancient, Great, Strong, Energetic, the very mighty Wielder of the Thunder.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Amid the sages, with the Sun he brightened the Parents: glorified, he burst the mountain; And, roaring with the holy-thoughted singers, he loosed the bond that held the beams of Morning.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Famed for great deeds, with priests who kneel and laud him, he still hath conquered in the frays for cattle, And broken down the forts, the Fort-destroyer, a Friend with friends, a Sage among the sages.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come with thy girthed mares, with abundant vigour and plenteous strength to him who sings thy praises. Come hither, borne by mares with many heroes, Lover of song! Steer! for the people's welfare.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra with rush and might, sped by his Coursers, hath swiftly won the waters from the southward. Thus set at liberty the rivers daily flow to their goal, incessant and exhaustless.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: GIVE us the rapture that is mightiest, Indra, prompt to bestow and swift to aid, O Hero, That wins with brave steeds where brave steeds encounter, and quells the Vrtras and the foes in battle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For with loud voice the tribes invoke thee, Indra, to aid them in the battlefield of heroes. Thou, with the singers, hast pierced through the Panis: the charger whom thou aidest wins the booty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Both races, Indra, of opposing foemen, O Hero, both the Arya and the Dasa, Hast thou struck down like woods with well-shot lightnings: thou rentest them in fight, most manly Chieftain!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, befriend us with no scanty succour, prosper and aid us, Loved of all that liveth, When, fighting for the sunlight, we invoke thee, O Hero, in the fray, in war's division.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Be ours, O Indra, now and for the future, be graciously inclined and near to help us. Thus may we, singing, sheltered by the Mighty, win many cattle on the day of trial.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: FULL Many songs have met in thee, O Indra, and many a noble thought from thee proceedeth. Now and of old the eulogies of sages, their holy hymns and lauds, have yearned for Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He, praised of many, bold, invoked of many, alone is glorified at sacrifices. Like a car harnessed for some great achievement, Indra must be the cause of our rejoicing.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They make their way to Indra and exalt him, bim whom no prayers and no laudations trouble; For when a hundred or a thousand singers. laud him who loves the song their praise delights him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As brightness mingles with the Moon in heaven, the offered Soma yearns to mix with Indra. Like water brought to men in desert places, our gifts at sacrifice have still refreshed him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To him this mighty eulogy, to Indra hath this our laud been uttered by the poets, That in the great encounter with the foemen, Loved of all life, Indra may guard and help us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WHEN shall our prayers rest in thy car beside thee? When dost thou give the singer food for thousands? When wilt thou clothe this poet's laud with plenty, and when wilt thou enrich our hymns with booty?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When wilt thou gatber men with men, O Indra, heroes with heroes, and prevail in combat? Thou shalt win triply kine in frays for cattle, so, Indra, give thou us celestial glory.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yea, when wilt thou, O Indra, thou Most Mighty, make the prayer all-sustaining for the singer? When wilt thou yoke, as we yoke songs, thy Horses, and come to offerings that bring wealth in cattle?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Grant to the Singer food with store of cattle, splendid with horses and the fame of riches. Send food to swell the milch-cow good at milking: bright be its shine among the Bharadvajas.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Lead otherwise this present foeman, Sakra! Hence art thou praised as Hero, foe destroyer Him who gives pure gifts may I praise unceasing. Sage, quicken the Angirases by devotion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THY raptures ever were for all men's profit: so evermore have been thine earthly riches. Thou still hast been the dealer-forth of vigour, since among Gods thou hast had power and Godhead.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Men have obtained his strength by sacrificing, and ever urged him, on to hero valour. For the rein-seizing, the impetuous Charger they furnished power even for Vrtra's slaughter.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Associate with him, as teams of horses, help, manly might, and vigour follow Indra. As rivers reach the sea, so, strong with praises, our holy songs reach him the Comprehensive.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Lauded by us, let flow the spring, O Indra, of excellent and brightly-shining riches. For thou art Lord of men, without an equal: of all the world thou art the only Sovran.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hear what thou mayst hear, thou who, fain for worship, as heaven girds earth, guardest thy servant's treasure; Tlat thou mayst be our own, joying in power, famed through thy might in every generation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: LET thy Bay Horses, yoked, O mighty Indra, bring thy car hither fraught with every blessing. For thee, the Heavenly, e'en the poor invoketh: may we this day, thy feast-companions, prosper.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Forth to the vat the brown drops flow for service, and purified proceed directly forward. May Indra drink of this, our guest aforetime, Celestial King of the strong draught of Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bringing us hitherward all-potent Indra on well-wheeled chariot, may the Steeds who bear him Convey him on the road direct to glory, and ne'er may Vayu's Amrta cease and fail him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Supreme, he stirs this man to give the guerdon,-Indra, most efficacious of the princes,- Wherewith, O Thunderer, thou removest sorrow, and, Bold One! partest wealth among the nobles.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra is hewho gives enduring vigour: may our songs magnify the God Most Mighty. Best Vrtra-slayer be the Hero Indra these things he gives as Prince, with strong endeavour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: HE hath drunk hence, Most Marvellous, and carried away our great and splendid call on Indra. The Bounteous, when we serve the Gods, accepteth song yet more famous and the gifts we bring him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The speaker filleth with a cry to Indra his ears who cometh nigh e'en from a distance. May this my call bring Indra to my presence, this call to Gods composed in sacred verses.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him have I sung with my best song and praises, Indra of ancient birth and Everlasting. For prayer and songs in him are concentrated: let laud wax mighty when addressed to Indra:
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, whom sacrifice shall strengthen, Soma, and song and hymn, and praises and devotion, Whom Dawns shall strengthen when the night departeth, Indra whom days shall strengthen, months, and autumns.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him, born for conquering might in full perfection, and waxen strongfor bounty and for glory, Great, Powerful, will we to-day, O singer, invite to aid. us and to quell our foemen.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: OF this our charming, our celestial Soma, eloquent, wise, Priest, with inspired devotion, Of this thy close attendant, hast thou drunken. God, send the singer food with milk to grace it.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Craving the kine, rushing against the mountain led on by Law, with holyminded comrades, He broke the never-broken ridge of Vala. With words of might Indra subdued the Panis.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This Indu lighted darksome nights, O Indra, throughout the years, at morning and at evening. Him have they stablished as the days' bright ensign. He made the Mornings to be born in splendour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He shone and caused to shine the worlds that shone not. By Law he lighted up the host of Mornings. He moves with Steeds yoked by eternal Order, contenting men with nave that finds the sunlight.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now, praised, O Ancient King! fill thou the singer with plenteous food that he may deal forth treasures. Give waters, herbs that have no poison, forests, and kine, and steeds, and men, to him who lauds thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: DRINK, Indra; juice is shed to make thee joyful: loose thy Bay Steeds and give thy friends their freedom. Begin the song, seated in our assembly. Give strength for sacrifice to him who singeth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Drink thou of this whereof at birth, O Indra, thou drankest, Mighty One for power and rapture. The men, the pressing-stones, the cows, the waters have made this Soma ready for thy drinking.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The fire is kindled, Soma pressed, O Indra: let thy Bays, best to draw, convey thee hither. With mind devoted, Indra, I invoke thee. Come, for our great prosperity approach us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, come hither: evermore thou camest through our great strong desire to drink the Soma. Listen and hear the prayers which now we offer, and let this sacrifice increase thy vigour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Mayst thou, O Indra, on the day of trial, present or absent, wheresoe'er thou dwellest, Thence, with thy team, accordant with the Maruts, Song-lover! guard our sacrifice, to help us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: COME gracious to our sacrifice, O Indra: pressed Soma-drops are purified to please thee. As cattle seek their home, so Thunderwielder, come, Indra, first of those who claim our worship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With that well-formed most wide-extending palate, wherewith thou ever drinkest streams of sweetness, Drink thou; the Adhvaryu standeth up before thee: let thy spoil-winning thunderbolt attend thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This drop, steer-strong and omniform, the Soma, hath been made ready for the Bull, for India. Drink this, Lord of the Bays, thou Strong Supporter, this that is thine of old, thy food for ever.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Soma when pressed excels the unpressed Soma, better, for one who knows, to give him pleasure. Come to this sacrifice of ours, O Victor replenish all thy powers with this libation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We call on thee, O Indra: come thou hither: sufficient be the Soma for thy body. Rejoice thee, Satakratu! in the juices guard us in wars, guard us among our people.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: BRING sacrificial gifts to him, Omniscient, for he longs to drink, The Wanderer who comes with speed, the Hero ever in the van.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With Soma go ye nigh to him chief drinker of the Soma's juice: With beakers to the Impetuous God, to Indra with the drops effused.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What time, with Soma, with the juice effused, ye come before the God, Full wise he knows the hope of each, and, Bold One, strikes this foe and that.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To him, Adhvaryu! yea, to him give offerings of the juice expressed. Will he not keep us safely from the spiteful curse of each presumptuous high-born foe?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: IN whose wild joy thou madest once Sambara Divodasa's prey, This Soma is pressed out for thee, O Indra: drink!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whose gladdening draught, shed from the points, thou guardest in the midst and end, This Soma is pressed out for thee, O Indra drink!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In whose wild joy thou settest free the kine held fast within the rock, This Soma is pressed out for thee, O Indra: drink!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This, in whose juice delighting thou gainest the might of Maghavan, This Soma is pressed out for thee, O Indra drink!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THAT which is wealthiest, Wealthy God in splendoursmost illustrious, Soma is pressed: thy gladdening draught, Indra! libation's Lord! is this.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Effectual, Most Effectual One! thine, as bestowing wealth of hymns, Soma is pressed: thy gladdening draught, Indra! libation's Lord! is this.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wherewith thou art increased in strength, and conquerest with thy proper aids, Soma is pressed: thy gladdening draught, Indra! libation's Lord! is this.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him for your sake I glorify as Lord of Strength who wrongeth none, The Hero Indra, conquering all, Most Bounteous, God of all the tribes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Those Goddesses, both Heaven and Earth, revere the power and might of him, Him whom our songs increase in strength, the Lord of bounty swift to come.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To seat your Indra, I will spread abroad with power this song of praise. The saving succours that abide in him, like songs, extend and grow.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: A recent Friend, he found the skilful priest: he drank, and showed forth treasure from the Gods. He conquered, borne by strong all-shaking mares, and was with far-spread power his friends' Protector.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In course of Law the sapient juice was quaffed: the Deities to glory turned their mind. Winning through hymns a lofty title, he, the Lovely, made his beauteous form apparent.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bestow on us the most illustrious strength ward off men's manifold malignities. Give with thy might abundant vital force, and aid us graciously in gaining riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We turn to thee as Giver, liberal Indra. Lord of the Bay Steeds, be not thou ungracious. No friend among mankind have we to lookto: why have men called thee him who spurs the niggard?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Give us not up, Strong Hero! to the hungry: unharmed be we whom thou, so rich, befriendest. Full many a boon hast thou for men demolish those who present no gifts nor pour oblations.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As Indra thundering impels the rain-clouds, so doth he send us store of kine and horses. Thou art of old the Cherisher of singers let not the rich who bring no gifts deceive thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Adbyaryu, hero, bring to mighty Indrafor he is King thereof-the pressed-out juices; To him exalted by the hymns and praises, ancient and modern, of the singing Rsis.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In the wild joy of this hath Indra, knowing full many a form, struck down resistless Vrtras. Proclaim aloud to him the savoury Soma so that the Hero, strong of jaw, may drink it.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Indra drink this Soma poured to please him, and cheered therewith slay Vrtra with his thunder. Come to our sacrifice even from a distance, good lover of our songs, the bard's Supporter.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The cup whence Indra drinks the draught is present: the Amrta dear to Indra hath been drunken, That it may cheer the God to gracious favour, and keep far from us hatred and affliction.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Therewith enraptured, Hero, slay our foemen, the unfriendly, Maghavan be they kin or strangers, Those who still aim their hostile darts to smite us, turn them to flight, O Indra, crush and kill them.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Indra Maghavan, in these our battles win easy paths for us and ample freedom. That we may gain waters and seed and offspring, set thou our princes on thy side, O Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let thy Bay Stallions, harnessed, bring thee hither, Steeds with strong chariot and strong reins to hold them, Strong Horses, speeding hither, bearing thunder, well-harnessed, for the strong exciting potion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Beside the vat, Strong God! stand thy strong Horses, shining with holy oil, like waves exulting. Indra, they bring to thee, the Strong and Mighty, Soma of juices shed by mighty press-stones.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou art the Bull of earth, the Bull of heaven, Bull of the rivers, Bull of standing waters. For thee, the Strong, O Bull, hath Indu swollen. juice pleasant, sweet to drink, for thine election.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This God, with might, when first he had his being, with Indra for ally, held fast the Pani. This Indu stole away the warlike weapons, and foiled the arts of his malignant father.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Dawns he wedded to a glorious Consort, and set within the Sun the light that lights him. He found in heaven, in the third lucid regions, the threefold Amrta in its close concealment.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He stayed and held the heaven and earth asunder: the chariot with the sevenfold reins he harnessed. This Soma Set with power within the milch-kine a spring whose ripe contents ten fingers empty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THAT Indra is our youthful Friend, who with his trusty guidance led Turvasa, Yadu from afar.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Even to the dull and uninspired Indra, gives vital power, and wins Even with slow steed the offered prize.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Great are his ways of guiding us, and! manifold are his eulogies: His kind protections never fail.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Friends, sing your psalm and offer praise to him to whom the prayer is brought: For our great Providence is he.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, Slaughterer of Vrtra, art Guardian and Friend of one and two, Yea, of a man like one of us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Beyond men's hate thou leadest us, and givest cause to sing thy praise: Good hero art thou called by men.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I call with hymns, as 'twere a cow to milk, the Friend who merits praise, The Brahman who accepts the prayer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him in whose hands they say are stored all treasures from the days of old, The Hero, conquering in the fight.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Lord of Strength, Caster of the Stone, destroy the firm forts built by men, And foil their arts, unbending God!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thee, thee as such, O Lord of Power, O Indra, Soma-drinker, true, We, fain for glory, have invoked.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Such as thou wast of old, and art now to be called on when the prize lies ready, listen to our call.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With hymns and coursers we will gain, Indra, through thee, both steeds and spoil Most glorious, and the proffered prize.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, Indra, Lover of the Song, whom men must stir to help, hast been Great in the contest for the prize.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Slayer of foes, whatever aid of thine imparts the swiftest course, With that impel our car to speed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As skilfullest of those who drive the chariot, with our art and aim, O Conqueror, win the proffered prize.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Praise him who, Matchless and Alone, was born the Lord of living men, Most active, with heroic soul.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou who hast been the singers' Friend, a Friend auspicious with thine aid, As such, O Indra, favour us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Grasp in thine arms the thunderbolt, O Thunder-armed, to slay the fiends: Mayst thou subdue the foemen's host.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I call the ancient Friend, allied with wealth, who speeds the lowly man, Him to whom chiefly prayer is brought.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For he alone is Lord of all the treasures of the earth: he speeds Hither, chief Lover of the Song.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So with thy yoked teams satisfy our wish with power and wealth in steeds And cattle, boldly, Lord of kine!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sing this, what time the ' juice is pressed, to him your Hero, Much-invoked, To please him as a mighty Steer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He, Excellent, withholdeth not his gift of power and wealth in kine, When he hath listened to our songs.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May he with might unclose for us the cow's stall, whosesoe'er it be, To which the Dasyu-slayer goes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Indra Satakratu, these our songs have called aloud to thee, Like mother cows to meet their calves.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hard is thy love to win: thou art a Steer to him who longs for steers: Be to one craving steeds a Steed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Delight thee with the juice we pour for thine own great munificence: Yield not thy singer to reproach.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These songs with every draught we pour come, Lover of the Song, to thee, As milch-kine hasten to their young
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To thee most oft invoked, amid the many singers' rivalry Who beg with all their might for wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Nearest and most attractive may our laud, O Indra come to thee. Urge thou us on to ample wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Brbu hath set himself above the Panis, o'er their highest head, Like the wide bush on Ganga's bank.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He whose good bounty, thousandfold, swift as the rushing of the wind, Suddenly offers as a gift.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So all our singers ever praise the pious Brbu's noble deed, Chief, best to give his thousands, best to give a thousand liberal gifts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THAT we may win us wealth and power we poets, verily, call on thee: In war men call on thee, Indra, the hero's Lord, in the steed's race-course call on thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As such, O Wonderful, whose hand holds thunder, praised as mighty, Caster of the Stone! Pour on us boldly, Indra, kine and chariotsteeds, ever to be the conqueror's strength.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We call upon that Indra, who, most active, ever slays the foe: Lord of the brave, Most Manly, with a thousand powers, help thou and prosper us in fight.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Rcisama, thou forcest men as with a bull, with anger, in the furious fray. Be thou our Helper in the mighty battle fought for sunlight, water, and for life.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Indra, bring us name and fame, enriching, mightiest, excellent, Wherewith, O Wondrous God, fair-visored, thunder-armed, thou hast filled full this earth and heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We call on thee, O King, Mighty amid the Gods, Ruler of men, to succour us. All that is weak in us, Excellent God, make firm: make our foes easy to subdue.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: All strength and valour that is found, Indra, in tribes of Nahusas, and all the splendid fame that the Five Tribes enjoy Bring, yea, all manly powers at once.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Or, Maghavan, what vigorous strength in Trksi lay, in Druhyus or in Paru's folk, Fully bestow on us, that, in the conquering fray, we may subdue our foes in fight.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Indra, grant a happy home, a triple refuge triply strong. Bestow a dwelling-place on the rich lords and me, and keep thy dart afar from these.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They who with minds intent on spoil subdue the foe, boldly attack and smite him down,- From these, O Indra Maghavan who lovest song, be closest guardian of our lives.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And now, O Indra, strengthen us: come near and aid us in the fight, What time the feathered shafts are flying in the air, the arrows with their sharpened points.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Give us, where heroes strain their bodies in the fight, the shelter that our fathers loved. To us and to our sons give refuge: keep afar all unobserved hostility.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When, Indra, in the mighty fray thou urgest chargers to their speed, On the uneven road and on a toilsome path, like falcons, eager for renown,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Speeding like rivers rushing down a steep descent, responsive to the urging call, That come like birds attracted to the bait, held in by reins in both the driver's hands.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: YEA, this is good to taste and full of. sweetness, verily it is strong and rich in flavour. No one may conquer Indra in the battle when he hath drunken of the draught we offer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This sweet juice here had mightiest power to gladden: it boldened Indra when he siaughtered Vrtra, When he defeated Sambara's many onslaughts, and battered down his nineand ninety ramparts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This stirreth up my voice when I have drunk it: this hath aroused from sleep my yearning spirit. This Sage hath measured out the six expanses from which no single creature is excluded.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This, even this, is he who hath created the breadth of earth, the lofty height of heaven. He formed the nectar in three headlong rivers. Soma supports the wide mid-air above us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He found the wavy sea of brilliant colours in forefront of the Dawns who dwell in brightness. This Mighty One, the Steer begirt by Maruts, hath propped the heavens up with a mighty pillar.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Drink Soma boldly from the beaker, Indra, in war for treasures, Hero, Vrtra-slayer! Fill thyself full at the mid-day libation, and give us wealth, thou Treasury of riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Look out for us, O Indra, as our Leader, and guide us on to gain yet goodlier treasure. Excellent Guardian, bear us well through peril, and lead us on to wealth with careful guidance.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Lead us to ample room, O thou who knowest, to happiness, security, and sunlight. High, Indra, are the arms of thee the Mighty: may we betake. us to their lofty shelter.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Set us on widest chariot-seat, O Indra, with two steeds best to draw, O Lord of Hundreds! Bring us the best among all sorts of viands: let not the foe's wealth, Maghavan, subdue us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Be gracious, Indra, let my days be lengthened: sharpen my thought as 'twere a blade of iron Approve whatever words I speak, dependent on thee, and grant me thy divine protection.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra the Rescuer, Indra the Helper, Hero who listens at each invocation, Sakra I call, Indra invoked of many. May Indra Maghavan prosper and bless us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May helpful Indra as our good Protector, Lord of all treasures, favour us with succour, Baffle our foes, and give us rest and safety, and may we be the lords of hero vigour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May we enjoy the grace of him the Holy, yea, may we dwell in his auspicious favour. May helpful Indra as our good Preserver drive from us, even from afar, our foemen.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like rivers rushing down a slope, O Indra, to thee haste songs and prayers and linked verses. Thou gatherest, Thunderer! like widespread bounty, kine, water, drops, and manifold libations.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who lauds him, satisfies him, pays him worship? E'en the rich noble still hath found him mighty. With power, as when one moves his feet alternate, he makes the last precede, the foremost follow.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Famed is the Hero as each strong man's tamer, ever advancing one and then another. King of both worlds, hating the high and haughty, Indra protects the men who are his people.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He loves no more the men he loved aforetime: he turns and moves away allied with others. Rejecting those who disregard his worship, Indra victorious lives through many autumns.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In every figure he hath been the mode: this is his only form for us to look on. Indra moves multiform by his illusions; for his Bay Steeds are yoked, ten times a hundred.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Here Tvastar, yoking to the car the Bay Steeds, hath extended sway. Who will for ever stand upon the foeman's side, even when our princes sit at ease?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Gods, we have reached a country void of pasture the land, though spacious, was too small to hold us. Brhaspati, provide in war for cattle; find a path, Indra, for this faithful singer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Day after day far from their seat he drove them, alike, from place to place, those darksome creatures. The Hero slew the meanly-huckstering Dasas, Varcin and Sambara, where the waters gather.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Out of thy bounty, Indra, hath Prastoka bestowed ten coffers and ten mettled horses. We have received in turn from Divodasa Sambara's wealth, the gift of Atithigva.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ten horses and ten treasure-chests, ten garments as an added gift, These and ten lumps of gold have I received from Divodasa's hand.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ten cars with extra steed to each, for the Atharvans hundred cows, Hath Asvatha to Payu given.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thus Srnjaya's son honoured the Bharadvajas, recipients of all noble gifts and bounty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Lord of the wood, be firm and strong in body: be, bearing us, a brave victorious hero Show forth thy strength, compact with straps of leather, and let thy rider win all spoils of battle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Its mighty strength was borrowed from the heaven and earth: its conquering force was brought from sovrans of the wood. Honour with holy gifts the Car like Indra's bolt, the Car bound round with straps, the vigour of the floods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou Bolt of Indra, Vanguard of the Maruts, close knit to Varuna and Child of Mitra,- As such, accepting gifts which here we offer, receive, O Godlike Chariot, these oblations.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Send forth thy voice aloud through earth and heaven, and let the world in all its breadth regard thee; O Drum, accordant with the Gods and Indra, drive thou afar, yea, very far, our foemen.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thunder out strength and fill us full of vigour: yea, thunder forth and drive away all dangers. Drive hence, O War-drum, drive away misfortune: thou art the Fist of Indra: show thy firmness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Drive hither those, and these again bring hither: the War-drum speaks aloud as battle's signal. Our heroes, winged with horses, come together. Let our car-warriors, Indra, be triumphant.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: SING to your Agni with each song, at every sacrifice, for strength. Come, let us praise the Wise and Everlasting God, even as a well-beloved Friend,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Son of Strength; for is he not our gracious Lord? Let us serve him who bears our gifts. In battle may he be our help and strengthener, yea, be the saviour of our lives.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, thou beamest forth with light, great Hero, never changed by time. Shining, pure Agni! with a light that never fades, beam with thy fair beams brilliantly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou worshippest great Gods: bring them without delay by wisdom and thy wondrous power. O Agni, make them turn hither to succour us. Give strength, and win it for thyself.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He whom floods, stones, and trees support, the offspring of eternal Law; He who when rubbed with force is brought to life by men upon the lofty height of earth;
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who hath filled both worlds fult with his brilliant shine, who hastens with his smoke to heaven; He made himself apparent through the gloom by night, the Red Bull in the darksome nights, the Red Bull in the darksome nights.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Agni, with thy lofty beams, with thy pure brilliancy, O God, Kindled, Most Youthful One! by Bharadvaja's hand, shine on us, O pure God, with wealth, shine, Purifier! splendidly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou art the Lord of house and home of all the tribes, O Agni, of all tribes of men. Guard with a hundred forts thy kindler from distress, through hundred winters, Youngest God! and those who make thy singers rich.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wonderful, with thy favouring help, send us thy bounties, gracious Lord. Thou art the Charioteer, Agni, of earthly wealth: find rest and safety for our seed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With guards unfailing never negligent speed thou our children and our progeny. Keep far from us, O Agni, all celestial wrath and wickedness of godless men.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hither, O friends, with newest song drive her who freely pours her milk; Loose her who never turns away;
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who, for the host of Maruts bright with native sheen, hath shed immortal fame like milk; Whom the impetuous Maruts look upon with love, who moves in splendour on their ways.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For Bharadvaja she poured down in days of old The milch-cow yielding milk for all, and food that gives all nourishment.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Your friend like Indra passing wise, with magic power like Varuna. Like Aryaman joy-giving, bringing plenteous food like Visnu for my wish, I praise,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bright as the host of Maruts mighty in their roar. May they bring Pusan free from foes; May they bring hither hundreds, thousands for our men: may they bring hidden stores to light, and make wealth easy to be found.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Haste to me, Pusan, in thine car, bright Deity: I fain would speak: Most sinful is our foeman's hate.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Tear not up by the roots the Kakambira tree: destroy thou all malignity. Let them not snare by day the neck of that Celestial Bird the Sun.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Uninjured let thy friendship be, like the smooth surface of a skin, A flawless skin, containing curds, full to the mouth, containing curds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For thou art high above mankind, in glory equal to the Gods. Therefore, O Pusan, look upon us in the fight: now help us as in days of old.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May the kind excellence of him the Kind, loud Roarers! be our guide, Be it the God's, O Maruts, or a mortal man's who worships, ye impetuous Ones!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They whose high glory in a moment like the God, the Sun, goes round the space of heaven, The Maruts have obtained bright strength, a sacred name, strength that destroys the Vrtras, strength Vrtra-destroying excellent.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Once, only once, the heaven was made, once only once, the earth was formed- Once, only Prsni's milk was shed: no second, after this, is born.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I LAUD with newest songs the Righteous People, Mitra and Varuna who make us happy. Let them approach, here let them listen,Agni, Varuna, Mitra, Lords of fair dominion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him, to be praised at each tribe's sacrifices, the Two young Matrons' sober-minded Herald, The Son of Strength, the Child of Heaven, the signal of sacrifice, red Agni will I worship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Unlike in form are the Red God's two Daughters: one is the Sun's, and stars bedeck the other. Apart, the Sanctifiers, in succession, come to the famed hymn, praised in holy verses.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I with a lofty song call hither Vayu, all-bounteous, filler of his car, most wealthy. Thou, Sage, with bright path, Lord of harnessed horses, impetuous, promptly honourest the prudent.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: That chariot of the Asvins, fair to look on, pleaseth me well, yoked with a thought, refulgent, Wherewith, Nasatyas, Chiefs, ye seek our dwelling, to give new strength to us and to our children.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bulls of the Earth, O Vata and Parjanya, stir up for us the regions of the water. Hearers of truth, ye, Sages, World-Supporters, increase his living wealth whose songs delight you.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So may Sarasvati, the Hero's Consort, brisk with rare life, the lightning's Child, inspire us, And, with the Dames accordant, give the singer a refuge unassailable and flawless.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I praise with eloquence him who guards all pathways. He, when his love impelled him, went to Arka. May he vouchsafe us gear with gold to grace it: may Pusan make each prayer of ours efective.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Herald Agni, fulgent, bring for worship Tvastar adored, in homes and swift to listen, Glorious, first to share, the life-bestower, the ever active God, fair-armed, fair-handed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Rudra by day, Rudra at night we honour with these our songs, the Universe's Father. Him great and lofty, blissful, undecaying let us call specially as the Sage impels us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye who are youthful, wise, and meet for worship, come, Maruts, to the longing of the singer. Coming, as erst to Angiras, O Heroes, ye animate and quicken e'en the desert.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Even as the herdsman driveth home his cattle, I urge my songs to him the strong swift Hero May he, the glorious, lay upon his body the singer's hymns, as stars bedeck the heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who for man's behoof in his afiliction thrice measured out the earthly regions, Visnu- When one so great as thou affordeth shelter, may we with wealth and with ourselves be happy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sweet be this song of mine to Ahibudhnya, Parvata, Savitar, with Floods and Lightnings; Sweet, with the Plants, to Gods who seek oblations. May liberal Bhaga speed us on to riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Give riches borne on cars, with many heroes, contenting men, the guard of mighty Order. Give us a lasting home that we may battle with godless bands of men who fight against us, and meet with tribes to whom the Gods are gracious.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I CALL with prayers on Aditi your Goddess, on Agni, Mitra, Varuna for favour, On Aryaman who gives unasked, the gracious, on Gods who save, on Savitar and Bhaga.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Visit, to prove us free from sin, O Surya Lord of great might, the bright Gods sprung from Daksa, Twice-born and true, observing sacred duties, Holy and full of light, whose tongue is Agni.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And, O ye Heaven and Earth, a wide dominion, O ye most blissful Worlds, our lofty shelter, Give ample room and freedom for our dwelling, a home, ye Hemispheres, which none may rival.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This day invited may the Sons of Rudra, resistless, excellent, stoop down to meet us; For, when beset with slight or sore affliction, we ever call upon the Gods, the Maruts;
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To whom the Goddess Rodasi clings closely, whom Pusan follows bringing ample bounty. What time ye hear our call and come, O Maruts, upon your separate path all creatures tremble.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With a new hymn extol, O thou who singest, the Lover of the Song, the Hero Indra. May he, exalted, hear our invocation, and grant us mighty wealth and strength when lauded.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Give full protection, Friends of man, ye Waters, in peace and trouble, to our sons and grandsons. For ye are our most motherly physicians, parents of all that standeth, all that moveth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Savitar come hither and approach us, the God who rescues, Holy, goldenhanded, The God who, bounteous as the face of Morning, discloses precious gifts for him who worships.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And thou, O Son of Strength, do thou turn hither the Gods to-day to this our holy service. May I for evermore enjoy thy bounty and, Agni, by thy grace be rich in heroes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come also to my call, O ye Nasatyas, yea, verily, through my prayers, ye Holy Sages. As from great darkness ye delivered Atri, protect us, Chiefs, from danger in the conflict.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Gods, bestow upon us riches, splendid with strength and heroes, bringing food in plenty. Be gracious, helpful Gods of earth, of heaven, born of the Cow, and dwellers in the waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Rudra and Sarasvati, accordant, Visnu and Vayu, pour down gifts and bless us; Rbhuksan, Vaja, and divine Vidhatar, Parjanya, Vata make our food abundant.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May this God Savitar, the Lord, the Offspring of Waters, pouring down his dew be gracious, And, with the Gods and Dames accordant, Tvastar; Dyaus with the Gods and Prthivi with oceans.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Aja-Ekapad and Ahibudhnya, and Earth and Ocean hear our invocation; All Gods who strengthen Law, invoked and lauded, and holy texts uttered by sages, help us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So with my thoughts and hymns of praise the children of Bharadvaja sing aloud to please you. The Dames invoked, and the resistless Vasus, and all ye Holy Ones have been exalted.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THAT mighty eye of Varuna and Mitra, infallible and dear, is moving upward. The pure and lovely face of holy Order hath shone like gold of heaven in its arising.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Sage who knows these Gods' three ranks and orders, and all their generations near and distant, Beholding good and evil acts of mortals, Sura marks well the doing of the pious.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I praise you Guards of mighty Law eternal, Aditi, Mitra, Varuna, the noble, Aryaman, Bhaga, all whose thoughts are faithful: hither I call the Bright who share in common.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Lords of the brave, infallible, foe-destroyers, great Kings, bestowers of fair homes to dwell in, Young, Heroes, ruling heaven with strong dominion, Adityas, Aditi I seek with worship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Heaven our Father, Earth our guileless Mother, O Brother Agni, and ye Vasus, bless us. Grant us, O Aditi and ye Adityas, all of one mind, your manifold protection.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Give us not up to any evil creature, as spoil to wolf or she-wolf, O ye Holy. For ye are they who guide aright our bodies, ye are the rulers of our speech and vigour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let us not suffer for the sin of others, nor do the deed which ye, O Vasus, punish. Ye, Universal Gods! are all-controllers: may he do harm unto himself who hates Me.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Mighty is homage: I adopt and use it. Homage hath held in place the earth and heaven. Homage to Gods! Homage commands and rules them. I banish even committed sin by homage
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: You Furtherers of Law, pure in your spirit, infallible, dwellers in the home of Order, To you all Heroes mighty and far-seeing I bow me down, O Holy Ones, with homage.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For these are they who shine with noblest splendour; through all our troubles these conduct us safely- Varuna, Mitra, Agni, mighty Rulers, trueminded, faithful to the hymn's controllers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May they, Earth, Aditi, Indra, Bhaga, Pusan increase our laud, increase the Fivefold people. Giving good help, good refuge, goodly guidance, be they our good deliverers, good protectors.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come now, O Gods, to your celestial station: the Bharadvajas' priest entreats your favour. He, sacrificing, fain for wealth, hath honoured the Gods vath those who sit and share oblations.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, drive thou the wicked foe, the evil-hearted thief away, Far, far, Lord of the brave I and give us easy paths.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Soma, these pressing-stones have called aloud to win thee for our Friend. Destroy the greedy Pani, for a wolf is he.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye, O most bountiful, are they who, led by Indra, seek the sky. Give us good paths for travel: guard us ivell at home.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now have we entered on the road that leads to bliss, without a foe, The road whereon a man escapes all enemies and gathers wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THIS I allow not in the earth or heaven, at sacrifice or in these holy duties. May the huge mountains crush him down: degraded be Atiyaja's sacrificing patron.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Or he who holds us in contempt, O Maruts, or seeks to blame the prayer that we are making, May agonies of burning be his portion. May the sky scorch the man who hates devotion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Why then, O Soma, do they call thee keeper of prayer? Why then our guardian from reproaches? Why then beholdest thou how men revile us? Cast thy hot dart at him who hates devotion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Mornings as they spring to life, protect me, and may the Rivers as they swell preserve me. My guardians be the firmly-seated mountains: the Fathers, when I call on Gods, defend me!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Through all our days may we be healthy. minded, and look upon the Sun when he arises. Grant this the Treasure-Lord of treasures, coming, observant, oftenest of Gods, with succour!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Most near, most oft comes Indra with protection, and she Sarasvati, who swells with rivers - Parjanya, bringing health with herbs, and Agni, well lauded swift to listen, like a father.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hear this mine invocation; come hither, O Universal Gods, Be seated on this holy grass.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To him who comes to meet you, Gods, with offerings bathed in holy oil- Approach ye, one and all, to him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: All Sons of Immortality shall listen to the songs we sing, And be exceeding good to us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May all the Gods who strengthen Law, with Rtus, listening to our call, Be pleased with theit appropriate draught.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May 1ndra, with the Marut host, with Tvastar, Mitra, Aryaman, Accept the laud and these our gifts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Agni, Priest, as rules ordain, offer this sacrifice of ours, Remembering the Heavenly Folk.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Listen, All-Gods, to this mine invocation, Ye who inhabit heaven, and air's midregions, All ye, O Holy Ones, whose tongue is Agni, seated upon this sacred grass, be joyful.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May the All-Gods who claim our worship hear my thought; may the two World-halves hear it, and the Waters' Child. Let me not utter words that ye may disregard. Closely allied with you may we rejoice in bliss.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And those who, Mighty, with the wiles of serpents, were born on earth, in heaven, where waters gather- May they vouchsafe us life of full duration. May the Gods kindly give us nights and mornings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: At this my call, O Agni and Parjanya, help, swift to hear, my thought and our laudation. One generates holy food, the other offspring, so grant us food enough with store of children.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When holy grass is strewn and fire enkindled, with hymn and lowly homage I invite you. All-Gods, to day in this our great assembly rejoice, ye Holy, in the gifts we offer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: LORD of the path, O Pusan, we have yoked and bound thee to our hymn, Even as a car, to win the prize.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bring us the wealth that men require, a manly master of a house, Free-handed with the liberal meed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Even him who would not give, do thou, O glowing Pusan, urge to give, And make the niggard's soul grow soft.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Clear paths that we may win the prize; scatter our enemies afar. Strong God, be all our thoughts fulfilled.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Penetrate with an awl, O Sage, the hearts of avaricious churls, And make them subject to our will.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thrust with thine awl, O Pusan: seek that which the niggard's heart holds dear, And make him subject to our will.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Tear up and read in pieces, Sage, the hearts of avaricious churls, And make them subject to our will.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, glowing Pusan, carriest an awl that urges men to prayer; Therewith do thou tear up and rend to shreds the heart of every one.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou bearest, glowing Lord! a goad with horny point that guides the cows Thence do we seek thy gift of bliss.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And make this hymn of ours produce kine, horses, and a store of wealth For our delight and use as men.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O PUSAN, bring us to the man who knows, who shall direct us straight, And say unto us, It is here.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May we go forth with Pusan who shall point the houses out to us, And say to us, These same are they.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Unharmed is Pusan's chariot wheel; the box ne'er falleth to the ground, Nor doth the loosened felIy shake.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Pusan forgetteth not the man who serveth him with offered gift: That man is first to gather wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Pusan follow near our kine; may Pusan keep our horses safe: May Pusan gather gear for us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Follow the kine of him who pours libations out and worships thee; And ours who sing thee songs of praise.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let none be lost, none injured, none sink in a pit and break a limb. Return with these all safe and sound.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Pusan who listens to our prayers, the Strong whose wealth is never lost, The Lord of riches, we implore.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Secure in thy protecting care, O Pusan, never may we fail. We here are they who sing thy praise.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: From out the distance, far and wide, may Pusan stretch his right hand forth, And drive our lost again to us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: SON of Deliverance, come, bright God! Let us twain go together: be our charioteer of sacrifice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We pray for wealth to thee most skilled of charioteers, with braided hair, Lord of great riches, and our Friend.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bright God whose steeds are goats, thou art a stream of wealth, a treasure-heap, The Friend of every pious man.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Pusan, who driveth goats for steeds, the strong and Mighty, who is called His Sister's lover, will we laud.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: His Mother's suitor I address. May he who loves his Sister hear, Brother of Indra, and my Friend.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May the sure-footed goats come nigh, conveying Pusan on his car, The God who visiteth mankind.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WHOSO remembers Pusan as cater of mingled curd and meal Need think no more upon the God.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And he is best of charioteers. Indra, the hero's Lord, allied With him as Friend, destroys the foes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And there the best of charioteers hath guided through the speckled cloud The golden wheel of Sura's car.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whate'er we speak this day to thee, Wise, Wondrous God whom many praise, Give thou fulfilment of our thought.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Lead on this company of ours, that longs for kine, to win the spoil: Thou, Pusan, art renowned afar.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Prosperity we crave from thee, afar from sin and near to wealth, Tending to perfect happiness both for to. morrow and to-day.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: INDRA and Pusan will we call for friend ship and prosperity And for the winning of the spoil.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: One by the Soma sits to drink juice which the mortar hath expressed: The other longs for curd and meal.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Goats are the team that draws the one: the other hath Bay Steeds at hand; With both of these he slays the fiends.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When Indra, wondrous strong, brought down the streams, the mighty waterfloods, Pusan was standing by his side.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To this, to Pusan's favouring love, and Indra's, may we closely cling, As to a tree's extended bough.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As one who drives a car draws in his reins, may we draw Pusan near, And Indra, for our great success.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: LIKE heaven art thou: one form is bright, one holy, like Day and Night dissimilar in colour. All magic powers thou aidest, self-depen. dent! Auspicious be thy bounty here, O Pusan.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Goat-borne, the guard of cattle, he whose home is strength, inspirer of the hymn, set over all the world; Brandishing here and there his lightly. moving goad, beholding every creature, Pusan, God, goes forth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Pusan, with thy golden ships that travel across the ocean, in the air's mid-region, Thou goest on an embassy to Surya, subdued by love, desirous of the glory.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Near kinsman of the heaven and earth is Pusan, liberal, Lord of food, of wondrous iustre, Whom strong and vigorous and swiftlymoving, subdued by love, the Deities gave to Surya.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I WILL declare, while juices flow, the manly deeds that ye have done: Your Fathers, enemies of Gods, were smitten down, and, Indra-Agni, ye survive.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thus, Indra-Agni verily your greatness merits loftiest praise, Sprung from one common Father, brothers, twins are ye; your Mother is in every place.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These who delight in flowing juice, like fellow horses at their food, Indra and Agni, Gods armed with the thunderbolt, we call this day to come with help.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra and Agni, Friends of Law, served with rich gifts, your speech is kind To him who praises you while these libations flow: that man, O Gods, ye ne'er consume.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What mortal understands, O Gods, Indra and Agni, this your way? One of you, yoking Steeds that move to every side, advances in your common car.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: First, Indra-Agni, hath this Maid come footless unto those with feet. Stretching her head and speaking loudly with her tongue, she hath gone downward thirty steps.
