verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: E'en now, O Indra-Agni, men hold in their arms and stretch their bows. Desert us not in this great fray, in battles for the sake of kine.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The foeman's sinful enmities, Indra and Agni, vex me sore. Drive those who hate me far away, and keep them distant from the Sun.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra and Agni, yours are all the treasures of the heavens and earth. Here give ye us the opulence that prospers every living man.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Indra-Agni, who accept the laud, and hear us for our praise, Come near us, drawn by all our songs, to drink of this our Soma juice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: HE slays the foe and wins the spoil who worships Indra and Agni, strong and mighty Heroes, Who rule as Sovrans over ample riches, victorious, showing forth their power in conquest.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So battle now, O Indra and thou, Agni, for cows and waters, sunlight, stolen Mornings. Team-borne, thou makest kine thine own, O Agni: thou, Indra, light, Dawns, regions, wondrous waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With Vrtra-slaying might, Indra and Agni, come, drawn by homage, O ye Vrtra-slayers. Indra and Agni, show yourselves among us with your supreme and unrestricted bounties.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I call the Twain whose deeds of old have all been famed in ancient days O Indra-Agni, harm us not.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Strong, the scatterers of the foe, Indra and Agni, we invoke; May they be kind to one like me.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They slay our Arya foes, these Lords of heroes, slay our Dasyu foes And drive our enemies away.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra and Agni, these our songs of praise have sounded forth to you: Ye who bring blessings! drink the juice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come, Indra-Agni, with those teams, desired of many, which ye have, O Heroes, for the worshipper.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With those to this libation poured, ye Heroes, Indra-Agni, come: Come ye to drink the Soma juice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Glorify him who compasses all forests with his glowing flame, And leaves them blackened with his tongue.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who gains Indra's bliss with fire enkindled finds an easy way Over the floods to happiness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Give us fleet coursers to convey Indra and Agni, and bestow Abundant strengthening food on us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra and Agni, I will call you hither and make you joyful with the gifts I offer. Ye Twain are givers both of food and riches: to win me strength and vigour I invoke you.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come unto us with riches, come with wealth in horses and in kine. Indra and Agni, we invoke you both, the Gods, as Friends for friendship, bringing bliss.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra and Agni, hear his call who worships. with libations poured. Come and enjoy the offerings, drink the sweetly-flavoured Soma juice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To Vadhryasva when. be worshipped her with gifts she gave fierce Divodasa, canceller of debts. Consumer of the churlish niggard, one and all, thine, O Sarasvati, are these effectual boons.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: She with her might, like one who digs for lotus-stems, hath burst with her strong waves the ridges of the hills. Let us invite with songs and holy hymns for help Sarasvati who slayeth the Paravatas.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou castest down, Sarasvati, those who scorned the Gods, the brood of every Brsaya skilled in magic arts. Thou hast discovered rivers for the tribes of men, and, rich in wealth! made poison flow away from them.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May the divine Sarasvati, rich in her wealth, protect us well, Furthering all our thoughts with might
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whoso, divine Sarasvati, invokes thee where the prize is set, Like Indra when he smites the foe.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Aid us, divine Sarasvad, thou who art strong in wealth and power Like Pusan, give us opulence.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yea, this divine Sarasvati, terrible with her golden path, Foe-slayer, claims our eulogy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whose limitless unbroken flood, swift-moving with a rapid rush, Comes onward with tempestuous roar.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: She hath spread us beyond all foes, beyond her Sisters, Holy One, As Surya spreadeth out the days.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yea, she most dear amid dear stream, Seven-sistered, graciously inclined, Sarasvati hath earned our praise.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Guard us from hate Sarasvati, she who hath filled the realms of earth, And that wide tract, the firmament!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Seven-sistered, sprung from threefold source, the Five Tribes' prosperer, she must be Invoked in every deed of might.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Marked out by majesty among the Mighty Ones, in glory swifter than the other rapid Streams, Created vast for victory like a chariot, Sarasvati must be extolled by every sage.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Guide us, Sarasvati, to glorious treasure: refuse us not thy milk, nor spurn us from thee. Gladly accept our friendship and obedience: let us not go from thee to distant countries.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I LAUD the Heroes Twain, this heaven's Controllers: singing with songs of praise I call the Asvins, Fain in a moment, when the morns are breaking, to part the earth's ends and the spacious regions.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Moving to sacrifice through realms of lustre they light the radiance of the car that bears them. Traversing many wide unmeasured spaces, over the wastes ye pass, and fields, and waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye to that bounteous path of yours, ye mighty, have ever borne away our thoughts with horses, Mind-swift and full of vigour, that the trouble of man who offers gifts might cease and slumber.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So ye, when ye have yoked your chariothorses, come to the hymn of the most recent singer. Our true and ancient Herald Priest shall bring you, the Youthful, bearing splendour, food, and vigour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With newest hymn I call those Wonder-Workers, ancient and brilliant, and exceeding mighty, Bringers of bliss to him who lauds and praises, bestowing varied bounties on the singer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So ye, with birds, out of the sea and waters bore Bhujyu, son of Tugra, through the regions. Speeding with winged steeds through dustless spaces, out of the bosom of the flood they bore him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Victors, car-borne, ye rent the rock asunder: Bulls, heard the calling of the eunuch's consort. Bounteous, ye filled the cow with milk for Sayu: thus, swift and zealous Ones, ye showed your favour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whate'er from olden time, Heaven, Earth! existeth great object of the wrath of Gods and mortals, Make that, Adityas, Vasus, sons of Rudra, an evil brand to one allied with demons.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May he who knows, as Varuna and Mitra, air's realm, appointing both the Kings in season, Against the secret fiend cast forth his weapon, against the lying words that strangers utter.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come to our home with friendly wheels, for offipring; come on your radiant chariot rich in heroes. Strike off, ye Twain, the heads of our assailants who with man's treacherous attack approach us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come hitherward to us with teams of horses, the highest and the midmost and the lowest. Bountiful Lords, throw open to the singer doors e'en of the firm-closed stall of cattle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WHERE hath the hymn with reverence, like an envoy, found both fair Gods to-day, invoked of many-
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come readily to this mine invocation, lauded with songs, that ye may drink the juices. Compass this house to keep it from the foeman, that none may force it, either near or distant.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Juice in wide room hath been prepared to feast you: for you the grass is strewn, most soft to tread on. With lifted hands your servant hath adored you. Yearningfor you the press-stones shed the liquid.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni uplifts him at your sacrifices: forth goes the oblation dropping oil and glowing. Up stands the grateful-minded priest, elected, appointed to invoke the two Nasatyas.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Lords of great wealth! for glory, Surya's Daughter mounted your car that brings a hundred succours. Famed for your magic arts were ye, magicians! amid the race of Gods, ye dancing Heroes!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye Twain, with these your glories fair to look on, brought, to win victory, rich gifts for Surya. After you flew your birds, marvels of beauty: dear to our hearts! the song, well lauded, reached you.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May your winged coursers, best to draw. Nasatyas! convey you to the object of your wishes. Swift as the thought, your car hath been sent onward to food of many a sort and dainty viands.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Lords of great wealth, manifold is your bounty: ye filled our cow with food that never faileth. Lovers of sweetness! yours are praise and singers, and poured libations which have sought your favour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Mine were two mares of Puraya, brown, swift-footed; a hundred with Sumidha, food with Peruk Sanda gave ten gold-decked and well-trained horses, tame and obedient and of lofty stature.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Nasatyas! Purupanthas offered hundreds, thousands of steeds to him who sang your praises, Gave, Heroes! to the singer Bharadvaja. Ye-Wonder-Workers, let the fiends be slaughtered.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May I with princes share your bliss in freedom.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THE radiant Dawns have risen up for glory, in their white splendour like the waves of waters. She maketh paths all easy, fair to travel, and, rich, hath shown herself benign and friendly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We see that thou art good: far shines thy lustre; thy beams, thy splendours have flown up to heaven. Decking thyself, thou makest bare thy bosom, shining in majesty, thou Goddess Morning.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Red are the kine and luminous that bear her the Blessed One who spreadeth through the distance. The foes she chaseth like a valiant archer, like a swift warrior she repelleth darkness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thy ways are easy on the hills: thou passest Invincible! Se1f-luminous! through waters. So lofty Goddess with thine ample pathway, Daughter of Heaven, bring wealth to give us comfort.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Dawn, bring me wealth: untroubled, with thine oxen thou bearest riches at thy will and pleasure; Thou who, a Goddess, Child of Heaven, hast shown thee lovely through bounty when we called thee early.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As the birds fly forth from their resting places, so men with store of food rise at thy dawning. Yea, to the liberal mortal who remaineth at home, O Goddess Dawn, much good thou bringest.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: SHEDDING her light on human habitations this Child of Heaven hath called us from our slumber; She who at night-time with her argent lustre hath shown herself e'en through the shades of darkness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: All this with red-rayed steeds have they divided: the Dawns on bright cars shine in wondrous fashion. They, bringing near the stately rite's commencement, drive far away the night's surrounding shadows.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Dawns, bringing hither, to the man who worships, glory and power and might and food and vigour, Opulent, with imperial sway like heroes, favour your servant and this day enrich him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now is there treasure for the man who serves you, now for the hero, Dawns! who brings oblation; Now for the singer when he sings the praise-song. Even to one like me ye brought aforetime.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Dawn who standest on the mountain ridges, Angirases now praise thy stalls of cattle. With prayer and holy hymn they burst them open: the heroes' calling on the Gods was fruitful.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Shine on us as of old, thou Child of Heaven,on him, rich Maid! who serves like Bharadvaja. Give to the singer wealth with noble heroes, and upon us bestow wide-spreading glory.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: E'EN to the wise let that be still a wonder to which the general name of Cow is given. The one hath swelled among mankind for milking: Prsni hath drained but once her fair bright udder.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They who like kindled flames of fire are glowing,. the Maruts, twice and thrice have waxen mighty. Golden and dustless were their cars, invested with their great strength and their heroic vigour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They who are Sons of the rain-pouring Rudra, whom the long-lasting One had power to foster: The Mighty Ones whose germ great Mother Prsni is known to have received for man's advantage.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They shrink not from the birth; in this same manner still resting there they purge away reproaches. When they have streamed forth, brilliant, at their pleasure, with their own splendour they bedew their bodies.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Even those who bear the brave bold name of Maruts, whom not the active quickly wins for milking. Even the liberal wards not off those fierce ones, those who are light and agile in their greatness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When, strong in strength and armed with potent weapons, they had united wellformed earth and heaven, Rodasl stood among these furious Heroes like splendour shining with her native brightness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: No team of goats shall draw your car, O Maruts, no horse no charioteer be he who drives it. Halting not, reinless, through the air it travels, speeding alone its paths through earth and heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: None may obstruct, none overtake, O Maruts, him whom ye succour in the strife of battle For sons and progeny, for kine and waters: he bursts the cow-stall on the day of trial.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bring a bright hymn to praise the band of Maruts, the Singers, rapid, strong in native vigour, Who conquer mighty strength with strength more mighty: earth shakes in terror at their wars, O Agni.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bright like the flashing flames of sacrifices, like tongues of fire impetuous in their onset, Chanting their psalm, singing aloud, like heroes, splendid from birth, invincible, the Maruts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: That swelling band I call with invocation, the brood of Rudra, armed with glittering lances. Pure hymns are meet for that celestial army: like floods and mountains have the Strong Ones battled.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: NOW Mitra-Varuna shall be exalted high by your songs, noblest of all existing; They who, as 'twere with reins are best Controllers, unequalled with their arms to check the people.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To you Two Gods is this my thought extended, turned to the sacred grass with loving homage. Give us, O Mitra-Varuna, a dwelling safe from attack, which ye shall guard, Boon-Givers!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come hither, Mitra-Varuna, invited with eulogies and loving adoration, Ye who with your might, as Work-Controllers, urge even men who quickly hear to labour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whom, of pure origin, like two strong horses, Aditi bore as babes in proper season, Whom, Mighty at your birth, the Mighty Goddess brought forth as terrors to the mortal foeman.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As all the Gods in their great joy and gladness gave you with one accord your high dominion, As ye surround both worlds, though wide and spacious your spies are ever true and never bewildered.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So, through the days maintaining princely power. ye prop the height as 'twere from loftiest heaven. The Star of all the Gods, established, filleth the heaven and earth with food of man who liveth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Take the strong drink, to quaff till ye are sated, when he and his attendants fill the chamber. The young Maids brook not that none seeks to win them, when, Quickeners of all! they scatter moisture.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So with your tongue come ever, when your envoy, faithful and very wise, attends our worship. Nourished by holy oil! he this your glory: annihilate the sacrificer's trouble.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When, Mitra-Varuna, they strive against you and break the friendly laws ye have established, They, neither Gods nor men in estimation, like Api's sons have godless sacrifices.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When singers in their song uplift their voices, some chant the Nivid texts with steady purpose. Then may we sing you lauds that shall be fruitful: do ye not rival all the Gods in greatness?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Mitra-Varuna, may your large bounty come to us hither, near to this our dwelling, When the kine haste to us, and when they harness the fleet-foot mettled stallion for the battle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: HIS honouring rite whose grass is trimmed is offered swiftly to you, in Manu's wise, accordant, The rite which Indra-Varuna shall carry this day to high success and glorious issue.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For at Gods' worship they are best through vigour; they have become the strongest of the Heroes; With mighty strength, most liberal of the Princes, Chiefs of the host, by Law made Vrtra's slayers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Praise those Twain Gods for powers that merit worship, Indra and Varuna, for bliss, the joyous. One with his might and thunderbolt slays Vrtra; the other as a Sage stands near in troubles.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Though dames and men have waxen strong and mighty, and all the Gods selfpraised among the Heroes, Ye, Indra-Varuna, have in might surpassed them, and thus were ye spread wide, O Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Righteous is he, and liberal and helpful who, Indra-Varuna, brings you gifts with gladness. That bounteous man through food shall conquer faemen, and win him opulence and wealthy people.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May wealth which ye bestow in food and treasure on him who brings you gifts and sacrifices, Wealth, Gods! which breaks the curse of those who vex us, be, Indra-Varuna, e'en our own possession.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So also, Indra-Varuna, may our princes have riches swift to save, with Gods to guard them- They whose great might gives victory in battles, and their triumphant glory spreads with swiftness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra. and Varuna, Gods whom we are lauding, mingle ye wealth with our heroic glory. May we, who praise the strength of what is mighty, pass dangers, as with boats we cross the waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now will I sing a dear and far-extending hymn to Varuna the God, sublime, imperial Lord, Who, mighty Governor, Eternal, as with flame, illumines both wide worlds with majesty and power.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: True to Law, Indra-Varuna, drinkers of the juice, drink this pressed Soma which shall give you rapturous joy. Your chariot cometh to the banquet of the Gods, to sacrifice, as it were home, that ye may drink.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra and Varuna, drink your fill, ye Heroes, of this invigorating sweetest Soma. This juice is shed by us that ye may quaff it: on this trimmed grass be seated, and rejoice you
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: INDRA and Visnu, at my task's completion I urge you on with food and sacred service. Accept the sacrifice and grant us riches, leading us on by unobstructed pathways.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye who inspire all hymns, Indra and Visnu, ye vessels who contain the Soma juices, May hymns of praise that now are sung address you, the lauds that are recited by the singers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Lords of joy-giving draughts, Indra and Visnu, come, giving gifts of treasure, to the Soma. With brilliant rays of hymns let chanted praises, repeated with the lauds, adorn and deck you.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May your foe-conquering horses bring you hither, Indra and Visnu, sharers of the banquet. Of all our hymns accept the invocations list to my prayers and hear the songs I sing you.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This your deed, Indra-Visnu, must be lauded: widely ye strode in the wild joy of Soma. Ye made the firmament of larger compass, and made the regions broad for our existence.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Strengthened with sacred offerings, IndraVisnu, first eaters, served with worship ana oblation, Fed with the holy oil, vouchsafe us riches ye are the lake, the vat that holds the Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Drink of this meath, O Indra, thou, and Visnu; drink ye your fill of Soma, Wonder-Workers. The sweet exhilarating juice hath reached you. Hear ye my prayers, give ear unto my calling.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye Twain have conquered, ne'er have you been conquered: never hath either of the Twain been vanquished. Ye, Indra-Visnu, when ye fought the battle, produced this infinite with three divisions.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: FILLED full of fatness, compassing all things that be, wide, spacious, dropping meath, beautiful in their form, The Heaven and the Earth by Varuna's decree, unwasting, rich in germs, stand parted each from each.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Everlasting Pair, with full streams, rich in milk, in their pure rule pour fatness for the pious man. Ye who are Regents of this world, O Earth and Heaven, pour into us the genial flow that prospers meit.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whoso, for righteous life, pours offerings to you, O Heaven and Earth, ye Hemispheres, that man succeeds. He in his seed is born again and spreads by Law: from you flow things diverse in form, but ruled alike.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Enclosed in fatness, Heaven and Earth are bright therewith: they mingle with the fatness which they still increase. Wide, broad, set foremost at election of the priest, to them the singers pray for bliss to further them.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Heaven and Earth pour down the balmy rain for us, balm-dropping, yielding balm, with balm upon your path, Bestowing by your Godhead sacrifice and wealth, great fame and strength for us and good heroic might.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Heaven and Earth make food swell plenteously for us, all-knowing Father, jother, wondrous in their works. Pouring out bounties, may, in union, both the Worlds, all beneficial, send us gain, and power, and wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: FULL of effectual wisdom Savitar the God hath stretched out golden arms that he may bring forth life. Young and most skilful, while he holds the region up, the Warrior sprinkles fatness over both his hands.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May we enjoy the noblest vivifying force of Savitar the God, that he may give us wealth: For thou art mighty to produce and lull to rest the world of life that moves on two feet and on four.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Protect our habitation, Savitar, this day, with guardian aids around, auspicious, firm and true. God of the golden tongue, keep us for newest bliss: let not the evil-wisher have us in his power.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This Savitar the God, the golden-handed, Friend of the home, hath risen to meet the twilight. With cheeks of brass, with pleasant tongue, the Holy, he sends the worshipper rich gifts in plenty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like a Director, Savitar hath extended his golden arms, exceeding fair to look on. He hath gone up the heights of earth and heaven, and made each monster fall and cease from troubling.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Fair wealth, O Savitar, to-day, to-morrow, fair wealth produce for us each day that passes. May we through this our song be happy gainers, God, of a fair and spacious habitation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: GREAT is this might of yours, Indra and Soma: the first high exploits were your own achievements. Ye found the Sun ye found the light of heaven: ye killed all darkness and the Gods' blasphemers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye, Indra-Soma, gave her light to Morning, and led the Sun on high with all his splendour. Ye stayed the heaven with a supporting pillar, and spread abroad apart, the Earth, the Mother.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye slew the flood -obstructing serpent Vrtra, Indra and Soma: Heaven approved your exploit. Ye urged to speed the currents of the rivers, and many seas have ye filled full with waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye in the unripe udders of the milch-kine have set the ripe milk, Indra, thou, and Soma. Ye have held fast the unimpeded whiteness within these many-coloured moving creatures.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Verily ye bestow, Indra and Soma, wealth, famed, victorious, passing to our children. Ye have invested men, ye Mighty Beings, with manly strength that conquers in the battle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: SERVED with oblations, first-born, mountain-render, Angiras' son, Brhaspati, the Holy, With twice-firm path, dwelling in light, our Father, roars loudly, as a bull, to Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Brhaspati, who made for such a people wide room and verge when Gods were invocated, Slaying his enemies, breaks down their castles, quelling his foes and conquering those who hate him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Brhaspati in war hath won rich treasures, hath won, this God, the great stalls filled with cattle. Striving to win waters and light, resistless, Brhaspati with lightning smites the foeman.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: HOLD fast your Godlike sway, O Soma-Rudra: let these our sacrifices quickly reach you. Placing in every house your seven great treasures, bring blessing to our quadrupeds and bipeds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Soma and Rudra, chase to every quarter the sickness that hath visited our dwelling. Drive Nirrti away into the distance, and give us excellent and happy glories.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Provide, O Soma-Rudra, for our bodies all needful medicines to heal and cure us. Set free and draw away the sin committed which we have still inherent in our persons.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Armed with keen shafts and weapons, kind and loving, be gracious unto us, Soma and Rudra. Release us from the noose of Varuna; keep us from sorrow, in your tender loving-kindness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THE warrior's look is like a thunderous rain-cloud's, when, armed with mail, he seeks the lap of battle. Be thou victorious with unwounded body: so let the thickness of thy mail protect thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With Bow let us win kine, with Bow the battle, with Bow be victors in our hot encounters. The Bow brings grief and sorrow to the foeman: armed with the Bow may we subdue all regions.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Close to his car, as fain to speak, She presses, holding her well-loved Friend in her embraces. Strained on the Bow, She whispers like a woman-this Bowstring that preserves us in the combat.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These, meeting like a woman and her lover, bear, mother-like, their child upon their bosom. May the two Bow-ends, starting swift asunder, scatter, in unison, the foes who hate us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With many a son, father of many daughters, He clangs and clashes as he goes to battle. Slung on the back, pouring his brood, the Quiver vanquishes all opposing bands and armies.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Upstanding in the Car the skilful Charioteer guides his strong Horses on whithersoe'er he will. See and admire the strength of those controlling Reins which from behind declare the will of him who drives.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Horses whose hoofs rain dust are neighing loudly, yoked to the Chariots, showing forth their vigour, With their forefeet descending on the foemen, they, never flinching, trample and destroy them.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Car-bearer is the name of his oblation, whereon are laid his Weapons and his Armour. So let us here, each day that passes, honour the helpful Car with hearts exceeding joyful.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In sweet association lived the fathers who gave us life, profound and strong in trouble, Unwearied, armed with shafts and wondrous weapons, free, real heroes, conquerors of armies.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Brahmans, and the Fathers meet for Soma-draughts, and, graciously inclined, unequalled Heaven and Earth. Guard us from evil, Pusan, guard us strengtheners of Law: let not the evil-wisher master us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Her tooth a deer, dressed in an eagle's feathers, bound with cow-hide, launched forth, She flieth onward. There where the heroes speed hither and thither, there may the Arrows shelter and protect us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Avoid us thou whose flight is straight, and let our bodies be as stone. May Soma kindly speak to us, and Aditi protect us well.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He lays his blows upon their backs, he deals his blows upon their thighs. Thou, Whip, who urgest horses, drive sagacious horses in the fray.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: It compasses the arm with serpent windings, fending away the friction of the bowstring: So may the Brace, well-skilled in all its duties, guard manfully the man from every quarter.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now to the Shaft with venom smeared, tipped with deer-horn, with iron mouth, Celestial, of Parjanya's seed, be this great adoration paid.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Loosed from the Bowstring fly away, thou Arrow, sharpened by our prayer. Go to the foemen, strike them home, and let not one be left alive.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: There where the flights of Arrows fall like boys whose locks are yet unshorn. Even there may Brahmanaspati, and Aditi protect us well, protect us well through all our days.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thy vital parts I cover with thine Armour: with immortality King Soma clothe thee. Varuna give thee what is more than ample, and in thy triumph may the Gods be joyful.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whoso would kill us, whether he be a strange foe or one of us,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THE men from fire-sticks, with their hands' swift movement, have, in deep thought, engendered glorious Agni, Far-seen, with pointed flame, Lord of the homestead.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Vasus set that Agni in the dwelling, fair to behold, for help from every quarter: Who, in the home for ever, must be honoured.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Shine thou before us, Agni, well-enkindled, with flame, Most Youthful God, that never fadeth. To thee come all our sacrificial viands.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Among all fires these fires have shone most brightly, splendid with light, begirt by noble heroes, Where men of lofty birth sit down together.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Victorious Agni, grant us wealth with wisdom, wealth with brave sons, famous and independent, Which not a foe who deals in magic conquers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To whom, the Strong, at morn and eve comes, maid-like, the ladle dropping oil, with its oblation. Wealth-seeking comes to him his own devotion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Burn up all malice with those flames, O Agni, wherewith of old thou burntest up Jarutha, And drive away in silence pain and sickness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With him who lighteth up thy splendour, Agni, excellent, pure, refulgent, Purifier, Be present, and with us through these our praises.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, the patriarchal men, the mortals who have in many places spread thy lustre,- Be gracious to us here for their sake also.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let these men, heroes in the fight with foemen, prevail against all godless arts of magic,- These who approve the noble song I sing thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let us not sit in want of men, O Agni, without descendants, hero less, about thee: But, O House-Friend, in houses full of children.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: By sacrifice which the Steeds' Lord ever visits, there make our dwelling rich in seed and offspring, Increasing still with lineal successors.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Guard us, O Agni, from the hated demon, guard us from malice of the churlish sinner: Allied with thee may I subdue assailants.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May this same fire of mine surpass all others, this fire where offspring, vigorous and firm-handed, Wins, on a thousand paths, what ne'er shall perish.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This is that Agni, saviour from the foeman, who guards the kindler of the flame from sorrow: Heroes of noble lineage serve and tend him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This is that Agni, served in many places, whom the rich lord who brings oblation kindles, And round him goes the priest at sacrifices.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, may we with riches in possession bring thee continual offerings in abundance, Using both means to draw thee to our worship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, bear thou, Eternal, these most welcome oblations to the Deities' assembly: Let them enjoy our very fragrant presents.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Give us not up, Agni, to want of heroes, to wretched clothes, to need, to destitution. Yield us not, Holy One, to fiend or hunger; injure us not at home or in the forest.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Give strength and power to these my prayers, O Agni; O God, pour blessings on our chiefs and nobles. Grant that both we and they may share thy bounty. Ye Gods, protect us evermore with blessings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou Agni, swift to hear, art fair of aspect: beam forth, O Son of Strength, in full effulgence. Let me not want, with thee, a son for ever: let not a manly hero ever fail us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Condemn us not to indigence, O Agni, beside these flaming fires which Gods have kindled; Nor, even after fault, let thy displeasure, thine as a God, O Son of Strength, o'ertake us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Agni, fair of face, the wealthy mortal who to the Immortal offers his oblation. Hath him who wins him treasure by his Godhead, to whom the prince, in need, goes supplicating.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Knowing our chief felicity, O Agni, bring hither ample riches to our nobles, Wherewith we may enjoy ourselves, O Victor, with undiminished life and hero children.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Give strength and power to these my prayers, O Agni; O God, pour blessings on bur chiefs and nobles. Grant that both we and they may share thy bounty. Ye Gods, protect us evermore with blessings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: GLADLY accept, this day, our fuel, Agni: send up thy sacred smoke and shine sublimely. Touch the celestial summits with thy columns, and overspread thee with the rays of Surya.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With sacrifice to these we men will honour the majesty of holy Narasamsa- To these the pure, most wise, the thought. inspirers, Gods who enjoy both sorts of our oblations.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We will extol at sacrifice for ever, as men may do, Agni whom Manu kindled, Your very skilful Asura, meet for worship, envoy between both worlds, the truthful speaker.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bearing the sacred grass, the men who serve him strew it with reverence, on their knees, by Agni. Calling him to the spotted grass, oil-sprinkled, adorn him, ye Adhvaryus, with oblation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With holy thoughts the pious have thrown open Doors fain for chariots in the Gods' assembly. Like two full mother cows who lick their youngling, like maidens for the gathering, they adorn them.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And let the two exalted Heavenly Ladies, Morning and Night, like a cow good at milking, Come, much-invoked, and on our grass be seated ' wealthy, deserving worship, for our welfare.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: You, Bards and Singers at men's sacrifices, both filled with wisdom, I incline to worship. Send up our offerings when we call upon you, and so among the Gods obtain us treasures.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Bharati with all her Sisters, Ila accordant with the Gods, with mortals Agni, Sarasvati with all her kindred Rivers, come to this grass, Three Goddesses, and seat them.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Well pleased with us do thou, O God, O Tvastar, give ready issue to our procreant vigour, Whence springs the hero, powerful, skilled in action, lover of Gods, adjuster of the press-stones.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Send to the Gods the oblation, Lord of Forests, and let the Immolator, Agni, dress it. He as the truer Priest shall offer worship, for the God's generations well he knoweth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come thou to us, O Agni, duly kindled, together with the potent Gods and Indra. On this our grass sit Aditi, happy Mother, and let our Hail! delight the Gods Immortal.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: ASSOCIATE with fires, make your God Agni envoy at sacrifice, best skilled in worship, Established firm among mankind, the Holy, flame-crowned and fed with oil, the Purifier.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like a steed neighing eager for the pasture, when he hath stepped forth from the great enclosure: Then the wind following blows upon his splendour, and, straight, the path is black which thou hast travelled.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: From thee a Bull but newly born, O Agni, the kindled everlasting flames rise upward. Aloft to heaven thy ruddy smoke ascendeth: Agni, thou speedest to the Gods as envoy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou whose fresh lustre o'er the earth advanceth when greedily with thy jaws thy food thou eatest. Like a host hurried onward comes thy lasso: fierce, with thy tongue thou piercest, as 'twere barley.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The men have decked him both at eve and morning, Most Youthful Agni, as they tend a courser. They kindle him, a guest within his dwelling: bright shines the splendour of the worshipped Hero.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O fair of face, beautiful is thine aspect when, very near at hand, like gold thou gleamest, Like Heaven's thundering roar thy might approaches, and like the wondrous Sun thy light thou showest.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: That we may worship, with your Hail to Agni! with sacrificial cakes and fat oblations, Guard us, O Agni, with those boundless glories as with a hundred fortresses of iron.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thine are resistless songs for him who offers, and hero-giving hymns wherewith thou savest; With these, O Son of Strength, O Jatavedas, guard us, preserve these princes and the singers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When forth he cometh, like an axe new-sharpened, pure in his form, resplendent in his body, Sprung, sought with eager longing, from his Parents, for the Gods' worship, Sage and Purifier:
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Shine this felicity on us, O Agni: may we attain to perfect understanding. All happiness be theirs who sing and praise thee. Ye Gods, preserve us evermore with blessings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: BRING forth your gifts to his refulgent splendour, your hymn as purest offering to Agni, To him who goes as messenger with knowledge between all songs of men and Gods in heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wise must this Agni be, though young and tender, since he was born, Most Youthful, of his Mother; He who with bright teeth seizeth fast the forests, and eats his food, though plenteous, in a moment.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Before his presence must we all assemble, this God's whom men have seized in his white splendour. This Agni who hath brooked that men should seize him hath shone for man with glow insufferable.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Far-seeing hath this Agni been established, deathless mid mortals, wise among the foolish. Here, O victorious God, forbear to harm us: may we forever share thy gracious favour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who hath occupied his God-made dwelling, Agni, in wisdom hath surpassed Immortals. A Babe unborn, the plants and trees support him, and the earth beareth him the All-sustainer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni is Lord of Amrta. in abundance, Lord of the gift of wealth and hero valour, Victorious God, let us not sit about thee like men devoid of strength, beauty, and worship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The foeman's treasure may be won with labour: may we be masters of our own possessions. Agni, no son is he who springs from others: lengthen not out the pathways of the foolish.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Unwelcome for adoption is the stranger, one to be thought of as another's offspring, Though grown familiar by continual presence. May our strong hero come, freshly triumphant.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Guard us from him who would assail us, Agni; preserve us O thou Victor, from dishonour. Here let the place of darkening come upon thee: may wealth be ours, desirable, in thousands.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Shine this felicity on us, O Agni: may we attain to perfect understanding. All happiness be theirs who sing and praise thee. Ye Gods, preserve us evermore with blessings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: BRING forth your song of praise to mighty Agni, the speedy messenger of earth and heaven, Vaisvanara, who, with those who wake, hath waxen great in the lap of all the Gods Immortal.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sought in the heavens, on earth is Agni stablished, leader of rivers, Bull of standing waters. Vaisvanara when he hath grown in glory, shines on the tribes of men with light and treasure.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For fear of thee forth fled the dark-hued races, scattered abroad, deserting their possessions, When, glowing, O Vaisvanara, for Puru, thou Agni didst light up and rend their castles.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni Vaisvanara, both Earth and Heaven submit them to thy threefold jurisdiction. Refulgent in thine undecaying lustre thou hast invested both the worlds with splendour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, the tawny horses, loudly neighing our resonant hymns that drop with oil, attend thee; Lord of the tribes, our Charioteer of riches, Ensign of days, Vaisvanara of mornings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In thee, O bright as Mitra, Vasus seated the might of Aduras, for they loved thy spirit. Thou drivest Dasyus from their home, O Agni, and broughtest forth broad light to light the Arya.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Born in the loftiest heaven thou in a moment reachest, like wind, the place where Gods inhabit. Thou, favouring thine offspring, roaredst loudly when giving life to creatures, Jatavedas.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Send us that strength, Vaisvanara, send it, Agni, that strength, O Jatavedas, full of splendour, Wherewith, all-bounteous God, thou pourest riches, as fame wide-spreading, on the man who offers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, bestow upon our chiefs and nobles that famous power, that wealth which feedeth many. Accordant with the Vasus and the Rudras, Agni, Vaisvanara, give us sure protection.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: PRAISE of the Asura, high imperial Ruler, the Manly One in whom the folk shall triumph- I laud his deeds who is as strong as Indra, and lauding celebrate the Fort-destroyer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sage, Sing, Food, Light,-they bring him from the mountain, the blessed Sovran of the earth and heaven. I decorate with songs the mighty actions which Agni, Fort-destroyer, did aforetime.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The foolish, faithless, rudely-speaking niggards, without belief or sacrifice or worship,- Far far away hath Agni chased those Dasyus, and, in the cast, hath turned the godless westward.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him who brought eastward, manliest with his prowess, the Maids rejoicing in the western darkness, That Agni I extol, the Lord of riches, unyielding tamer of assailing foemen.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him who brake down the walls with deadly weapons, and gave the Mornings to a noble Husband, Young Agni, who with conquering strength subduing the tribes of Nahus made them bring their tribute.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In whose protection all men rest by nature, desiring to enjoy his gracious favour- Agni Vaisvanara in his Parents, bosom hath found the choicest seat in earth and heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Vaisvanara the God, at the sun's setting, hath taken to himself deep-hidden treasures: Agni hath taken them from earth and heaven, from the sea under and the sea above us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I SEND forth even your God, victorious Agni, like a strong courser, with mine adoration. Herald of sacrifice be he who knoweth he hath reached Gods, himself, with measured motion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: By paths that are thine own come hither, Agni, joyous, delighting in the Gods' alliance, Making the heights of earth roar with thy fury, burning with eager teeth the woods and forests.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The grass is strewn; the sacrifice advances adored as Priest, Agni is made propitious, Invoking both All-boon-bestowing Mothers of whom, Most Youthful! thou wast born to help us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Forthwith the men, the best of these for wisdom, have made him leader in the solemn worship. As Lord in homes of men is Agni stablished, the Holy One, the joyous, sweetly speaking.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He hath come, chosen bearer, and is seated in man's home, Brahman, Agni, the Supporter, He whom both Heaven and Earth exalt and strengthen whom, Giver of all boons, the Hotar worships.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These have passed all in glory, who, the manly, have wrought with skill the hymn of adoration; Who, listening, have advanced the people's welfare, and set their thoughts on this my holy statute.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We, the Vasisthas, now implore thee, Agni, O Son of Strength, the Lord of wealth and treasure. Thou hast brought food to singers and to nobles. Ye Gods, preserve us evermore with blessings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THE King whose face is decked with oil is kindled with homage offered by his faithful servant. The men, the priests adore him with oblations. Agni hath shone forth when the dawn is breaking.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yea, he hath been acknowledged as most mighty, the joyous Priest of men, the youthful Agni. He, spreading o'er the earth, made light around him, and grew among the plants with blackened fellies..
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: How dost thou decorate our hymn, O Agni? What power dost thou exert when thou art lauded? When, Bounteous God, may we be lords of riches, winners of precious wealth which none may conquer?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Far famed is this the Bharata's own Agni he shineth like the Sun with lofty splendour. He who hath vanquished Puru in the battle, the heavenly guest hath glowed in full refulgence.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Full many oblations are in thee collected: with all thine aspects thou hast waxen gracious. Thou art already famed as praised and lauded, yet still, O nobly born, increase thy body.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Be this my song, that winneth countless treasure, engendered with redoubled force for Agni, That, splendid, chasing sickness, slaying demons, it may delight our friend and bless the singers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We, the Vasisthas, now implore thee, Agni, O Son of Strength, the Lord of wealth and riches. Thou hast brought food to singers and to nobles. Ye Gods, preserve us evermore with blessings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: ROUSED from their bosom is the Dawns' beloved, the joyous Priest, most sapient, Purifier. He gives a signal both to Gods and mortals, to Gods oblations, riches to the pious.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Most wise is he who, forcing doors of Panis, brought the bright Sun to us who feedeth many. The cheerful Priest, men's Friend and home-companion, through still night's darkness he is made apparent.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wise, ne.'er deceived, uncircumscribed, refulgent, our gracious guest, a Friend with good attendants, Shines forth with wondrous light before the Mornings; the young plants hath he entered, Child of Waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Seeking our gatherings, he, your Jatavedas, hath shone adorable through human ages, Who gleams refulgent with his lovely lustre: the kine have waked to meet him when enkindled.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Go on thy message to the Gods, and fail not, O Agni, with their band who pray and worship. Bring all the Gods that they may give us riches, Sarasvati, the Maruts, Asvins, Waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Vasistha, when enkindling thee, O Agni, hath slain jarutha. Give us wealth in plenty. Sing praise in choral song, O Jatavedas. Ye Gods, preserve us evermore with blessings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: HE hath sent forth, bright, radiant, and refulgent, like the Dawn's Lover, his far-spreading lustre. Pure in his splendour shines the golden Hero: our longing thoughts hath he aroused and wakened.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He, like the Sun, hath shone while Morn is breaking, and priests who weave the sacrifice sing praises, Agni, the God, who knows their generations and visits Gods, most bounteous, rapid envoy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Our songs and holy hymns go forth to Agni, seeking the God and asking him for riches, Him fair to see, of goodly aspect, mighty, men's messenger who carries their oblations.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Joined with the Vasus, Agni, bring thou Indra bring hither mighty Rudra with the Rudras, Aditi good to all men with Adityas, Brhaspati All-bounteous, with the Singers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Men eagerly implore at sacrifices Agni, Most Youthful God, the joyous Herald. For he is Lord and Ruler over riches, and for Gods' worship an unwearied envoy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary
